Pending loads and completed results are cached until [`Self::remove_asset`].
This method does not subscribe a view to completion notifications.
doc_texts.fn:App::find_display: Returns the display with the given [`DisplayId`], or `None` if it is not connected.
doc_texts.fn:App::focus_handle:
Creates a new [`FocusHandle`] for tracking keyboard focus.

Attach the handle to an element with `track_focus`, and move focus to it with
[`Window::focus`].
doc_texts.fn:App::foreground_executor:
Returns the [`ForegroundExecutor`], which runs futures on the main thread.

# Panics

Panics if called after the quit handlers have started running (from
[`App::on_app_quit`]).
doc_texts.fn:App::foreground_journal:
Returns the foreground work journal for this app's foreground thread.
Apps constructed on the same thread share the stream.
doc_texts.fn:App::get_menus: Returns the menu bar most recently set with [`App::set_menus`], or `None` if none was set.
doc_texts.fn:App::get_name:
Returns the debugging name of this app, if one was set.

Only available in tests, with the `test-support` feature, or in debug builds.
doc_texts.fn:App::global:
Returns the global of type `G`.

# Panics

Panics if no global of type `G` has been set. Use [`App::try_global`] when the
global may be missing.
doc_texts.fn:App::global_mut:
Returns the global of type `G` for mutation, and notifies global observers.

Observers registered with [`App::observe_global`] run when the current update
finishes. The notification happens on every call, even if you don't change the
value.

# Panics

Panics if no global of type `G` has been set. Use [`App::default_global`] to
create one on first use.
doc_texts.fn:App::graphical_environment:
The environment of the display server the platform is connected to, or `None` while
headless. Its activation token is always unset, since the connection has used it.

Programs an app launches inherit this process's environment, which may name another
graphical session, or none if the app started headless. Pass them this one with
[`GraphicalEnvironment::apply_to`](crate::GraphicalEnvironment::apply_to).

On macOS, the environment carries nothing, and this is `None` while the activation
policy is `Accessory`. Always `None` on platforms that can't switch windowing modes.
doc_texts.fn:App::has_active_drag: Returns whether a drag is in progress.
doc_texts.fn:App::has_asset:
Returns whether `source` is cached for asset type `A`, either loading or loaded.

This doesn't start a load. Only available in tests and with the `test-support` feature.
doc_texts.fn:App::has_global: Returns whether a global of type `G` has been set.
doc_texts.fn:App::hide: Hides the app, the same as choosing Hide from the app menu.
doc_texts.fn:App::hide_other_apps: Hides all other applications.
doc_texts.fn:App::http_client: Returns the app's HTTP client. See [`Application::with_http_client`].
doc_texts.fn:App::init_colors: Sets the default [`Colors`] global, which `cx.default_colors()` returns.
doc_texts.fn:App::intercept_keystrokes:
Calls `f` for every key-down that reaches any window, before it is dispatched.

Unlike [`App::observe_keystrokes`], which runs after handling, the interceptor runs
first. Calling [`App::stop_propagation`] inside it stops the keystroke from reaching
action dispatch. Keep the returned [`Subscription`] alive.
doc_texts.fn:App::is_action_available:
Returns whether `action` would be handled if it were dispatched now.

Checks the active window's focus path and its bindings, then the global listeners
from [`App::on_action`]. Use it to enable or disable menu items.
doc_texts.fn:App::is_cursor_visible:
Returns whether the cursor is currently visible according to the
platform. This will report `false` after a keyboard input has hidden
the cursor and the user has not yet moved the mouse to restore it.

See [`App::set_cursor_hide_mode`].
doc_texts.fn:App::is_screen_capture_supported: Returns whether [`App::screen_capture_sources`] can return sources on this platform.
doc_texts.fn:App::is_test:
Whether this app runs on the deterministic test scheduler. See
[`BackgroundExecutor::is_test`].
doc_texts.fn:App::key_bindings:
Returns the app's keymap, shared with the app.

Borrow it to inspect bindings. Don't hold the borrow across a call that changes
bindings, such as [`App::bind_keys`], because the borrow panics.
doc_texts.fn:App::keyboard_layout:
Returns the keyboard layout that is active now.

Use it to translate between keystrokes and the characters they produce. The
value is updated when the layout changes, which [`App::on_keyboard_layout_change`]
reports.
doc_texts.fn:App::keyboard_mapper: Returns the keyboard mapper for the active layout.
doc_texts.fn:App::observe_displays:
Invokes a handler when a display is connected, disconnected, or its
properties change.
doc_texts.fn:App::observe_keystrokes:
Calls `f` for every keystroke that reaches any window of the app.

The callback runs after action and event handling has finished, and the event
names the action that handled the keystroke, if any. Keystrokes consumed by an
interceptor or a raw keyboard event handler are not observed, and a modifier
pressed on its own is observed when it is released. Use
[`App::intercept_keystrokes`] to see keystrokes before they are dispatched. Keep
the returned [`Subscription`] alive.
doc_texts.fn:App::observe_new:
Calls `on_new` each time an entity of type `T` is created.

The callback receives the new state, the [`Window`] if the entity was created with
one, and a [`Context`] for it. Use it to set up behavior for every instance of a
type, such as registering an observer. Keep the returned [`Subscription`] alive
for the callback to keep running.
doc_texts.fn:App::observe_release:
Calls `on_release` when the entity behind `handle` is released.

The callback runs after the entity's last strong handle is dropped, and before the
entity's state is dropped. It receives the state as `&mut T`. Keep the returned
[`Subscription`] alive for the callback to run.
doc_texts.fn:App::observe_release_in:
Calls `on_release` when the entity behind `handle` is released, inside `window`.

Like [`App::observe_release`], but the callback also receives `window`. The
callback doesn't run if `window` has already closed when the entity is released.
doc_texts.fn:App::on_app_lifecycle:
Observes mobile application lifecycle changes. Desktop platforms do not
emit these events. On iOS these currently describe the single connected
scene, not individual windows.

Save important changes incrementally: neither disconnection nor quit is
guaranteed before the system terminates a backgrounded application.
Dropping the returned subscription removes the observer.
doc_texts.fn:App::on_app_quit:
Calls `on_quit` when the app is about to quit, and waits for the returned future.

Use it to flush data to disk or close connections. The quit can't be cancelled
at this point. Native apps wait up to [`SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT`] for the futures, so
keep the work short. Keep the returned [`Subscription`] alive for the callback to
run.
doc_texts.fn:App::on_app_restart:
Calls `on_restart` when the app is about to restart, before any [`App::on_app_quit`] handlers run.

Keep the returned [`Subscription`] alive for the callback to run.
doc_texts.fn:App::on_keyboard_layout_change:
Calls `callback` each time the user switches the keyboard layout.

The subscription stays active while you hold it. Drop it to stop receiving
calls. By the time the callback runs, [`App::keyboard_layout`] already returns
the new layout.
doc_texts.fn:App::on_memory_warning:
Observes mobile memory-pressure warnings so applications can release
expendable caches. Dropping the subscription removes the observer.
doc_texts.fn:App::on_system_notification_response:
Registers the handler invoked when the user activates a system
notification, either by clicking its body or one of its action
buttons. Subsequent registrations replace the handler.
doc_texts.fn:App::on_system_sleep:
Invokes a handler when the system is about to sleep.

The platform gives the process only a short time before suspending, so
handlers should record state or cancel work rather than start it.
doc_texts.fn:App::on_system_wake:
Calls `callback` when the system wakes from sleep.

Use it to reconnect to network services or refresh data that went stale
while the machine slept. The subscription stays active while you hold it.
doc_texts.fn:App::on_thermal_state_change:
Calls `callback` when the system's thermal state changes.

The subscription stays active while you hold it.
doc_texts.fn:App::on_window_closed:
Calls `on_closed` with the [`WindowId`] each time a window closes.

The window is no longer accessible when the callback runs. Keep the returned
[`Subscription`] alive for the callback to run.
doc_texts.fn:App::open_url:
Opens `url` in the platform's default browser or handler.

The call returns immediately. In tests, `TestApp::opened_url` reports the last
URL passed here.
doc_texts.fn:App::open_with_system: Opens `path` with the system's default application for its file type.
doc_texts.fn:App::path_for_auxiliary_executable:
Returns the path to a helper executable named `name` that ships with the app.

See [`Application::path_for_auxiliary_executable`].
doc_texts.fn:App::perform_dock_menu_action:
Runs the dock menu item at index `action`, as set with [`App::set_dock_menu`].

Only Windows uses this path.
doc_texts.fn:App::play_haptic_feedback:
Plays a haptic feedback pulse of the given style.

Call it from the main thread, for example in response to a click or a drop that
the user should feel. It does nothing on platforms without haptics. Check
[`App::supports_haptic_feedback`] to decide whether to show a haptic option.
Styles correspond to
[`NSHapticFeedbackPattern`](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appkit/nshapticfeedbackmanager/feedbackpattern)
values on macOS.
doc_texts.fn:App::prevent_idle_sleep: Prevents idle sleep while the returned guard is held.
doc_texts.fn:App::primary_display: Returns the primary display, or `None` if the platform reports none.
doc_texts.fn:App::prompt_for_new_path:
Shows the platform's save dialog and returns the path the user chose.

`directory` is the folder the dialog opens in, and `suggested_name` pre-fills the
file name. The result arrives on the returned channel. Cancelling yields
`Ok(None)`. On Linux the channel yields an error if the dialog can't be opened.
doc_texts.fn:App::prompt_for_paths:
Shows the platform's file or folder picker and returns the user's choice.

The result arrives on the returned channel once the user picks paths or cancels.
Cancelling yields `Ok(None)`. The picker is shown without blocking the caller.
On Linux the channel yields an error if the picker can't be opened.
doc_texts.fn:App::propagate:
Lets the current event or action continue to later handlers.

Use it in a handler to pass the event on to the next handler, for example an
action listener on a parent element or a global handler from [`App::on_action`].
It cancels an earlier [`App::stop_propagation`] in the same dispatch.
doc_texts.fn:App::quit:
Asks the platform to quit the app, the same as choosing Quit from the app menu.

The quit happens later, not inside this call. The platform then calls
[`App::shutdown`], which runs the [`Context::on_app_quit`] handlers and closes
the windows. Use this to quit from your own code. [`QuitMode`] controls quits
that happen when the last window closes.
doc_texts.fn:App::read_credentials:
Reads the username and password stored for `url`.

The task resolves to `None` when nothing is stored for `url`. Use the same `url`
that you passed to [`App::write_credentials`].
doc_texts.fn:App::read_from_clipboard:
Reads the current contents of the system clipboard.

Returns `None` if the clipboard is empty or holds nothing GPUI can read. On
the web, use [`App::read_from_clipboard_async`] instead, because this method
cannot wait for permission.
doc_texts.fn:App::read_from_clipboard_async:
Reads the system clipboard and resolves once the contents are available.

Prefer this over [`App::read_from_clipboard`] in code that can await. On
platforms where clipboard access is asynchronous and permission-gated (such as
the web), the synchronous read always returns `None` while this method performs
a real read. The task resolves to an error if the read fails.
doc_texts.fn:App::read_from_find_pasteboard:
Reads data from macOS's "Find" pasteboard.

Used to share the current search string between apps.

<https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appkit/nspasteboard/name-swift.struct/find>
doc_texts.fn:App::read_from_primary:
Reads data from the primary selection buffer.
Only available on Linux and FreeBSD.
doc_texts.fn:App::reduce_motion:
Returns whether non-essential animations should render in a static state.

Check this before you start a decorative animation, such as a spinner that only
looks busy. The app sets it, and it defaults to `false`.
doc_texts.fn:App::refresh_windows:
Redraws every window once the current update finishes.

Calling it several times in one update still causes a single redraw per window.
Use [`Context::notify`] on the entity that changed instead when you can. Use this
when state outside any entity changes what is drawn.
doc_texts.fn:App::register_inspector_element: Registers a renderer specific to an inspector state.
doc_texts.fn:App::register_url_scheme:
Registers `scheme` (for example `zed` for `zed://` links) so that links with it open this app.

Use [`Application::on_open_urls`] to receive the links. On some platforms you
declare schemes when you package the app. This method registers them at runtime.
doc_texts.fn:App::remove_asset: Removes the cached result for `source`, so the next [`App::fetch_asset`] loads it again.
doc_texts.fn:App::remove_global:
Removes the global of type `G` and returns it.

Notifies global observers when the current update finishes.

# Panics

Panics if no global of type `G` has been set.
doc_texts.fn:App::request_windowing:
Switches the platform between headless and windowed modes.

On Linux, headless means no display server: windows opened afterwards lay out and handle
input but draw nothing. Windowed, the platform connects to the display server the
environment names. On macOS, the modes set the [`ActivationPolicy`]: headless is
`Accessory` (no Dock icon or menu bar) and windowed is `Regular`. Switching to windowed
doesn't activate the app: call [`App::activate`] for that.

The returned task resolves once the switch has been applied. It fails if the platform is
already in the requested mode (switching to another display server means going headless
first), if the platform doesn't allow the mode or can't switch at all, if any window is
open (a window belongs to the display server that opened it), or if the display server
can't be reached.
doc_texts.fn:App::reset_prompt_builder: Reset the prompt builder to the default implementation.
doc_texts.fn:App::restart:
Restarts the app. Runs the handlers from [`App::on_app_restart`], then asks the
platform to relaunch it.

The relaunch uses the path from [`App::set_restart_path`] and the arguments from
[`Application::with_restart_arguments`].
doc_texts.fn:App::reveal_path: Shows `path` in the platform's file manager, such as Finder on macOS.
doc_texts.fn:App::screen_capture_sources:
Asks the platform for the screens and windows that can be captured.

The list arrives on the returned channel, so the call doesn't block. The channel
yields an error if the platform can't list sources. Check
[`App::is_screen_capture_supported`] first.
doc_texts.fn:App::set_activation_policy:
Sets whether the application participates in the system's foreground UI.

Only has an effect on macOS, where [`Self::request_windowing`] normally sets it. Use this
for an accessory app that shows windows, such as a menu bar utility. It overrides the
policy until the next [`Self::request_windowing`], and the app counts as headless while
`Accessory`. After switching to [`ActivationPolicy::Regular`], activate the app yourself
with [`Self::activate`]; otherwise its menu bar may not appear until the app is
reactivated.
doc_texts.fn:App::set_active_drag_cursor_style: Sets the cursor shown during the active drag. Returns `false` if no drag is in progress.
doc_texts.fn:App::set_app_identity:
Sets the app's identifier and user-visible name for the operating system.

The identifier is used for platform identity mechanisms such as the Windows
AppUserModelID. The name is shown wherever the operating system presents the app.
doc_texts.fn:App::set_cursor_hide_mode:
Sets the policy that decides when GPUI hides the cursor while typing.

Takes effect for the next keystroke. The cursor reappears when the mouse moves.
doc_texts.fn:App::set_dock_menu: Sets the menu that appears when the user right-clicks the app's Dock icon.
doc_texts.fn:App::set_gpu_requirements:
Sets the GPU device requirements (extra features and limits) for the renderer.
Only macOS uses them.

Call this before opening any window. The argument must be a
`gpui_wgpu::WgpuDeviceRequirements` boxed as `Box<dyn Any>`.
doc_texts.fn:App::set_http_client: Replaces the HTTP client that [`App::http_client`] returns.
doc_texts.fn:App::set_inspector_renderer: Sets the renderer for the inspector.
doc_texts.fn:App::set_keyring_label:
Sets the label applied to credentials stored in the system keyring.
Call before writing credentials. Only Linux/FreeBSD apply the label.
doc_texts.fn:App::set_menus:
Replaces the app's menu bar with `menus`.

Menu items that name an action show the key bindings from the keymap.
doc_texts.fn:App::set_prompt_builder:
Replaces the default and platform prompts with `renderer`.

The renderer is called for each prompt the app shows. It receives the prompt's
level, message, detail and buttons, and returns the handle that the window renders.
Use [`App::reset_prompt_builder`] to go back to the default prompts.
doc_texts.fn:App::set_quit_mode:
Sets when the app quits on its own. See [`QuitMode`].

Defaults to [`QuitMode::Default`].
doc_texts.fn:App::set_reduce_motion:
Sets whether non-essential animations should render in a static state.

Setting a different value redraws all windows. Animations that are needed to
show state, such as a progress bar, should keep running.
doc_texts.fn:App::set_restart_path: Sets the executable path that [`App::restart`] launches. The path is used once, by the next restart.
doc_texts.fn:App::set_text_rendering_mode:
Sets how text is rasterized for every window in the app.

The default is [`TextRenderingMode::PlatformDefault`]. The new mode applies to
text drawn after this call.
doc_texts.fn:App::set_window_appearance:
Overrides the appearance (light/dark) applied to the app's windows, independent of
the OS-wide setting. Pass `None` to clear the override and follow the system again.
The current value is reported by [`App::window_appearance`].

On macOS this sets the underlying `NSApplication.appearance`, which controls the
native window chrome (the window border and titlebar) of every window. Use this
when the app uses a dark theme while the system is in light mode (or vice versa)
so the window edges render to match the theme. While an appearance is forced,
windows stop tracking system light/dark changes; pass `None` to resume following
the system. On other platforms this is a no-op.
doc_texts.fn:App::should_auto_hide_scrollbars: Returns whether the user has configured scrollbars to auto-hide at the platform level.
doc_texts.fn:App::show_system_notification:
Posts a notification to the operating system's notification center.

Posting a notification whose [`SystemNotification::tag`] matches an
earlier one replaces that notification where the platform supports it.
No-op on platforms without notification support, or when delivery is
unavailable (e.g. authorization was denied).
doc_texts.fn:App::shutdown:
Runs the quit handlers, closes every window and flushes pending effects.

The platform calls this when the app quits. Handlers registered with
[`Context::on_app_quit`] run first. Native apps wait up to [`SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT`]
for them to finish and log an error if they don't. On the web the handlers run
asynchronously as best-effort cleanup, because the event loop cannot block.

To quit from your own code, call [`App::quit`] instead.
doc_texts.fn:App::spawn_with_priority: Like [`App::spawn`], but schedules the task with the given [`Priority`].
doc_texts.fn:App::start_drag:
Starts a drag with `drag` as its payload. Refresh the windows after calling this, so the drag shows.

# Panics

Debug builds panic if a drag is already in progress.
doc_texts.fn:App::start_hang_monitor:
Starts detecting foreground hangs on a dedicated thread.

Nothing is spawned unless the app calls this. The thread polls a
detector over this app's foreground journal every `config.interval`
and passes each poll's incidents, including empty polls, to `on_poll`
on that thread. When the app quits, a final poll with
[`HangMonitorPollReason::Flush`] runs during shutdown, concurrently
with quit handlers and within [`SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT`], so `on_poll` can
deliver batched results.

# Errors

Fails if the monitor was already started or its thread can't be
spawned.

[`HangMonitorPollReason::Flush`]: crate::profiler::hang::HangMonitorPollReason::Flush
doc_texts.fn:App::stop_active_drag: Stops active drag and clears any related effects.
doc_texts.fn:App::stop_drag:
Ends the drag in progress and returns its payload, if there was one.

Refresh the windows after calling this.
doc_texts.fn:App::stop_propagation:
Stops the current event or action from reaching later handlers.

Handlers for mouse events further down the z-order, and keyboard handlers higher
in the tree, don't run after this. Call [`App::propagate`] to undo it before the
effects are flushed.
doc_texts.fn:App::supports_haptic_feedback: Returns whether [`App::play_haptic_feedback`] does anything on this platform.
doc_texts.fn:App::svg_renderer: Returns the SVG renderer that draws the app's SVG assets.
doc_texts.fn:App::text_rendering_mode: Returns how text is currently rasterized. See [`App::set_text_rendering_mode`].
doc_texts.fn:App::text_system: Returns the app's [`TextSystem`], which shapes and rasterizes text.
doc_texts.fn:App::thermal_state:
Returns the system's current [`ThermalState`].

Check it before heavy work, such as a long animation or a background
computation, and reduce the work when the system is hot.
doc_texts.fn:App::to_async:
Returns an [`AsyncApp`] that can be held across `await` points.

The [`AsyncApp`] holds the app weakly, so it does not keep the app alive. Use
it in tasks that outlive the current update.
doc_texts.fn:App::try_global: Returns the global of type `G`, or `None` if it has not been set.
doc_texts.fn:App::unhide_other_apps: Shows the applications hidden by [`App::hide_other_apps`].
doc_texts.fn:App::update_jump_list:
Replaces the Windows jump list with `menus` and the recent `entries`.

Only Windows uses this. It also sets the dock menu.
doc_texts.fn:App::window_appearance:
Returns whether the windows use the light or dark appearance.

This is the system setting unless [`App::set_window_appearance`] overrides it.
doc_texts.fn:App::window_stack:
Returns the window handles ordered by their appearance on screen, front to back.

The first window in the returned list is the active/topmost window of the application.

This method returns None if the platform doesn't implement the method yet.
doc_texts.fn:App::windows:
Returns handles to every open window.

Each handle is untyped. [`AnyWindowHandle::downcast`] checks the root type recorded in
the handle. If the root may have been replaced, use [`AnyWindowHandle::update`] to
inspect the live root; the recorded type does not change with it.
doc_texts.fn:App::with_window:
Runs `f` with the window that most recently drew the entity `entity_id`.

If the entity has not been drawn yet, the window it was created in is used. The
callback receives the [`Window`] and the [`App`]. Returns `None` if the entity has
no current window, if that window has closed, or if the window is already being
updated higher up the call stack.
doc_texts.fn:App::write_credentials:
Stores a username and password for `url` in the platform keychain.

The task resolves once the store finishes, or to an error if it fails. Await it
from a task spawned with [`App::spawn`].
doc_texts.fn:App::write_to_find_pasteboard:
Writes data to macOS's "Find" pasteboard.

Used to share the current search string between apps.

<https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appkit/nspasteboard/name-swift.struct/find>
doc_texts.fn:App::write_to_primary:
Writes data to the primary selection buffer.
Only available on Linux and FreeBSD.
doc_texts.fn:Application::background_executor: Returns the executor for `Send` futures. See [`BackgroundExecutor`] for platform behavior.
doc_texts.fn:Application::foreground_executor: Returns the executor for futures that run on the foreground thread.
doc_texts.fn:Application::new_inaccessible:
Builds an app with accessibility (AccessKit) integration forcibly
disabled.

In this mode, accessibility APIs (e.g.
[`div().role()`][crate::StatefulInteractiveElement::role]) silently
no-op.

See the [accessibility guide](crate::_documentation::guides::accessibility) for the
features this disables.
doc_texts.fn:Application::on_open_urls:
Registers a handler for URLs that the user asks the app to open.

The handler receives the URLs as strings. Register a scheme with
[`App::register_url_scheme`] so the platform routes links with that scheme to
the app.
doc_texts.fn:Application::on_reopen:
Registers a handler for a second launch while the app is already running.

On macOS this happens when the user clicks the app icon in the Dock or in
Finder. A common response is to open a window if none is visible. The handler
receives the [`App`].
doc_texts.fn:Application::path_for_auxiliary_execu:
Returns the path to a helper executable named `name` that ships with the app.

Use this to launch a companion binary, such as a CLI or a helper process. It
returns an error if the platform cannot find the executable.
doc_texts.fn:Application::run:
Start the application. The provided callback will be called once the
app is fully launched.

On WebAssembly, this returns immediately and retains the app for the lifetime
of the Wasm instance. Use [`Self::run_embedded`] to control its lifetime explicitly.
doc_texts.fn:Application::run_embedded:
Start the application for an embedder that drives the run loop itself.

On ordinary platforms `Platform::run` blocks for the lifetime of the app, and the
app state is kept alive by [`Application::run`]'s stack frame. Embedded platforms —
where the run loop belongs to someone else, e.g. GPUI compiled into a Wasm guest,
or a GPUI view hosted inside a foreign native application — implement
`Platform::run` to invoke the launch callback and return immediately. This method
supports that shape: it returns an [`ApplicationHandle`] that keeps the app alive
and lets the embedder re-enter it whenever the external run loop yields control.
doc_texts.fn:Application::text_system: Returns a shared handle to the app's [`TextSystem`], which shapes and rasterizes text.
doc_texts.fn:Application::with_accessibility_force:
Build every window's accessibility tree every frame, even when no
assistive technology is connected.

For automation and tree inspection: [`crate::Window::debug_a11y_tree_json`]
otherwise reports nothing until a screen reader activates the platform
adapter. [`Application::new_inaccessible`] still wins when both are set.
doc_texts.fn:Application::with_activation_policy:
Sets the activation policy for the application (macOS only).

This determines how the application appears in the system:
- `Regular`: Normal app with Dock icon and menu bar
- `Accessory`: Background app without Dock icon (LSUIElement)
- `Prohibited`: Runs in background, no UI allowed

This must be called before the application finishes launching to take effect.
The method exists only on macOS, so cross-platform code calls it behind
`#[cfg(target_os = "macos")]`.
doc_texts.fn:Application::with_assets:
Sets the source of assets (images, fonts and SVGs) that the app loads by path.

The registry is returned by [`App::assets`], and the SVG renderer is rebuilt to
read from it. Set it before you open windows that load assets.
doc_texts.fn:Application::with_http_client:
Sets the HTTP client that [`App::http_client`] returns.

The default fails every request. Pass a real client to let the app fetch URLs,
for example for remote images.
doc_texts.fn:Application::with_platform:
Creates an application that uses a platform implementation you provide.

Most apps should use `gpui_platform::application()`, which chooses the platform
for you. Use this when you want a custom or test platform. The app starts with
an empty [`AssetRegistry`], an HTTP client that fails every request, and
[`QuitMode::Default`].

# Panics

Panics if called from a thread other than the main thread.
doc_texts.fn:Application::with_quit_mode:
Sets when the app quits on its own. See [`QuitMode`] for the choices.

Defaults to [`QuitMode::Default`]. You can also change it at runtime with
[`App::set_quit_mode`].
doc_texts.fn:Application::with_restart_arguments: Sets the command-line arguments that [`App::restart`] passes to the new process.
doc_texts.fn:Application::with_windowing:
Starts the event loop and calls `on_finish_launching` once the app has launched.

The callback runs on the main thread with the [`App`], and runs once. Open your
first window there. On native platforms this method blocks until the app quits,
so code after it runs only after the app exits. On the web it returns right away,
and the app keeps running in the page.

See the [`Application`] example for a complete `main`.
Sets the windowing mode the app starts in. See [`App::request_windowing`].

Defaults to windowed. On Linux, the default environment is the process's own, and the app
starts headless if that names no allowed display server. On macOS, headless means the app
starts without a Dock icon or menu bar ([`ActivationPolicy::Accessory`]). Has no effect on
other platforms.
doc_texts.fn:ApplicationHandle::to_async:
Returns an [`AsyncApp`] for use across await points.

The [`AsyncApp`] holds the app weakly. This handle must stay alive for the
[`AsyncApp`] to do anything useful.
doc_texts.fn:ApplicationHandle::update:
Runs `f` with the app context, from outside the platform's run loop.

Call this each time the external run loop gives GPUI control. Effects queued by `f`,
such as deferred callbacks, run before this returns. Don't call it from
inside an update on the same app: the app state is a `RefCell`, so a re-entrant
call panics with a double borrow.
doc_texts.fn:ArenaClearNeeded::clear:
Clear the element arena of the App the draw ran against. If an enclosing
draw is still in progress (this draw was nested inside it), the clear is
deferred to the enclosing draw's own `ArenaClearNeeded` so that its live
allocations aren't freed.

Panics if passed a different App than the draw ran against, since
clearing another App's arena could free memory its draws still
reference.
doc_texts.fn:AssetRegistry::extend:
Adds each `(path, entry)` pair in order.

# Errors

Returns the [`DuplicateAssetPath`] of every pair whose path was already registered, in
order. The other pairs are still added, and each duplicate is logged.
doc_texts.fn:AssetRegistry::iter_embed:
Yields every file in a [`RustEmbed`](rust_embed::RustEmbed) folder as a preloaded entry.

`T` is a type that derives `RustEmbed` for a folder. Each path is the file name relative to
that folder. Pass the iterator to [`AssetRegistry::extend`]. This needs the
`embedded-assets` feature of gpui, which also brings in the `rust-embed` crate.
doc_texts.fn:AssetRegistry::load:
Returns the bytes at `path`, or `None` if the path isn't registered.

Preloaded entries are returned as [`Cow::Borrowed`] with no copy. An on-demand entry runs its
loader on each call, so the bytes may be read from disk again. An on-demand loader that
returns `None` makes this return `None` too.
doc_texts.fn:AsyncApp::background_executor: Returns the [`BackgroundExecutor`], for running work on other threads.
doc_texts.fn:AsyncApp::foreground_executor: Returns the [`ForegroundExecutor`], for running futures on the main thread.
doc_texts.fn:AsyncApp::has_global: Returns whether a global of type `G` has been set.
doc_texts.fn:AsyncApp::is_test:
Whether this app runs on the deterministic test scheduler. See
[`BackgroundExecutor::is_test`].
doc_texts.fn:AsyncApp::open_window:
Opens a window with `options` and returns a handle to it.

`build_root_view` creates the window's root view. The method returns an error if the app is
quitting.

# Panics

Panics if the app has been released, or if it is already borrowed.
doc_texts.fn:AsyncApp::read_default_global:
Like [`AsyncApp::read_global`], but first sets a `G::default()` if no global of
type `G` has been set.
doc_texts.fn:AsyncApp::read_global:
Calls `read` with the global of type `G` and the app, and returns its result.

Use [`AsyncApp::try_read_global`] if the global may not be set.

# Panics

Panics if no global of type `G` has been set, or if the app has been released.
doc_texts.fn:AsyncApp::refresh:
Schedules a redraw of every window.

The windows draw on the next frame. This doesn't draw anything itself.
doc_texts.fn:AsyncApp::spawn:
Runs the future returned by `f` on the main thread, and returns a task for its
result.

`f` receives an `&mut AsyncApp`. Dropping the returned [`Task`] cancels the
future, so store it, await it or call [`Task::detach`].
doc_texts.fn:AsyncApp::subscribe:
Calls `on_event` each time `entity` emits an `Event`.

The callback receives the emitting entity, the event and the app. The
subscription stays active while you hold it. Dropping it unsubscribes, and
[`Subscription::detach`] keeps the subscription for as long as the entity lives.
Inside an entity's own context, [`Context::subscribe`] is the usual choice.
doc_texts.fn:AsyncApp::try_read_global:
Like [`AsyncApp::read_global`], but returns `None` instead of panicking when no
global of type `G` is set, or when the app is quitting.
doc_texts.fn:AsyncApp::update:
Runs `f` with the app and returns its result.

Effects queued by `f`, such as notifications, are flushed before this returns.

# Panics

Panics if the app has been released, or if it is already borrowed, such as when
called from inside another update.
doc_texts.fn:AsyncApp::update_global:
Updates the global of type `G` with `update`, and returns its result.

While `update` runs, the global is taken out of the app. Reading it through the
app from inside `update` panics, so change the global through the `&mut G` that
`update` receives.

# Panics

Panics if no global of type `G` has been set, or if the app has been released.
doc_texts.fn:AsyncWindowContext::on_next_frame:
Runs `f` before the window draws its next frame. Does nothing if the window has
closed.

Schedules the callback like [`Window::on_next_frame`], but tolerates a window that has
already been closed.
doc_texts.fn:AsyncWindowContext::prompt:
Shows a platform alert with one button for each entry in `answers`.

The receiver resolves to the index of the button the user clicked. If the window
has closed, the receiver is canceled, so awaiting it returns an error. See
[`Window::prompt`] for `level` and `detail`.
doc_texts.fn:AsyncWindowContext::read_global:
Calls `read` with the global of type `G`, the window and the app, and returns its
result.

# Errors

Returns an error if the window has closed.

# Panics

Panics if no global of type `G` has been set.
doc_texts.fn:AsyncWindowContext::spawn:
Runs the future returned by `f` on the main thread, with an
`AsyncWindowContext` for this window, and returns a task for its result.

Dropping the returned [`Task`] cancels the future. Store it, await it or call
[`Task::detach`].
doc_texts.fn:AsyncWindowContext::update:
Runs `update` with the window and the app, and returns its result.

Effects queued by `update` are flushed before this returns.

# Errors

Returns an error if the window has closed, or if the app is quitting or already
borrowed.
doc_texts.fn:AsyncWindowContext::update_global:
Updates the global of type `G` with `update`, and returns its result.

The global is taken out of the app while `update` runs, as with
[`AsyncApp::update_global`].

# Errors

Returns an error if the window has closed.

# Panics

Panics if no global of type `G` has been set.
doc_texts.fn:AsyncWindowContext::update_root:
Like [`AsyncWindowContext::update`], but also passes the window's root view.

# Errors

Returns an error under the same conditions as [`AsyncWindowContext::update`].
doc_texts.fn:AsyncWindowContext::window_handle: Returns the handle of the window this context is for.
doc_texts.fn:AtlasKey::texture_kind: Returns the texture kind for this atlas key.
doc_texts.fn:AtlasTextureKind::validate_upload:
Validates a tightly packed bitmap before an atlas allocates or caches its tile.
Monochrome tiles contain one coverage byte; color and LCD tiles contain four bytes.
doc_texts.fn:BackdropFilter::max_blur_radius: Returns the largest Gaussian blur radius in this filter chain, in device pixels.
doc_texts.fn:Background::as_solid: Returns the color if this is a solid background, and `None` otherwise.
doc_texts.fn:Background::color_space:
Sets the color space that a gradient's colors are interpolated in.

The default for [`linear_gradient`] is [`ColorSpace::Oklab`]. Solid colors and patterns
don't interpolate, so this has no effect on them.

<https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/color-interpolation-method>
doc_texts.fn:Background::interpolation_space: The color space used to interpolate this background, set by [`Background::color_space`].
doc_texts.fn:Background::is_transparent:
Returns whether this background paints nothing.

A solid, pattern or checkerboard background is transparent when its color has zero
alpha. A gradient is transparent only when both of its stops have zero alpha.
doc_texts.fn:Background::kind: Returns the decoded form of this background.
doc_texts.fn:Background::opacity:
Returns a copy of this background with the alpha of every color multiplied by `factor`.

The factor is clamped to `0.0..=1.0`. Gradient stops are scaled too.
doc_texts.fn:BackgroundExecutor::advance_clock:
Moves the simulated clock forward by `duration`.

Ready tasks run as the clock passes each timer, in time order, so a task that
waits on a timer resumes at the right moment. When the call returns, the clock
reads its earlier value plus `duration`. Only available in tests.

# Panics

Panics if this executor isn't a test executor.
doc_texts.fn:BackgroundExecutor::allow_parking:
Lets blocking waits in tests sleep in real time when no test work can make progress.

By default, a blocking call that cannot progress panics. With parking allowed, it waits
in real time instead, and the test fails if the wait lasts 15 seconds. Use this for tests
that wait on real I/O. Undo it with [`BackgroundExecutor::forbid_parking`].
doc_texts.fn:BackgroundExecutor::dispatcher:
Returns the platform dispatcher this executor sends work through. GPUI uses this
internally.
doc_texts.fn:BackgroundExecutor::forbid_parking:
Undoes [`BackgroundExecutor::allow_parking`], so a blocking call that can't
progress panics again. Only available in tests.
doc_texts.fn:BackgroundExecutor::is_main_thread: Returns whether the current thread is the main thread.
doc_texts.fn:BackgroundExecutor::is_test:
Whether this executor runs on the deterministic test scheduler.

Available in every build. Use it, rather than `cfg(feature =
"test-support")`, for behavior that must differ under tests, so that
compiling `test-support` into an application doesn't change it.
doc_texts.fn:BackgroundExecutor::new:
Creates an executor that sends its work through `dispatcher`.

Platform code creates the executor. Apps get one from [`App::background_executor`].
doc_texts.fn:BackgroundExecutor::now:
Returns the current time.

Use this in place of `std::time::Instant::now` so that tests can control time. In
tests it reads the simulated clock, which moves only when the test advances it.
doc_texts.fn:BackgroundExecutor::num_cpus:
Returns the number of CPUs the dispatcher reports.

In tests this is 4 unless it was changed with [`BackgroundExecutor::set_num_cpus`].
doc_texts.fn:BackgroundExecutor::prevent_app_nap:
Prevents App Nap-style throttling while the returned guard is held.

This does not prevent the system from entering idle sleep.
doc_texts.fn:BackgroundExecutor::rng:
Returns the seeded random number generator that the test scheduler uses.

Draw from it when a test makes its own random choices, so that the choices
repeat with the same `SEED`. Only available in tests.
doc_texts.fn:BackgroundExecutor::run_until_parked:
Runs ready tasks in tests until none can make progress.

This doesn't move the simulated clock. A timer that hasn't expired stays pending,
until [`BackgroundExecutor::advance_clock`] moves time past it. Only available in
tests.
doc_texts.fn:BackgroundExecutor::scheduler_executo: Returns the underlying scheduler executor, for code that takes one directly.
doc_texts.fn:BackgroundExecutor::scoped_priority:
Like [`BackgroundExecutor::scoped`], but runs every future in the scope at
`priority`.
doc_texts.fn:BackgroundExecutor::set_block_on_tick:
Sets the range that the tick budget of a [`ForegroundExecutor::block_with_timeout`]
call is drawn from, in tests.

The default is 1 to 1000 ticks. Only available in tests.
doc_texts.fn:BackgroundExecutor::set_num_cpus:
Sets the value that [`BackgroundExecutor::num_cpus`] returns, in tests.

# Panics

Panics if this executor isn't a test executor.
doc_texts.fn:BackgroundExecutor::simulate_random_d:
Yields a random number of times, allowing other ready tasks to run between steps.

Await it between steps of a test to shake out ordering bugs. Only available in
tests.

# Panics

Panics if this executor isn't a test executor.
doc_texts.fn:BackgroundExecutor::spawn_dedicated:
Runs the future that `f` returns on a thread of its own, and returns a task for
its result.

Use this instead of [`BackgroundExecutor::spawn`] for work whose polls need more
stack than the shared background threads provide. A dedicated thread gets the
standard library's default stack of 2 MiB. Dropping the task cancels the work, as it
does for any task.
doc_texts.fn:BackgroundExecutor::spawn_with_priori:
Like [`BackgroundExecutor::spawn`], but with a [`Priority`].

Higher priorities are more likely to run first, but the order isn't guaranteed.
[`Priority::RealtimeAudio`] runs the future on a dedicated thread with realtime
scheduling. Use it only for audio work.
doc_texts.fn:BackgroundExecutor::tick:
Runs one unit of ready work in tests.

Returns `true` if it ran a task or fired a timer, and `false` if there was nothing
to do. Only available in tests.

# Panics

Panics if this executor isn't a test executor.
doc_texts.fn:Bounds::bottom: Returns the y coordinate of the bottom edge, which is outside the bounds.
doc_texts.fn:Bounds::left: Returns the x coordinate of the left edge.
doc_texts.fn:Bounds::right: Returns the x coordinate of the right edge, which is outside the bounds.
doc_texts.fn:Bounds::top: Returns the y coordinate of the top edge.
doc_texts.fn:BoxShadow::new:
Creates a new [`BoxShadow`] with the given offset and color. The blur and spread
radii are 0 and the shadow is outset. Use the builder methods to change them, or to
make the shadow inset.
doc_texts.fn:CaretAffinity::for_inserted_text:
Returns the affinity for a caret placed right after `text` was inserted.

Returns [`CaretAffinity::Downstream`] when `text` is empty or ends with a hard line break,
so the caret starts the next line. Otherwise it returns [`CaretAffinity::Upstream`].
doc_texts.fn:CaretMovement::move_or_select_to:
Moves the caret to `caret`, or extends the selection to it when `extend` is true.

Either way, the retained vertical coordinate is cleared.
doc_texts.fn:CaretPosition::attached_to_next_clust: Creates a caret attached to the next logical cluster.
doc_texts.fn:CaretPosition::attached_to_previous_c: Creates a caret attached to the previous logical cluster.
doc_texts.fn:CaretSelection::byte_range: Returns the selected UTF-8 byte range, with the smaller index first.
doc_texts.fn:CaretSelection::endpoint_ordering: Compares the caret's byte index with the anchor's. `Less` means the caret is before the anchor.
doc_texts.fn:CaretSelection::is_empty:
Returns whether the anchor and the caret have the same byte index.

Affinity is ignored, so a caret at a wrap point with two affinities is still empty.
doc_texts.fn:CaretSelection::min: Limits both selection endpoints to `max_idx` while preserving their affinities.
doc_texts.fn:CaretSelection::with_caret: Moves the active end while preserving the anchor.
doc_texts.fn:ClickEvent::click_count:
Returns how many clicks in a row this click completes. A double click is 2.

A keyboard click always returns 1. A mouse click returns the count from its
release. A touch click returns its tap count.
doc_texts.fn:ClickEvent::first_focus:
Returns `true` if this click activated the window, as reported by the
platform in [`MouseDownEvent::first_mouse`].

Keyboard and touch clicks always return `false`. A keyboard click needs
the element to be focused already.
doc_texts.fn:ClickEvent::is_keyboard: Returns `true` if this click came from the keyboard.
doc_texts.fn:ClickEvent::is_middle_click:
Returns `true` if this is a mouse click made with the middle button.

Keyboard and touch clicks always return `false`.
doc_texts.fn:ClickEvent::is_right_click:
Returns `true` if this is a mouse click made with the right button.

Keyboard and touch clicks always return `false`. Use
[`ClickEvent::is_secondary`] to also match long presses.
doc_texts.fn:ClickEvent::is_secondary:
Returns `true` if this click is a secondary activation, the kind that
usually opens a context menu.

That is a right-button mouse click, or a long press when a future direct
touch click is delivered. On macOS, Control-clicks already arrive as right
clicks. Keyboard clicks always return `false`.
doc_texts.fn:ClickEvent::modifiers:
Returns the modifier keys held during the click.

Keyboard and touch clicks have none, so this returns the default
[`Modifiers`]. A mouse click returns the modifiers held when the button was
released.
doc_texts.fn:ClickEvent::mouse_position:
Returns the mouse position of the click, or `None` if it did not come from
a mouse.

Keyboard and touch clicks return `None`. Use [`ClickEvent::position`] when
you need a position for every kind.
doc_texts.fn:ClickEvent::position:
Returns the window position of the click, in logical pixels.

For a mouse click this is where the button was released. For a touch it
is where the tap happened. For a keyboard click, which has no pointer,
it is the bottom-left corner of the clicked element.
doc_texts.fn:ClickEvent::standard_click:
Returns `true` for a primary activation: a left-button click, a keyboard
click, or a direct touch tap that is not a long press.

Right, middle and navigation button clicks return `false`. Use
[`ClickEvent::is_secondary`] to test for the right button and long presses.
doc_texts.fn:ClipboardItem::into_entries: Consumes the item and returns its entries.
doc_texts.fn:ClipboardItem::metadata:
Returns the metadata of the item's string entry, or `None`.

Returns `None` unless the item has exactly one entry and that entry is a string.
doc_texts.fn:ClipboardItem::new_image: Creates an item holding a copy of `image`.
doc_texts.fn:ClipboardItem::new_string: Creates an item holding `text`, with no metadata.
doc_texts.fn:ClipboardItem::new_string_with_json_m:
Creates an item holding `text` and `metadata`, serialized as JSON.

Read the metadata back with [`ClipboardString::metadata_json`].

# Panics

Panics if `metadata` can't be serialized to JSON, such as a map with non-string keys.
doc_texts.fn:ClipboardItem::new_string_with_metada:
Creates an item holding `text` and a raw `metadata` string.

Use [`ClipboardItem::new_string_with_json_metadata`] to store structured data.
doc_texts.fn:ClipboardItem::text:
Returns the text of all string entries joined together, or `None` if the item has no text.

If the string entries contain no text, the file paths of any [`ClipboardEntry::ExternalPaths`]
entries are joined with no separator instead. The result is `None` if there are no paths either.
doc_texts.fn:ClipboardString::into_text: Consumes the string and returns its text.
doc_texts.fn:ClipboardString::metadata_json:
Returns the metadata deserialized as `T`.

Returns `None` if there is no metadata or it doesn't deserialize as `T`.
doc_texts.fn:ClipboardString::new: Creates a clipboard string with `text` and no metadata.
doc_texts.fn:ClipboardString::text: Returns the text.
doc_texts.fn:ClipboardString::text_hash: Returns a hash of `text`. Use it to detect whether the clipboard text has changed.
doc_texts.fn:ClipboardString::with_json_metadata:
Sets the metadata to `metadata`, serialized as JSON. Returns the updated string.

# Panics

Panics if `metadata` can't be serialized to JSON.
doc_texts.fn:ContentMask::intersect:
Returns the region visible through both this mask and `other`.

For each edge, the mask that actually clips at that edge contributes its
fade; when both masks clip at the same coordinate, the stronger fade wins.
doc_texts.fn:ContentMask::scale: Returns this mask in [`ScaledPixels`], with every value multiplied by `factor`.
doc_texts.fn:Context::defer_in:
Runs `f` with this entity and `window` at the end of the current effect cycle.

Use it to change this entity from code that is still on the stack, such as a method called from
inside this entity's own update. The callback runs after the outermost update finishes, when the
entity is no longer borrowed. It doesn't run if this entity has been released.
doc_texts.fn:Context::entity:
Returns a strong handle to the entity this context works on.

The handle keeps the entity alive. Use [`Context::weak_entity`] when a callback should not
keep it alive.
doc_texts.fn:Context::entity_id: Returns the id of the entity this context works on.
doc_texts.fn:Context::focus_self:
Focuses this entity's focus handle in `window`.

This entity must implement [`Focusable`]. The focus change happens at the end of the current effect
cycle.
doc_texts.fn:Context::focus_view:
Focuses `view` in `window`.

`W` must implement [`Focusable`]. The focus change uses the focus handle that `view` returns.
doc_texts.fn:Context::observe_button_layout_change:
Calls `callback` when the window's titlebar button layout changes.

Keep the returned [`Subscription`] alive for as long as you want the callback to run. The callback
stops once this entity is released.
doc_texts.fn:Context::observe_global:
Calls `f` whenever the global of type `G` is set or updated.

`f` runs after the update that changed the global finishes. It doesn't receive the value, so
read it with [`App::global`]. Keep the returned [`Subscription`] alive for as long as you want
the callback to run. To also receive a window, use [`Context::observe_global_in`].
doc_texts.fn:Context::observe_global_in:
Calls `f` with the window whenever the global of type `G` is set or updated.

Pass the window this entity is shown in. If that window is unavailable, for example during a nested
update of it, the callback is skipped for that change and stays registered. The callback stops
once this entity is released.
doc_texts.fn:Context::observe_in:
Calls `on_notify` when `observed` calls [`Context::notify`], and passes it the window.

Pass the window that displays this entity. If that window has been closed, the callback
does not run.
doc_texts.fn:Context::observe_keystrokes:
Calls `f` with this entity for each keystroke that [`App::observe_keystrokes`] observes.

The keystroke's `action` is set when a key binding handled it. Keep the returned
[`Subscription`] alive for as long as you want the callback to run.
doc_texts.fn:Context::observe_pending_input:
Calls `callback` when the pending input of `window` changes.

Pending input is a partly typed key sequence, such as the first key of a multi-key binding. The
callback runs when the sequence starts, grows, or is cleared. Keep the returned [`Subscription`]
alive for as long as you want the callback to run.
doc_texts.fn:Context::observe_release:
Calls `on_release` when `entity` is released.

The callback receives this entity mutably and the released value. It doesn't run if this entity
has been released too. The callback stays registered while the returned [`Subscription`] is
alive.
doc_texts.fn:Context::observe_release_in:
Calls `on_release` when `observed` is released, and passes it the window.

The callback does not run if `window` has been closed, or if this entity has been released.
doc_texts.fn:Context::observe_self:
Calls `on_event` whenever this entity calls [`Context::notify`].

It runs after the update that called `notify` finishes. Keep the returned
[`Subscription`] alive for as long as you want the callback to run.
doc_texts.fn:Context::observe_window_activation:
Calls `callback` when `window` becomes active or inactive.

Keep the returned [`Subscription`] alive for as long as you want the callback to run. The callback
stops once this entity is released.
doc_texts.fn:Context::observe_window_appearance:
Calls `callback` when the system appearance changes between light and dark.

Keep the returned [`Subscription`] alive for as long as you want the callback to run. The callback
stops once this entity is released.
doc_texts.fn:Context::observe_window_bounds:
Calls `callback` when the bounds of `window` change.

Keep the returned [`Subscription`] alive for as long as you want the callback to run. The callback
stops once this entity is released.
doc_texts.fn:Context::observe_window_display:
Registers a callback invoked when the window moves to another display
or its display's refresh interval changes. See
[`Window::observe_window_display`].
doc_texts.fn:Context::observe_window_visibility:
Registers a callback to be invoked when the window's visibility changes
(see [`WindowVisibility`]).
doc_texts.fn:Context::on_action:
Calls `listener` when an action of type `action_type` is dispatched to `window`.

Pass `TypeId::of::<A>()` for the action type `A`. The listener receives the action as `&dyn Any`
together with the [`DispatchPhase`], so it can tell capture from bubble. It also gets the window and
a context for this entity.

Like [`Window::on_action`], the listener is registered for the next frame only. Call this during
paint, on every frame that should handle the action.
doc_texts.fn:Context::on_app_quit:
Calls `on_quit` when the application quits, and waits for the future it returns.

GPUI polls the returned future for up to [`SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT`](crate::SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT) while the
app quits. Use this to save state before the process exits. The callback doesn't run if this
entity has been released.
doc_texts.fn:Context::on_app_restart:
Calls `on_restart` when the application is about to restart.

The callback doesn't run if this entity has been released. Keep the returned [`Subscription`]
alive for as long as you want the callback to run.
doc_texts.fn:Context::on_blur:
Calls `listener` when `handle` stops being the focused element.

The listener also runs when focus moves from `handle` to one of its descendants, since `handle`
is no longer the focused element. Use [`Context::on_focus_out`] to hear only about focus leaving
`handle` and its descendants. Keep the returned [`Subscription`] alive for as long as you want the
listener to run.
doc_texts.fn:Context::on_drop:
Returns a guard that calls `f` with this entity when the guard is dropped.

The guard is returned as a `Deferred`. Call `abort` on it to cancel the callback. If the entity
has been released by the time the guard is dropped, `f` doesn't run.

# Panics

Panics if the guard is dropped while the app is already borrowed, for example inside another
update of the same app, and the entity is still alive. Drop the guard from a later update instead.
doc_texts.fn:Context::on_focus:
Calls `listener` when `handle` becomes the focused element.

The listener doesn't run when focus moves into a descendant of `handle`. Use [`Context::on_focus_in`]
to hear about that as well. Keep the returned [`Subscription`] alive for as long as you want the
listener to run.
doc_texts.fn:Context::on_focus_in:
Calls `listener` when focus moves into `handle` or one of its descendants.

The listener doesn't run when focus was already inside `handle` and moves to another descendant.
Keep the returned [`Subscription`] alive for as long as you want the listener to run.
doc_texts.fn:Context::on_focus_lost:
Calls `listener` when no element in `window` has focus.

This happens when the focused element is removed from the tree. Use it to move focus to a sensible
default. Keep the returned [`Subscription`] alive for as long as you want the listener to run.
doc_texts.fn:Context::on_focus_out:
Calls `listener` when focus leaves `handle` or one of its descendants.

The listener receives a [`FocusOutEvent`] that says which element lost focus. Keep the returned
[`Subscription`] alive for as long as you want the listener to run.
doc_texts.fn:Context::on_next_frame:
Runs `f` with this entity and `window` on the next frame of `window`.

The callback runs once, during the next frame. It doesn't run if this entity has been released.
doc_texts.fn:Context::on_release:
Calls `on_release` when GPUI releases this entity.

GPUI releases an entity at the end of the update in which its last strong handle was dropped.
The callback runs then, while the value still exists, and receives it mutably together with the
app. Use it to tear down resources the entity holds outside GPUI.

The callback stays registered while the returned [`Subscription`] is alive. Dropping the
subscription cancels the callback. Call [`Subscription::detach`] to keep it until the entity is
released.
doc_texts.fn:Context::on_release_in:
Calls `on_release` with the window when this entity is released.

The callback doesn't run if the window was closed before this entity was released.
doc_texts.fn:Context::processor:
Wraps `f` in a closure that receives this entity mutably and returns a value.

Use this when the caller needs the handler's return value. For event handlers, prefer
[`Context::listener`]. The returned closure holds a strong handle to this entity, so it
keeps the entity alive for as long as the closure exists.
doc_texts.fn:Context::spawn_in:
Runs the future returned by `f` on the main thread, with a weak handle to this entity and a window
context.

`f` receives an [`AsyncWindowContext`] for `window`, so the future can reach it after an
`.await`. Window operations through the context return errors once the window has closed.

The returned [`Task`] cancels the future when it's dropped. Call [`Task::detach`] to let the future
run to completion.
doc_texts.fn:Context::spawn_in_with_priority:
Runs the future returned by `f` on the main thread at `priority`, with a weak handle to this entity
and a window context.

The returned [`Task`] cancels the future when it is dropped.
doc_texts.fn:Context::subscribe_in:
Calls `on_event` when `emitter` emits an event of type `Evt`, and passes it the window.

Pass the window that displays this entity. If that window has been closed, the callback
does not run.
doc_texts.fn:Context::subscribe_self:
Calls `on_event` whenever this entity emits an event of type `Evt`.

This is [`Context::subscribe`] for events that this entity emits itself. Keep the returned
[`Subscription`] alive for as long as you want the callback to run.
doc_texts.fn:Context::weak_entity:
Returns a weak handle to the entity this context works on.

Store the weak handle in callbacks and tasks that can outlive the current update. Upgrade it
when you need the entity, and handle the case where it has been released.
doc_texts.fn:Deferred::priority_auto:
Sets the priority to one more than the enclosing deferred element's, or to 1 when no deferred
element encloses this one.

A deferred element is enclosing when it is being prepainted and creates this one, directly or
through other elements. Use it for nested popups, so that each level draws above the last.
doc_texts.fn:DispatchPhase::bubble: Returns `true` if this is the bubble phase.
doc_texts.fn:DispatchPhase::capture: Returns `true` if this is the capture phase.
doc_texts.fn:DisplayId::new: Creates a `DisplayId` from a raw platform display identifier.
doc_texts.fn:Div::image_cache:
Puts an image cache at this point in the element tree.

Descendants of this element use this cache for the images they load, instead of the cache of an ancestor.
doc_texts.fn:Div::on_children_prepainted:
Runs `listener` after the children have been prepainted, with their bounds in order.

Use it to record where children ended up, for example to scroll to one of them later. The bounds are in window
coordinates. The listener runs once per frame.
doc_texts.fn:Div::with_dynamic_prepaint_order:
Sets a function that chooses the order in which children are prepainted.

The function runs at prepaint and returns the indices of the children in the order to prepaint them. Each index
must appear exactly once. Use it when one child's prepaint changes state that another child reads, such as an
editor that must scroll before its sibling reads the scroll position.
doc_texts.fn:DivFrameState::measured_inline_paragr: Returns the display text and layout used to paint each inline paragraph.
doc_texts.fn:DragMoveEvent::drag:
Returns the value of the active drag, cast to `T`.

# Panics

Panics if the active drag is not of type `T`. The listener runs only for drags of type `T`, so this is a
bug in the code that started the drag.
doc_texts.fn:DragMoveEvent::dragged_item: Returns the value that is being dragged, as a `dyn Any`. Downcast it to get the concrete type.
doc_texts.fn:DropListener::can_drop_anywhere:
Sets a predicate that decides whether this handler receives drops, whether or not the pointer is over the element.

The predicate receives the dragged value, the element's hitbox, and the window and app. Check
[`Hitbox::is_hovered`] yourself if you need the pointer to be over the element.
doc_texts.fn:DropListener::can_drop_within:
Sets a predicate that decides whether this handler receives drops, which runs only while the pointer is over the element.

The predicate receives the dragged value and the window and app. The hitbox check is added for you, so the
predicate need not check it. A predicate on a listener for another type never runs.
doc_texts.fn:DropListener::into_any:
Converts this typed listener into one that stores any value and checks the type at runtime.

GPUI calls this when you pass a `DropListener` to [`InteractiveElement::on_drop_alt`]. The callbacks downcast the
dragged value to `T`. `on_drag_over` and `on_drop` panic if they receive another type, so register the listener only
for the type it was written for.
doc_texts.fn:DropListener::on_drag_over:
Sets the style to apply while a value of type `T` is dragged over the element.

The style applies only if [`can_drop`](DropListener::can_drop) allows the value, and only while the pointer is over the element.
doc_texts.fn:DropListener::on_drop:
Sets the function that handles a value of type `T` released over the element.

It runs only if [`can_drop`](DropListener::can_drop) allows the value. It receives the dragged value and the mouse
release event.
doc_texts.fn:Easing::new:
Creates an easing from `easing`, which maps `0.0..=1.0` to an eased value.

The result is not clamped, so the function may overshoot. It must return finite values.
doc_texts.fn:Easing::sample:
Returns the eased value of `progress`.

# Panics

Panics if the easing function returns NaN or an infinite value.
doc_texts.fn:ElementId::named_usize:
Returns an `ElementId::NamedInteger` made from `name` and `integer`.

It is the same as `(name, integer).into()` for a `usize` integer.
doc_texts.fn:ElementInputHandler::new:
Creates a handler that forwards platform text input to `view`.

Pass the bounds of the element that is painting. They are returned from
[`InputHandler::element_bounds`] and passed to
[`EntityInputHandler::bounds_for_range`]. Call this in
[`Element::paint`][element_paint], then pass the handler to
[`Window::handle_input`](crate::Window::handle_input). The window installs the handler only while the
given focus handle is focused.

[element_paint]: crate::Element::paint
doc_texts.fn:Entity::as_mut:
Returns a guard that dereferences to the value, so you can change it with `*` or with methods.

The guard borrows `cx` for as long as it lives. When the guard is dropped, the entity is notified,
as if you had called [`Context::notify`]. Use [`Entity::update`] when the change needs a
[`Context`].
doc_texts.fn:Entity::cached:
Returns this entity as an element laid out at a fixed root style.

An entity passed directly as a child already keeps its output while nothing it read has
changed, and sizes itself from its content. Use `cached` when the parent should decide the
view's root style instead: the view is laid out at `style`, and its content is laid out
within the bounds that style produces. See
[retained rendering](crate::_documentation::concepts::retained_rendering).
doc_texts.fn:Entity::condition:
Returns a future that resolves when `predicate` returns `true` for this entity.

The predicate is checked when the future is first polled, then again after
each notification or event from the entity.

# Panics

Panics if the entity is released while the future waits.
doc_texts.fn:Entity::downgrade:
Returns a [`WeakEntity`] to the same value.

A weak handle doesn't keep the value alive. Use it for back-references, and for callbacks that may
run after the entity is released.
doc_texts.fn:Entity::entity_id:
Returns the id of the entity.

Two handles have the same id exactly when they refer to the same entity.
doc_texts.fn:Entity::into_any: Converts this handle into an [`AnyEntity`]. The result keeps the value alive, without its type.
doc_texts.fn:Entity::next_event:
Returns a future that resolves with the next event `self` emits.

The subscription is made when you call this, not when you await the future, so
an event emitted in between is still received.

# Panics

Panics if the entity is released before it emits an event.
doc_texts.fn:Entity::next_notification:
Returns a future that resolves on the entity's next notification.

This advances the simulated clock by `advance_clock_by` as soon as you call it,
before the future is awaited. Use it when the notification comes from a timer
that the advance will fire.

# Panics

Panics if the entity is released while the future waits.
doc_texts.fn:Entity::read_with:
Calls `read` with the value and the app, and returns what `read` returns.

Use this when the callback needs the app as well as the value. It works with any [`AppContext`],
including [`Context`] and [`AsyncApp`](crate::AsyncApp). It panics in the same cases as [`Entity::read`].
doc_texts.fn:Entity::update_in:
Like [`Entity::update`], but also passes the [`Window`] that the entity is shown in.

Use it from a [`VisualContext`], which is a context that has a window. Returns an error if the
window has been closed.
doc_texts.fn:ExternalPaths::paths: Returns the dropped paths in the order the platform reported them.
doc_texts.fn:FileDragPaths::entries: Returns the dragged paths, each paired with whether it is a directory.
doc_texts.fn:FileDragPaths::new: Creates a drag payload from paths, each paired with whether it is a directory.
doc_texts.fn:Fill::color:
Unwrap this fill into a solid color, if it is one.

If the fill is not a solid color, this method returns `None`.
doc_texts.fn:Filter::is_identity:
Whether this filter has no visible effect, so painting can skip it entirely (and the
element can avoid the offscreen isolation pass when *all* of its filters are identities).

Each variant defines its own no-op case. A filter that returns `true` is dropped before it
reaches the renderer.
doc_texts.fn:Filter::scale:
Lower this logical-pixel filter into its scene-space ([`ScaledFilter`]) form for the
renderer, scaling any pixel magnitudes by `factor` (the window scale factor).
doc_texts.fn:FilterBoundary::max_blur_radius: Returns the largest Gaussian blur radius in this filter chain, in device pixels.
doc_texts.fn:FocusHandle::contains: Returns whether `other` is this element or a descendant of it, using the last rendered frame.
doc_texts.fn:FocusHandle::contains_focused: Returns whether the focused element is this element or one of its descendants.
doc_texts.fn:FocusHandle::dispatch_action:
Dispatches `action` along the element that rendered this handle.

The action runs through the element's capture and bubble listeners,
the same way a keybinding would dispatch it. Nothing happens if the
element isn't in the last rendered frame.
doc_texts.fn:FocusHandle::downgrade: Returns a [`WeakFocusHandle`] that doesn't keep the focus id alive.
doc_texts.fn:FocusHandle::focus: Moves focus to this handle's element. Same as [`Window::focus`].
doc_texts.fn:FocusHandle::is_focused: Returns whether this handle's element has focus.
doc_texts.fn:FocusHandle::tab_stop:
Sets whether this handle is a tab stop.

When `false`, [`Window::focus_next`] and [`Window::focus_prev`] skip this element.
Programmatic focus with [`Window::focus`] still works.
doc_texts.fn:FocusHandle::within_focused: Returns whether the focused element is this element's ancestor or the element itself.
doc_texts.fn:Font::bold: Returns this font with the weight set to [`FontWeight::BOLD`].
doc_texts.fn:Font::italic: Returns this font with the style set to [`FontStyle::Italic`].
doc_texts.fn:FontFallbacks::fallback_list: Returns the fallback families in the order the text system tries them.
doc_texts.fn:FontFallbacks::from_fonts: Creates a fallback list from family names, tried in the order given.
doc_texts.fn:FontFeatures::disable_ligatures:
Returns features that turn off `calt`, which many fonts use for programming ligatures.

Other features, such as `liga`, keep the font's default.
doc_texts.fn:FontFeatures::is_calt_enabled:
Returns whether `calt` is enabled, or `None` if this set doesn't mention `calt`.

Only the value `1` counts as enabled. Any other value, including `2`, returns `Some(false)`.
doc_texts.fn:FontFeatures::tag_value_list:
Returns the feature tags and values, in the order they were set.

Only features that were set are listed. A feature that isn't listed
keeps the font's default.
doc_texts.fn:FontMetrics::ascent: Returns the distance from the baseline up to the tallest glyphs, in pixels at `font_size`.
doc_texts.fn:FontMetrics::bounding_box: Returns the outer limits of the area that the font covers, in pixels at `font_size`.
doc_texts.fn:FontMetrics::cap_height: Returns the height of a capital letter above the baseline, in pixels at `font_size`.
doc_texts.fn:FontMetrics::descent: Returns the distance from the baseline down to the lowest glyphs, in pixels at `font_size`.
doc_texts.fn:FontMetrics::line_gap: Returns the recommended extra space between lines, in pixels at `font_size`.
doc_texts.fn:FontMetrics::underline_position: Returns the suggested position of the underline, in pixels at `font_size`.
doc_texts.fn:FontMetrics::underline_thickness: Returns the suggested thickness of the underline, in pixels at `font_size`.
doc_texts.fn:FontMetrics::x_height: Returns the height of a lowercase `x` above the baseline, in pixels at `font_size`.
doc_texts.fn:ForegroundExecutor::block_on:
Blocks the current thread until `future` completes, and returns its output.

Prefer [`ForegroundExecutor::block_with_timeout`], which gives up instead of
waiting indefinitely.
doc_texts.fn:ForegroundExecutor::block_test:
Runs `future` on the main thread until it completes, and returns its output. Only
available in tests.

If the future is waiting and no other test work can run, the simulated clock
moves to the next timer.

# Panics

Panics if `future` is waiting, no timer is pending, and parking isn't allowed.
doc_texts.fn:ForegroundExecutor::dispatcher:
Returns the platform dispatcher this executor sends work through. GPUI uses this
internally.
doc_texts.fn:ForegroundExecutor::idle_time_remaini:
Returns how much of the current idle slice is left.

Call it from a future that was spawned with
[`ForegroundExecutor::spawn_when_idle`]. Returns `None` on platforms that don't
meter idle time, and when the call isn't inside an idle slice. In that case,
fall back to a budget of your own.
doc_texts.fn:ForegroundExecutor::new:
Creates an executor that runs futures on the main thread through `dispatcher`.

Platform code creates the executor. Apps get one from
[`App::foreground_executor`] or [`crate::AsyncApp::foreground_executor`].
doc_texts.fn:ForegroundExecutor::retirement_handle:
Returns the platform retirement barrier when the dispatcher opted into
owner-thread task retirement.
doc_texts.fn:ForegroundExecutor::scheduler_executo: Returns the scheduler's local executor, for code that takes one directly.
doc_texts.fn:ForegroundExecutor::spawn_when_idle:
Runs `future` on the main thread when the platform is idle.

Use this for low-priority UI work that can wait. `timeout` sets how long the
future may wait. `None` lets it wait as long as the platform stays busy. With a
timeout, a poll that is still waiting after that long runs as ordinary main-thread
work. On platforms without idle scheduling the future runs at low priority, and
`timeout` is ignored.

Each poll uses part of one idle slice. Long synchronous stretches should check
[`ForegroundExecutor::idle_time_remaining`] and yield when it runs low.
doc_texts.fn:ForegroundExecutor::spawn_with_priori:
Like [`ForegroundExecutor::spawn`]. The priority is ignored: foreground futures run
in the order they were spawned.
doc_texts.fn:ForegroundTaskRetirement::begin: Latches retirement and wakes every tracked local task.
doc_texts.fn:ForegroundTaskRetirement::drain_once: Drains one batch of accepted/cancellation runnables on the owner thread.
doc_texts.fn:ForegroundTaskRetirement::try_finish:
Finishes the scope once its queues and tracked futures are quiescent.

Returns false while another owner-thread drain is required.
doc_texts.fn:FunctionReflection::invoke:
Calls the method on `value` and returns its result.

# Panics

Panics if the method returns a value that isn't a `T`. Generated reflections
always return `T`, so this indicates a bug in the generated code.
doc_texts.fn:GlyphRenderMode::rasterized_format: Returns the byte format required for this render mode.
doc_texts.fn:GraphicalEnvironment::apply_to:
Sets this environment's display variables on `command`, and removes the ones it doesn't
set, so the program connects to this graphical session rather than the one this process
started in. Leaves `XDG_ACTIVATION_TOKEN` alone.
doc_texts.fn:GraphicalEnvironment::detect:
Reads the display variables from this process's environment.

This only reads environment variables: whether they name a reachable display server is
checked when a platform connects. Leaves `activation_token` unset: see its documentation.
doc_texts.fn:GraphicalEnvironment::guess_composito:
Returns the compositor this environment selects: Wayland, then X11, then headless.

Does not attempt to connect to the compositor.
doc_texts.fn:HeadlessAppContext::advance_clock: Moves the simulated clock forward by `duration`, and runs the tasks that become ready.
doc_texts.fn:HeadlessAppContext::allow_parking:
Lets blocking waits in the scheduler sleep in real time, for tests that wait on real I/O.

Pair it with [`HeadlessAppContext::forbid_parking`]. See
[`BackgroundExecutor::allow_parking`](crate::BackgroundExecutor::allow_parking).
doc_texts.fn:HeadlessAppContext::capture_screensho:
Renders `window`'s last painted frame to an image.

# Errors

Returns an error if the context was created without a renderer, which is the
case for [`HeadlessAppContext::new`] and [`HeadlessAppContext::with_asset_source`].
Also returns an error if the window has been closed.
doc_texts.fn:HeadlessAppContext::debug_bounds:
Returns the bounds of the element with `debug_selector(selector)` in the last painted frame, or `None`.

# Errors

Returns an error if `window` has been closed.
doc_texts.fn:HeadlessAppContext::forbid_parking: Turns off the parking mode from [`HeadlessAppContext::allow_parking`], returning to deterministic execution.
doc_texts.fn:HeadlessAppContext::glyph_bounds:
Returns the device-pixel bounds of each monochrome glyph painted in `color` in the last painted frame.

The color must match exactly.

# Errors

Returns an error if `window` has been closed.
doc_texts.fn:HeadlessAppContext::new:
Creates a headless context that measures text with `platform_text_system`.

It has no asset source and no renderer, so [`HeadlessAppContext::capture_screenshot`]
returns an error. Use [`HeadlessAppContext::with_platform`] for screenshots.
doc_texts.fn:HeadlessAppContext::open_window:
Opens a hidden, unfocused window of `size` at the origin, with a root view from `build_root`.

# Errors

Returns an error if the window can't be opened.
doc_texts.fn:HeadlessAppContext::run_until_parked: Runs pending tasks until none can make progress. This doesn't move the simulated clock.
doc_texts.fn:HeadlessAppContext::solid_quad_bounds:
Returns the device-pixel bounds of each solid quad in `color` in the last painted frame.

The color must match exactly. Quads with other colors are skipped.

# Errors

Returns an error if `window` has been closed.
doc_texts.fn:HeadlessAppContext::underline_bounds:
Returns the device-pixel bounds of each underline painted in `color` in the last painted frame.

The color must match exactly.

# Errors

Returns an error if `window` has been closed.
doc_texts.fn:HeadlessAppContext::update: Runs `f` with mutable access to the [`App`]. This doesn't run pending tasks.
doc_texts.fn:HeadlessAppContext::update_window:
Runs `f` with the window's root view, the [`Window`] and the [`App`].

This doesn't paint the window. Methods that read painted output, such as
[`HeadlessAppContext::debug_bounds`], see the last frame that was painted.

# Errors

Returns an error if `window` has been closed.
doc_texts.fn:HeadlessAppContext::with_asset_source: Creates a headless context with `platform_text_system` and `asset_source`, and no renderer.
doc_texts.fn:HeadlessAppContext::with_platform:
Creates a headless context with a text system, an asset source and a renderer factory.

`renderer_factory` creates the renderer that windows draw with. Return `None`
from it to draw without a renderer, which disables screenshots. The scheduler seed
is read from `SEED`, and is `0` when it's unset or isn't a number.
doc_texts.fn:HighlightStyle::color: Creates a highlight style with a foreground color.
doc_texts.fn:HighlightStyle::highlight:
Blend this highlight style with another.
Non-continuous properties, like font_weight and font_style, are overwritten.
doc_texts.fn:HitTest::entry: Returns the metadata of a hitbox in this frame, whether or not it is under the mouse.
doc_texts.fn:HitTest::iter_hovered:
Returns the hitboxes that receive hover and mouse input, front to back.

The list stops at the first hitbox whose behavior blocks the mouse, which
is included as the last item. Hitboxes behind it are not hovered.
doc_texts.fn:HitTest::iter_scrollable:
Returns the hitboxes that receive scroll events, front to back.

The list runs past hitboxes with [`HitboxBehavior::BlockMouseExceptScroll`],
and stops after the first one with [`HitboxBehavior::BlockMouse`], which is
included as the last item.
doc_texts.fn:HitTestEntry::depth:
