Returns the width of the line in logical pixels.

This is the glyph advance width from the text shaping system. Use it to
advance a "pen" when you paint several lines or fragments on one row.
doc_texts.fn:ShapedText::len: Returns the length of the text in UTF-8 bytes.
doc_texts.fn:ShapedText::paint:
Paints the glyphs and decorations of every visual line.

`origin` is the top-left corner of the first line. Each following line
starts `line_height` below the previous one. `bounds` supplies the width
used for alignment; when it is `None`, the layout's wrap width is used.
See [`ShapedLine::paint`] for how the arguments place the text.

# Errors

Returns an error only if the window's paint layer fails. A glyph that
fails to paint is logged and skipped.
doc_texts.fn:ShapedText::paint_background:
Paints the background colors of every visual line before the foreground.
The arguments have the same meaning as [`ShapedText::paint`].
doc_texts.fn:ShapedTextLayout::adjacent_visual_car:
Returns the next caret stop to the left or right of `caret` on screen.

Returns `None` when there is no caret stop in that direction.
doc_texts.fn:ShapedTextLayout::ascent: Returns the distance from the baseline up to the tallest glyphs.
doc_texts.fn:ShapedTextLayout::byte_index_for_pixe:
The UTF-8 byte index for a point in GPUI layout coordinates.

The backend returns the logical start of the visual cluster under the point.
Whitespace is hit like any other cluster. Positions outside the line return the boundary at
that visual edge in `Err`.

See also [`Self::closest_byte_index_for_pixel_point`].
doc_texts.fn:ShapedTextLayout::caret_movement:
Returns where the caret lands after `movement`, without changing any state.

Pass the `vertical_navigation_x` from the previous move to keep the caret's column
across consecutive up or down moves. The result carries the new value.
doc_texts.fn:ShapedTextLayout::closest_byte_index_:
Returns the UTF-8 byte index of the cluster boundary closest to a point.

Use this for a click or drag that should always land on the nearest character,
even when the point is outside the text. For right-to-left clusters, the visual
left edge maps to the logical end and the visual right edge maps to the logical
start. Zero-width clusters share a stop with an adjacent cluster, and visual order
breaks the tie.

# Errors

Returns `Err` with the index when the point is outside a visual line, and `Ok`
otherwise. Both cases give an index, so use either value.
doc_texts.fn:ShapedTextLayout::closest_caret_for_p:
Returns the closest backend-native caret for a point in GPUI layout coordinates.

Returns `Err` with the caret at that edge when the point is outside a visual line,
the same way as [`Self::closest_byte_index_for_pixel_point`].
doc_texts.fn:ShapedTextLayout::descent: Returns the distance from the baseline down to the lowest glyphs.
doc_texts.fn:ShapedTextLayout::font_size: Returns the base font size that the text was shaped at, in logical pixels.
doc_texts.fn:ShapedTextLayout::fragments_for_line: Returns the fragments belonging to a visual line.
doc_texts.fn:ShapedTextLayout::len: Returns the length of the text in UTF-8 bytes.
doc_texts.fn:ShapedTextLayout::line_count: Returns the number of visual lines in this layout.
doc_texts.fn:ShapedTextLayout::logical_cluster_aft: Returns the byte range of the cluster after `caret` in logical order.
doc_texts.fn:ShapedTextLayout::logical_cluster_bef: Returns the byte range of the cluster before `caret` in logical order.
doc_texts.fn:ShapedTextLayout::normalized_caret: Moves a caret onto a valid cluster boundary, keeping its affinity when it can.
doc_texts.fn:ShapedTextLayout::selection_bounds: Returns rectangles covering all selected clusters in visual order.
doc_texts.fn:ShapedTextLayout::selection_from_pixe: Selects the word or line at a point in GPUI layout coordinates.
doc_texts.fn:ShapedTextLayout::selection_movement:
Returns where a selection lands after `movement`, using visual order.

Without `extend`, a left or right cluster or word move on a non-empty selection collapses
it to the visual edge in that direction. Other moves start from the caret. With `extend`, the
anchor stays fixed and the caret moves.

- `selection` is the current anchor and caret.
- `movement` gives the direction and the unit.
- `extend` keeps the anchor fixed when `true`, and collapses the selection when `false`.
- `vertical_navigation_x` carries the column across vertical moves.
- `line_height` converts caret positions into comparable visual coordinates.
doc_texts.fn:ShapedTextLayout::size: Returns the size of the whole layout, with each line `line_height` tall.
doc_texts.fn:ShapedTextLayout::visual_lines: Returns the visual lines in paint order.
doc_texts.fn:ShapedTextLayout::visual_position_for:
Returns the top-left corner of the caret for a UTF-8 byte index, or `None` if the index is past the end.

The position is on the cluster boundary, at the visual edge that matches the text direction.
An index inside an atomic cluster snaps to the start of that cluster. On a soft-wrap
boundary, the index places the caret at the start of the following visual line.
Returns the top-left corner of the caret for `caret`, or `None` if the caret has no position.
doc_texts.fn:ShapedTextLayout::width: Returns the width of the widest line, capped at the wrap width.
doc_texts.fn:SpringAnimation::from:
Sets the value a newly mounted spring starts from.

Without this, a new spring starts at its target and doesn't animate on mount. The value is
converted with [`SpringTarget::target`], so it must be the same kind of value as the target.
doc_texts.fn:SpringAnimation::new:
Creates a spring animation with `config`, which has no target yet.

Call [`to`](Self::to) to set the target before passing the animation to an element.
doc_texts.fn:SpringAnimation::playback:
Sets how the spring advances, and where it rests, when its animation changes state.

See [`SpringPlayback`].
doc_texts.fn:SpringAnimation::to:
Sets the target of this spring.

An `f32` targets a number, a [`Pixels`](crate::Pixels) or [`Rems`](crate::Rems) targets a
length, a `bool` targets `0.0` or `1.0`, and an [`AnimationPhase`] targets a phase.
The animator receives the target's [`SpringTarget::Output`].
doc_texts.fn:SpringAnimation::with_epsilon:
Sets how close the spring must be to its target before it counts as settled.

The tolerance is in the target's scalar coordinate. For a [`Pixels`](crate::Pixels) target,
it is in pixels. See [`Motion::with_epsilon`](crate::Motion::with_epsilon).
doc_texts.fn:SpringAnimationElement::map_element:
Applies `f` to the element being animated, and returns the animation with the result.

The spring's animator still runs on the element that `f` returns.
doc_texts.fn:SpringConfig::canonical:
Returns the natural angular frequency $\omega_0$ and the damping ratio $\zeta$.

A ratio below one describes an underdamped spring, which oscillates about its target.
One is critical damping; above one is overdamping. For a displaced spring released from
rest, critical damping gives the fastest approach to a fixed target without oscillation.
A spring that already has velocity can cross the target even with critical damping.
doc_texts.fn:SpringConfig::new: Creates a spring from its stiffness, damping and mass. See [`spring`].
doc_texts.fn:Style::effective_unicode_bidi: Resolves the initial Unicode bidi behavior against this style's direction.
doc_texts.fn:Style::has_opaque_background: Returns true if the style has a background that is not fully transparent. Visibility is not checked.
doc_texts.fn:Style::overflow_mask:
Get the content mask for this element style, based on the given bounds.
If the element does not hide its overflow, this will return `None`.
doc_texts.fn:Style::paint: Paints the background of an element styled with this style.
doc_texts.fn:Style::scroll_mask:
Get the content mask for a container that always clips and scrolls
vertically, like [`List`](crate::List) and
[`UniformList`](crate::UniformList): the vertical axis always clips,
the horizontal axis clips according to `overflow.x`, and
`overflow_fade` distances apply on each clipped axis.
doc_texts.fn:Style::text_style: Get the text style in this element style.
doc_texts.fn:StyledText::layout:
Returns the layout of this element, for mapping between byte indices and pixels.

The layout is filled in while the element is laid out and prepainted. Its query
methods panic if called before that, so call them from event handlers or after
the frame has been drawn. [`TextLayout`] is cheap to clone and shares its state.
doc_texts.fn:StyledText::new:
Creates a styled text element for `text`, with no styling beyond the inherited text style.

Add styling with [`StyledText::with_highlights`], [`StyledText::with_default_highlights`],
[`StyledText::with_runs`], or [`StyledText::with_font_family_overrides`].
doc_texts.fn:StyledText::with_default_highlights:
Styles the text with `default_style`, with `highlights` applied over it.

The runs are computed now, from `default_style`. Use this when you have a
[`TextStyle`] in hand. Otherwise use [`StyledText::with_highlights`], which
takes the inherited style at layout time.

Each range must lie on character boundaries inside the text. The ranges must
be sorted by start and must not overlap.

# Panics

Panics in debug builds if a range is outside the text, or if this element
already has highlights from [`StyledText::with_highlights`].
doc_texts.fn:StyledText::with_font_family_override:
Sets the font family for byte ranges of the text.

The family is applied at layout time, on top of the inherited style. An
override changes the family of a run only when that run lies entirely
inside the override's range. Runs are split only at highlight boundaries,
so to make an override cover part of the text, add a highlight at each
edge of the range. Can be combined with [`with_highlights`](Self::with_highlights).

The overrides must be sorted by range start and non-overlapping.
Each override range must fall on character boundaries.
doc_texts.fn:StyledText::with_runs:
Sets the runs that style the text. Each run gives its byte length and its [`TextRun`].

The run lengths must add up to the length of the text exactly, and each run
must end on a character boundary.

# Panics

Panics if the runs don't cover the text exactly, or if a run ends inside a
character. In debug builds the message includes the text and the run.
doc_texts.fn:Subscription::detach:
Forgets the cancellation handle and leaves the callback registered.

A callback created by GPUI may still remove itself when an entity it depends on is released.
Detaching does not run the `unsubscribe` callback supplied to [`Subscription::new`].
doc_texts.fn:Subscription::join:
Combines two subscriptions into one cancellation handle.

Dropping the result cancels both subscriptions. Calling [`Subscription::detach`] on the result
detaches both.
doc_texts.fn:Surface::object_fit: Sets how the frame is scaled to the element's bounds.
doc_texts.fn:Svg::data:
Sets the SVG from bytes that are already in memory, such as one included with `include_bytes!`.

The bytes are copied into the element. The rasterized icon is cached under a hash of the
bytes, so the same data is rasterized once. Calling this again replaces the bytes. When
several sources are set, this one wins.
doc_texts.fn:SvgRenderer::new:
Creates a renderer that loads fonts and files from `asset_registry`.

[`crate::Application::with_assets`] creates one for you. System fonts are scanned once per process,
the first time a font is needed.
doc_texts.fn:SvgRenderer::parse_svg:
Parses SVG bytes into a [`ParsedSvg`], which can then be rasterized at any size.

# Errors

Returns a `usvg::Error` if `bytes` is not a valid SVG document.
doc_texts.fn:SvgRenderer::render_parsed:
Rasterizes a parsed SVG at `size` into a [`RenderImage`].

A scale-factor size is drawn at [`SMOOTH_SVG_SCALE_FACTOR`] times the requested size, and the
image is marked so that it displays at the logical size. `Size` and `ExactSize` use device
pixels and are not scaled further. A result larger than 8192 pixels on either side is scaled
down to fit.

# Errors

Returns a `usvg::Error` if the rasterized size is zero, such as for a zero requested size.
doc_texts.fn:SystemWindowTab::new: Creates a tab for a window, with its current time as the last-active time.
doc_texts.fn:SystemWindowTabController::add_tab:
Adds the window `id` to the group that holds the other tabs in `tabs`.

If no existing group holds exactly the other tabs, `tabs` becomes a new group.
Does nothing if `tabs` does not contain `id`.
doc_texts.fn:SystemWindowTabController::get_next_t:
Returns the handle of the window in the tab group that follows the group containing `id`
in the iteration order of `tab_groups`. That order is arbitrary.

The window chosen is the most recently active tab in that group. Returns `None`
if `id` is not in a group.
doc_texts.fn:SystemWindowTabController::get_prev_t:
Returns the handle of the window in the tab group that precedes the group containing `id`
in the iteration order of `tab_groups`. That order is arbitrary.

The window chosen is the most recently active tab in that group. Returns `None`
if `id` is not in a group.
doc_texts.fn:SystemWindowTabController::init: Sets the global [`SystemWindowTabController`] to a new, empty controller.
doc_texts.fn:SystemWindowTabController::init_visib: Sets tab visibility to `visible`, but only if it has not been set yet.
doc_texts.fn:SystemWindowTabController::is_visible: Returns whether window tabs are shown. Defaults to `false` until set.
doc_texts.fn:SystemWindowTabController::merge_all_: Merges every tab group into one group, starting with the group that holds `id`.
doc_texts.fn:SystemWindowTabController::move_tab_t: Moves the tab for window `id` out of its group into a new group of its own.
doc_texts.fn:SystemWindowTabController::new: Creates an empty controller with no tab groups and tabs hidden.
doc_texts.fn:SystemWindowTabController::remove_tab:
Removes the tab for window `id` from its group and returns it.

A group that becomes empty is removed. Returns `None` if `id` is in no group.
doc_texts.fn:SystemWindowTabController::select_nex: Activates the tab after window `id`'s tab in its group, wrapping around at the end.
doc_texts.fn:SystemWindowTabController::select_pre: Activates the tab before window `id`'s tab in its group, wrapping around at the start.
doc_texts.fn:SystemWindowTabController::set_visibl: Shows or hides window tabs.
doc_texts.fn:SystemWindowTabController::tab_groups: Returns every tab group, keyed by group ID.
doc_texts.fn:SystemWindowTabController::tabs: Returns the tabs in the group that contains the window `id`, or `None` if it has none.
doc_texts.fn:SystemWindowTabController::update_las: Records that the window `id` is now the active tab, for ordering tab groups.
doc_texts.fn:SystemWindowTabController::update_tab:
Moves the tab for window `id` to index `ix` within its group.

Does nothing if `ix` is out of range or the tab is already there.
Sets the title of the tab for window `id`. Does nothing if the title is unchanged.
doc_texts.fn:TestApp::advance_clock:
Moves the simulated clock forward by `duration`.

Tasks that become ready run during the call, including timers that expire
within the window. Use this to test timeouts and delays, as in the example for
[`TestApp::run_until_parked`].
doc_texts.fn:TestApp::background_spawn:
Spawns a `Send` future on the background executor.

Like [`TestApp::spawn`], the future runs when the app runs tasks.
doc_texts.fn:TestApp::did_prompt_for_new_path:
Returns whether a [`App::prompt_for_new_path`] request is waiting for an answer.

Answer it with [`TestApp::simulate_new_path_selection`].
doc_texts.fn:TestApp::has_global: Returns whether a global of type `G` is set.
doc_texts.fn:TestApp::has_pending_prompt: Returns whether a prompt from [`Window::prompt`] is waiting for an answer.
doc_texts.fn:TestApp::new:
Creates a test app with scheduler seed `0`.

Text is shaped by the test text system, not by real fonts. Use
[`TestApp::with_text_system`] when a test measures real glyphs.
doc_texts.fn:TestApp::new_entity:
Creates an entity from `build` and runs pending tasks until parked.

This is `cx.new(build)` inside [`TestApp::update`].
doc_texts.fn:TestApp::open_window:
Opens a window sized to the test display and returns a [`TestAppWindow`] for its root view.

The window's bounds are the maximized bounds of the test display. Use
[`TestApp::open_window_with_options`] to choose other bounds.

# Panics

Panics if the window can't be opened.
doc_texts.fn:TestApp::open_window_with_options:
Opens a window with `options` and returns a [`TestAppWindow`] for its root view.

# Panics

Panics if the window can't be opened.
doc_texts.fn:TestApp::read:
Runs `f` with read-only access to the [`App`].

This doesn't run pending tasks. A task that is still waiting to run doesn't
run before `f` is called.
doc_texts.fn:TestApp::read_entity: Reads an entity without running pending tasks.
doc_texts.fn:TestApp::read_from_clipboard: Returns the item most recently written to the test clipboard, or `None` if nothing was written.
doc_texts.fn:TestApp::read_global:
Runs `f` with the global of type `G`.

# Panics

Panics if no global of type `G` is set. Check with [`TestApp::has_global`] first.
doc_texts.fn:TestApp::set_global: Sets the global of type `G`, replacing any previous value, then runs pending tasks.
doc_texts.fn:TestApp::simulate_new_path_selection:
Answers the oldest pending [`App::prompt_for_new_path`] request.

`select` receives the directory the app asked about and returns the chosen
path, or `None` to cancel the request.

# Panics

Panics if no new-path request is pending.
doc_texts.fn:TestApp::simulate_prompt_answer:
Answers the oldest pending prompt by pressing the button labelled `button`.

The prompt is removed before the label is checked, so a wrong label still
consumes it.

# Panics

Panics if no prompt is pending, or if no button has the label `button`.
doc_texts.fn:TestApp::spawn:
Spawns a future on the foreground executor, given an [`AsyncApp`] for this app.

The future runs when the app runs tasks: during [`TestApp::run_until_parked`],
[`TestApp::advance_clock`] or the next `update`. Await, store or detach the
returned [`Task`], as in a real app. See [async work](crate::_documentation::guides::async_work).
doc_texts.fn:TestApp::text_system: Returns the text system the app uses to shape and measure text.
doc_texts.fn:TestApp::to_async:
Returns an [`AsyncApp`] for this app.

The handle holds a weak reference, so it can't keep the app alive.
doc_texts.fn:TestApp::update_entity: Updates an entity and runs pending tasks until parked.
doc_texts.fn:TestApp::update_global:
Runs `f` with mutable access to the global of type `G`, then runs pending tasks.

# Panics

Panics if no global of type `G` is set.
doc_texts.fn:TestApp::windows: Returns the handles of all open windows.
doc_texts.fn:TestApp::with_seed:
Creates a test app whose scheduler orders ready tasks by `seed`.

The seed decides which ready task runs first. The same seed gives the same
order every time, so a failing seed can be replayed.
doc_texts.fn:TestApp::with_text_system:
Creates a test app that shapes text with `text_system`. Uses seed `0`.

Pass a real text system to measure glyphs as the app would on a platform.
doc_texts.fn:TestApp::with_text_system_and_assets:
Creates a test app with the given text system and asset source.

This is [`TestApp::with_text_system`] plus an [`AssetSource`](crate::AssetSource),
so views can load icons and other assets. Uses seed `0`.
doc_texts.fn:TestApp::write_to_clipboard:
Writes `item` to the test clipboard.

[`TestApp::read_from_clipboard`] returns the item until something else is written.
doc_texts.fn:TestAppContext::active_idle_sleep_pre: Returns the number of active idle sleep prevention tokens.
doc_texts.fn:TestAppContext::add_empty_window:
Opens a window with an empty root view and returns a [`VisualTestContext`] for it.

Runs pending tasks before it returns.
doc_texts.fn:TestAppContext::add_window:
Opens a window with maximized bounds and returns its handle.

The window is backed by a test platform window, so input and resize helpers
work on it. This doesn't run pending tasks.

# Panics

Panics if the window can't be opened.
doc_texts.fn:TestAppContext::add_window_view:
Opens a window whose root view `build_root_view` builds.

Returns the root view's entity and a [`VisualTestContext`] for the window. Use
the returned context from then on, which is the usual pattern:
`let (view, cx) = cx.add_window_view(...);`. Runs pending tasks before it returns.
See [testing a window](crate::_documentation::guides::testing) for an example.
doc_texts.fn:TestAppContext::app_identity: Returns the identifier and name set with `set_app_identity`, or `None` if none was set.
doc_texts.fn:TestAppContext::build:
Creates a context that runs on `dispatcher`.

`#[gpui::test]` calls this for you.
doc_texts.fn:TestAppContext::build_with_text_syste: Creates a test context backed by the provided platform text system.
doc_texts.fn:TestAppContext::condition:
Waits until `predicate` returns `true` for `entity`, checking after each notification.

# Panics

Panics if the predicate isn't true within 3 seconds of simulated time, or if
the entity is released while waiting.
doc_texts.fn:TestAppContext::cursor_style: Returns the cursor most recently applied to the test platform.
doc_texts.fn:TestAppContext::delivered_system_noti:
Returns the notifications that are shown and not yet dismissed.

A notification with the same tag as an earlier one replaces it.
doc_texts.fn:TestAppContext::did_prompt_for_new_pa: Returns whether a new-path prompt is waiting for [`TestAppContext::simulate_new_path_selection`].
doc_texts.fn:TestAppContext::did_prompt_for_paths: Returns whether a `prompt_for_paths` request is waiting for [`TestAppContext::simulate_path_prompt_response`].
doc_texts.fn:TestAppContext::disable_accessibility: Disables accessibility for subsequently created test windows.
doc_texts.fn:TestAppContext::dismissed_system_noti: Returns the tags of the notifications dismissed during the test, in order.
doc_texts.fn:TestAppContext::dispatch_action:
Dispatches `action` to the focused element in `window`, then runs pending tasks.

# Panics

Panics if `window` has been closed.
doc_texts.fn:TestAppContext::dispatch_keystroke:
Dispatches one keystroke to the focused element in `window`.

This doesn't run pending tasks. [`TestAppContext::simulate_keystrokes`] does.
doc_texts.fn:TestAppContext::events: Returns a stream of the events `entity` emits, cloned, in order.
doc_texts.fn:TestAppContext::executor: Returns a clone of the background executor.
doc_texts.fn:TestAppContext::expect_restart:
Returns a receiver that gets the path and arguments of the next restart request.

The app doesn't restart in a test. Calling this again replaces the previous
sender, so the previous receiver is cancelled.
doc_texts.fn:TestAppContext::foreground_executor: Returns the foreground executor.
doc_texts.fn:TestAppContext::has_global: Returns whether a global of type `G` is set.
doc_texts.fn:TestAppContext::has_pending_prompt: Returns whether a prompt is waiting for an answer.
doc_texts.fn:TestAppContext::new_app:
Creates another app that shares this context's scheduler, so tasks from both apps interleave deterministically.

The new app has its own state, windows and globals.
doc_texts.fn:TestAppContext::notifications:
Returns a stream that yields `()` each time `entity` notifies.

The stream ends when the entity is released.
doc_texts.fn:TestAppContext::on_quit: Registers `f` to run when the test ends, before the app shuts down.
doc_texts.fn:TestAppContext::open_window:
Opens a window of `window_size` at the origin and returns its handle.

Use this when a layout test needs a known size. [`TestAppContext::add_window`]
uses the size of the test display instead. This doesn't run pending tasks.

# Panics

Panics if the window can't be opened.
doc_texts.fn:TestAppContext::opened_url:
Returns the URL most recently passed to `open_url`, or `None`.

Only the last URL is kept.
doc_texts.fn:TestAppContext::pending_prompt:
Returns the message and detail of the oldest pending prompt, or `None`.

The detail is an empty string when the prompt has none.
doc_texts.fn:TestAppContext::quit:
Runs the cleanup registered with [`TestAppContext::on_quit`], then shuts the app down.

`#[gpui::test]` calls this when the test ends.
doc_texts.fn:TestAppContext::read: Runs `f` with read-only access to the [`App`].
doc_texts.fn:TestAppContext::read_from_clipboard: Returns the item most recently written to the test clipboard, or `None`.
doc_texts.fn:TestAppContext::read_global:
Runs `read` with the global of type `G`.

# Panics

Panics if no global of type `G` is set. Use [`TestAppContext::try_read_global`] when it might not be.
doc_texts.fn:TestAppContext::refresh: Marks every window for redraw on the next effect cycle. Always returns `Ok(())`.
doc_texts.fn:TestAppContext::run_until_parked:
Runs pending tasks until none can make progress.

This doesn't move the simulated clock. Use `executor().advance_clock` for that.
Timers that haven't expired stay pending.
doc_texts.fn:TestAppContext::set_global: Sets the global of type `G`, replacing any previous value.
doc_texts.fn:TestAppContext::set_idle_sleep_preven: Sets the delay for subsequent idle sleep prevention acquisitions.
Makes subsequent idle sleep prevention acquisitions fail or succeed.
doc_texts.fn:TestAppContext::set_name: Sets this app's name.
doc_texts.fn:TestAppContext::set_screen_capture_so: Sets the sources that screen capture queries return.
doc_texts.fn:TestAppContext::shown_system_notifica:
Returns every system notification shown during the test, in order.

A notification shown before the app has an identity is dropped and doesn't
appear here.
doc_texts.fn:TestAppContext::simulate_display_refr: Simulates a connected display changing its refresh interval.
doc_texts.fn:TestAppContext::simulate_input:
Types `input` into `window` by sending one keystroke per character, then runs pending tasks.

Each character is parsed as a keystroke, so the text reaches text inputs. A
space is sent with the key `" "`, not `"space"`.

Splitting on an empty string also sends an empty keystroke before the first
character and after the last. Don't rely on those.
doc_texts.fn:TestAppContext::simulate_keystrokes:
Sends each keystroke in a space-separated list to `window`, then runs pending tasks.

Each part is parsed as in [`TestAppWindow::simulate_keystroke`](crate::TestAppWindow::simulate_keystroke).
The space bar is the key `"space"`, which can't appear in this list, because
a space separates keystrokes. Two spaces in a row send an empty keystroke.

# Panics

Panics if any part isn't a valid keystroke.
doc_texts.fn:TestAppContext::simulate_new_path_sel:
Answers the oldest pending new-path prompt.

`select_path` receives the directory the app asked about and returns the chosen
path, or `None` to cancel.

# Panics

Panics if no new-path prompt is pending.
doc_texts.fn:TestAppContext::simulate_path_prompt_:
Answers the oldest pending `prompt_for_paths` request.

`select_paths` receives the prompt's options and returns the chosen paths, or
`None` to cancel.

# Panics

Panics if no paths prompt is pending. Also panics if `select_paths` returns more
than one path for a prompt that doesn't allow multiple selection.
doc_texts.fn:TestAppContext::simulate_prompt_answe:
Presses the button labelled `button` on the oldest pending prompt.

# Panics

Panics if no prompt is pending, or if no button on the prompt has the label `button`.

The future runs when tasks run, such as during [`TestAppContext::run_until_parked`]
or a `simulate_*` method. A plain `update` doesn't run it.

Makes this the active window, as if the user had clicked it, then runs pending tasks.

Windows that [`TestApp`] opens start inactive. Focus listeners such as
[`Context::on_focus`] only run in the active window, so activate it before testing them.
doc_texts.fn:TestAppWindow::draw:
Paints the window now, so that later input and hit tests use the current layout.

Call this after building the view and after anything changes its layout, before
simulating a click at a position. It doesn't run pending tasks. See the example
on [`TestApp`].

# Panics

Panics if the window has been closed.

Returns the root view's entity.

# Panics

Panics if the window has been closed.
doc_texts.fn:TestAppWindow::simulate_click:
Presses and releases `button` at `position`, then runs pending tasks.

Both events have a click count of `1`, so calling this twice in a row sends two
single clicks, never a double click. Call [`TestAppWindow::draw`] first, so
the click hits the element you expect. See the example on [`TestApp`].
doc_texts.fn:TestAppWindow::simulate_event:
Dispatches `event` to the window as platform input, then runs pending tasks.

Use this for input events that have no dedicated method on [`TestAppWindow`].
doc_texts.fn:TestAppWindow::simulate_mouse_down:
Presses `button` at `position`, then runs pending tasks.

The click count is always `1`, so this never sends a double click.
doc_texts.fn:TestAppWindow::simulate_mouse_move: Moves the pointer to `position` with no button held, then runs pending tasks.
doc_texts.fn:TestAppWindow::simulate_mouse_up:
Releases `button` at `position`, then runs pending tasks.

The click count is always `1`.
doc_texts.fn:TestAppWindow::simulate_resize:
Sets the window's size to `size`, then runs pending tasks.

This runs the window's resize callback, if it has one, and updates the viewport that
`Window::viewport_size` reports. It doesn't paint the window: call
[`TestAppWindow::draw`] to paint at the new size.
doc_texts.fn:TestAppWindow::simulate_scale_factor_: Simulate the window moving to a display with a different scale factor.
doc_texts.fn:TestAppWindow::simulate_scroll:
Scrolls by `delta`, in pixels, with the pointer at `position`, then runs pending tasks.

No modifier keys are held.
doc_texts.fn:TestAppWindow::update:
Runs `f` with the root view, its [`Window`] and a [`Context`], then runs pending tasks until parked.

Panics if the window has been closed.
doc_texts.fn:Text::new:
Create a new [`Text`] element with a specific ID.

If you want a unique ID to be assigned automatically, use the [`text!`](crate::text!)
macro. The docs for [`Text`] have more detail about choosing IDs.
doc_texts.fn:Text::new_inaccessible:
Create a new [`Text`] element that is inaccessible to screen readers.

Text without an id has no accessibility node. Use [`text!`](crate::text!) for a generated
id or [`Text::new`] to choose one.

Use it for decorative text or text whose parent supplies the accessible representation.
doc_texts.fn:Text::text: The text that this [`Text`] element will display.
doc_texts.fn:Text::with_id: Produce a new [`Text`] with the given `id`.
doc_texts.fn:TextDirection::with_boundary: Returns a [`TextMovement`] in this direction that stops at `boundary`.
doc_texts.fn:TextLayout::apply_truncation:
Shortens `text` so that it fits `truncation.width`, and returns the text to display.

When `truncation.width` is `None`, the text and runs come back unchanged. Otherwise
the removed part is replaced by `truncation.affix`, on the side given by
`truncation.source`. Wrapping and `line_clamp` from `text_style` still apply.
The returned runs match the returned text. They borrow `runs` when nothing changes.
doc_texts.fn:TextLayout::bounds:
Returns the window bounds of the element, as set during prepaint.

# Panics

Panics if the element hasn't been prepainted.
doc_texts.fn:TextLayout::evaluate_alignment_width:
Returns the width that text aligns within, from the known or available width.

The known width wins. Otherwise a definite available width is used. Under
min-content or max-content sizing, this returns `None`.
doc_texts.fn:TextLayout::evaluate_overflow:
Returns how the text should be truncated, from the style's `text_overflow`.

When the style has no `text_overflow`, the result has no width and an empty affix,
so the text is never truncated.
doc_texts.fn:TextLayout::evaluate_wrap_width:
Returns the width that text wraps at, or `None` when it doesn't wrap.

Text does not wrap when `white_space` is [`WhiteSpace::Nowrap`]. Otherwise
the width comes from [`TextLayout::evaluate_alignment_width`].
doc_texts.fn:TextLayout::index_for_position:
Returns the UTF-8 byte index of the character at `pixel_point`, in window coordinates.

Returns `Ok` with the index of the character under the point. Returns `Err`
with `0` when the point is above the text. Points to the side of or below the
text return `Err` with the closest index. Use this for hit testing, such as
placing a caret on click.

# Panics

Panics if the element hasn't been laid out or prepainted.
doc_texts.fn:TextLayout::len:
Returns the length of the shaped text in UTF-8 bytes.

This is the length after any text transform or truncation. It is `0`
when the text has not been shaped.

# Panics

Panics if the element hasn't been laid out.
doc_texts.fn:TextLayout::line_height:
Returns the line height that the text is laid out with, in logical pixels.

# Panics

Panics if the element hasn't been laid out.
doc_texts.fn:TextLayout::line_layout_for_index:
Returns the shaped layout of the text, or `None` if `index` is past the end or the
text has not been shaped.

The layout covers the whole text, not one visual line or paragraph.
Use [`TextLayout::line_layouts`] to get every layout in source order.

# Panics

Panics if the element hasn't been laid out.
doc_texts.fn:TextLayout::line_layouts:
Returns the shaped layout of the text as a collection with one entry.

This returns an empty collection if the text has not been shaped.

# Panics

Panics if the element hasn't been laid out.
doc_texts.fn:TextLayout::paint_background:
Paints the backgrounds of the text runs without the glyphs, so callers can paint
content such as highlights between the backgrounds and text.
doc_texts.fn:TextLayout::paint_foreground: Paints the glyphs and decorations without the run backgrounds.
doc_texts.fn:TextLayout::position_for_index:
Returns the top-left corner of the caret for `byte_index`, in window coordinates.

Returns `None` if the text has no shaped layout, or if `byte_index` is past the end
of the text. Use this to place a caret or an overlay at a position in the text.

# Panics

Panics if the element hasn't been laid out or prepainted.
doc_texts.fn:TextLayout::text:
Returns the text that was shaped, as a `String`.

This is the text after any [`TextTransform`] and truncation. A truncated
text includes the affix, such as an ellipsis. It returns an empty string if
the text has not been shaped.

# Panics

Panics if the element hasn't been laid out.
doc_texts.fn:TextLayout::wrapped_text:
Returns the shaped text with each visual line followed by a `\n`, except the last.

Soft wraps therefore become `\n`. A hard line break keeps its own `\n` as part of
its line, so it is followed by one more `\n`. Use this to copy wrapped text as it
appears on screen.

# Panics

Panics if the element hasn't been laid out.
doc_texts.fn:TextStyle::font: Get the font configured for this text style.
doc_texts.fn:TextStyle::highlight: Create a new text style with the given highlighting applied.
doc_texts.fn:TextStyle::line_height_in_pixels: Returns the rounded line height in pixels.
doc_texts.fn:TextStyle::to_run: Convert this text style into a [`TextRun`], for the given length of the text.
doc_texts.fn:TextSystem::add_fonts:
Registers font files so that [`Font`]s can resolve to them.

Each entry is the bytes of one font file, such as a `.ttf` or `.otf`.
Use `Cow::Borrowed` for bytes compiled into the binary with
`include_bytes!`, and `Cow::Owned` for bytes loaded at runtime. The
family names come from each font's name table, so pass those names to
[`font`](crate::font) or set [`Font::family`] to use them.

The web starts with an empty font database, so add the fonts your
application uses before you open a window.

# Errors

Returns an error if an entry contains no font face that the platform
supports. The parley backend, used on macOS, Windows, Linux, and the web, checks
every entry before it registers any, so a failed call leaves the set of
fonts unchanged.

# Examples

```
# use gpui::TestApp;
# use std::borrow::Cow;
# let mut app = TestApp::new();
let bytes = include_bytes!(concat!(
    env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"),
    "/../../assets/fonts/lilex/Lilex-Regular.ttf"
));
app.text_system()
    .add_fonts(vec![Cow::Borrowed(bytes.as_slice())])
    .expect("Lilex is a valid font");
```

See [text](crate::_documentation::guides::text) for how fonts are chosen.
doc_texts.fn:TextSystem::advance:
Returns the advance of `ch` at `font_size`: how far the pen moves after drawing it.

The `width` of the result is the advance, which is the glyph's horizontal
width in the font, not its ink width. Layout uses it to place the next character.

# Errors

Returns an error if the font has no glyph for `ch`.
doc_texts.fn:TextSystem::all_font_names:
Returns the font family names that this text system can resolve.

Use these names as [`Font::family`] values. On the web, the list contains
only the families registered with [`TextSystem::add_fonts`] and the
`.SystemUIFont` alias, because the web has no system fonts.
doc_texts.fn:TextSystem::ascent: Returns the distance from the baseline up to the top of the font's tallest glyphs, at `font_size`.
doc_texts.fn:TextSystem::baseline_offset:
Returns the distance from the top of a line box of `line_height` to the baseline.

The ascent and descent are centered in the line box, so extra
`line_height` is split evenly above and below the glyphs. Use this to
place text inside a box with a fixed height.
doc_texts.fn:TextSystem::bounding_box:
Returns the font's bounding box at `font_size` in logical pixels.

The bounding box is the smallest rectangle that encloses every glyph in
the font when they are all drawn at the same origin.
doc_texts.fn:TextSystem::descent:
Returns the distance from the baseline down to the bottom of the font's lowest glyphs, at `font_size`.

The value is positive. It is the distance below the baseline, not a
signed coordinate.
doc_texts.fn:TextSystem::new:
Creates a text system that delegates font work to `platform_text_system`.

GPUI creates the text system for each application. You don't need to call this
yourself, except in tests that supply their own platform text system.
doc_texts.fn:TextSystem::prewarm_fonts:
Resolves each font and loads its platform caches ahead of time.

Loading system fonts can be slow, so call this from a background
executor before the first frame that uses the fonts. Fonts that are not
prewarmed are loaded when they are first used.

# Panics

Panics if any font cannot be resolved, as [`TextSystem::resolve_font`] does.
doc_texts.fn:TextSystem::rasterize_glyph:
Rasterizes one glyph to pixels, and checks that the result is well formed.

GPUI calls this when it draws a glyph that is not in the glyph atlas yet.
Application code rarely needs it.

# Errors

Returns an error if the platform cannot rasterize the glyph, or if the
pixel buffer does not match the size and format it reports. See
[`RasterizedGlyph::validate`](crate::RasterizedGlyph::validate).
doc_texts.fn:TextSystem::resolve_font:
Resolves a [`Font`] to the [`FontId`] of the face that will be used to draw it.

Resolution applies the family, weight, style, width, and fallbacks, and
the result is cached. Use the returned id with the metric methods on this
type, such as [`TextSystem::ascent`].

# Panics

Panics if the platform cannot resolve the font. Pass the family name of
a font from [`TextSystem::all_font_names`] or one added with
[`TextSystem::add_fonts`] to avoid this.
doc_texts.fn:TextSystem::typographic_bounds:
Returns the bounding rectangle of the glyph for `character` at `font_size` in logical pixels.

# Errors

Returns an error if the font has no glyph for `character` or the platform
cannot read its bounds.
doc_texts.fn:TextSystem::units_per_em:
Returns the number of font units in the font's em square.

The em square is the grid that font sizes are measured on. Divide a
font-unit measurement by this value to get a fraction of the font size.
doc_texts.fn:TextSystem::x_height: Returns the height of lowercase `x` at `font_size`.
doc_texts.fn:Tiling::is_tiled: Returns `true` if any edge is tiled.
doc_texts.fn:Tiling::tiled: Returns a [`Tiling`] with every edge tiled.
doc_texts.fn:TooltipId::is_hovered: Returns whether the mouse is over the tooltip shown for this id in the last frame.
doc_texts.fn:Transformation::rotate: Creates a transformation that rotates the SVG around its center by `rotate`.
doc_texts.fn:Transformation::scale: Creates a transformation that scales the SVG by `scale` on each axis. `1.0` keeps the size.
doc_texts.fn:Transformation::translate: Creates a transformation that moves the SVG by `translate`, in logical pixels.
doc_texts.fn:TransformationMatrix::apply: Returns `point` transformed by this matrix.
doc_texts.fn:TransformationMatrix::compose:
Returns `self` combined with `other`, so that `other` is applied to points first. This is the
matrix product `self * other`.
doc_texts.fn:TransformationMatrix::rotate:
Returns this transform combined with a clockwise rotation by `angle` around the origin. Clockwise
is on screen, where the y axis points down.
doc_texts.fn:TransformationMatrix::scale: Returns this transform combined with a scale by `size` around the origin.
doc_texts.fn:TransformationMatrix::translate:
Returns this transform combined with a translation by `point`. The translation is applied to
points before this transform.
doc_texts.fn:TransformationMatrix::unit: Returns the identity transform, which leaves points unchanged.
doc_texts.fn:Transition::continuous:
Sets whether a new goal continues from the current value.

Continuous is the default. Pass `false` to restart from the initial value on every goal
change instead.
doc_texts.fn:Transition::entity_id:
Returns the ID of the entity that holds this transition's state.

Use it to tell two transitions apart.
doc_texts.fn:Transition::evaluate:
Returns the value for the current frame, and requests another frame while it moves.

The value depends on the time since the last goal change, and on the easing. The first call
samples the clock and caches the result. Later calls return the cached value until the goal
changes or the cache is cleared, so a `Transition` kept across frames returns the same value.
[`Window::use_keyed_transition`] returns a new `Transition` on every render, which avoids
this. Call this during render or paint.
doc_texts.fn:Transition::evaluate_delta:
Returns the eased progress for the current frame, without requesting another frame.

Progress may overshoot zero through one. It doesn't mean the run has finished: restarting
iterations begin again, and alternating iterations run in reverse.
doc_texts.fn:Transition::jump_to:
Sets the value and the goal to `target`, with no animation.

Later calls to [`evaluate`](Self::evaluate) return `target` until the goal changes again.
Use this when the next animation should start from a different value.
doc_texts.fn:Transition::new:
Creates a transition that stores its state in `state` and animates with `motion`.

Inside render, prefer [`Window::use_keyed_transition`], which creates the state for you.
doc_texts.fn:Transition::read_cache:
Returns the value cached by the last [`evaluate`](Self::evaluate), or `None` if the cache
was cleared.

The cache is cleared when the goal changes, and by [`jump_to`](Self::jump_to),
[`scale_by`](Self::scale_by), [`reset`](Self::reset) and [`with_easing`](Self::with_easing).
doc_texts.fn:Transition::read_goal:
Returns the goal: the value most recently set by [`update`](Self::update).

This isn't the value on screen while the transition moves. Use [`evaluate`](Self::evaluate)
for that.
doc_texts.fn:Transition::reset:
Returns the transition to its initial value, with no animation.

This clears any progress and sets the goal back to the value the transition was created
with. The cache is cleared too.
doc_texts.fn:Transition::scale_by:
Multiplies the start value and the goal by `ratio`.

An in-flight transition keeps its progress when the coordinate space changes, such as a
window resize. Pass the ratio of the new scale to the old one.
doc_texts.fn:Transition::update:
Changes the goal, and starts a run toward the new goal if it changed.

`update` passes the current goal to the closure, which can change it. If the new goal
differs from the old one, the value moves toward it. In continuous mode the run starts from
the current value. Otherwise it starts from the initial value. The goal isn't read during
render, so change it from an event handler.

Returns `true` if the goal changed, and `false` if it stayed the same.

This doesn't notify GPUI. Call `cx.notify()` inside the closure to redraw the view.
doc_texts.fn:Transition::with_easing:
Sets the easing of the forward pass. See [`Motion::with_easing`].

The easing maps normalized pass time to presentation progress. It may be non-monotonic, and
it may overshoot zero through one.
doc_texts.fn:UniformList::track_scroll:
Connects the list to `handle`, so the list reads scroll requests from it and writes its
scroll position to it.

Without this, the list still scrolls with the wheel, but nothing outside it can read or
set the position.
doc_texts.fn:UniformList::with_decoration: Adds a decoration that is drawn over the rows. Decorations are drawn in the order added.
doc_texts.fn:UniformList::with_horizontal_sizing_b:
Sets whether rows can be wider than the list.

With [`ListHorizontalSizingBehavior::FitList`], the default, rows are no wider than the list.
With [`ListHorizontalSizingBehavior::Unconstrained`], the content is as wide as the row
chosen by [`Self::with_width_from_item`], and the list scrolls horizontally when that is
wider than the list.
doc_texts.fn:UniformList::with_sizing_behavior:
Sets how the list sizes itself, like [`List::with_sizing_behavior`](crate::List::with_sizing_behavior).

[`ListSizingBehavior::Auto`], the default, takes the size from the style.
[`ListSizingBehavior::Infer`] makes the list as tall as all its rows, up to the space its
parent gives it.
doc_texts.fn:UniformList::with_width_from_item:
Chooses the row that sets the width and height of every row. `None` measures row 0.

An index past the last row measures the last row. The list measures the chosen row every
frame, so the row should be cheap to render.
doc_texts.fn:UniformList::y_flipped:
Puts item 0 at the bottom of the list, so the first row sits at the bottom and the last at
the top.

The list keeps its scroll position on the same rows when the value changes. This only takes
effect when a handle is set with [`Self::track_scroll`]. Call it after `track_scroll`,
because it reads the handle that `track_scroll` sets.
doc_texts.fn:UniformListScrollHandle::is_scrollabl:
Returns whether the rows are taller than the viewport, as of the last prepaint.

Returns `false` before the first prepaint.
doc_texts.fn:UniformListScrollHandle::is_scrolled_:
Returns whether the list shows its last row, or `None` if the list isn't scrollable.

`None` is also returned before the first prepaint.
doc_texts.fn:UniformListScrollHandle::logical_scro:
Returns the index of the first visible row.

If a scroll request is pending, this returns the row that request targets instead, so the
value is right after a request and one frame later. It is zero before the first prepaint.

Only available with the `test-support` feature, or in GPUI's own tests.
doc_texts.fn:UniformListScrollHandle::new:
Creates a handle that isn't attached to a list yet.

Pass it to [`UniformList::track_scroll`] when you build the list.
doc_texts.fn:UniformListScrollHandle::scroll_to_bo: Scrolls to the last row, as a request for the next prepaint.
doc_texts.fn:UniformListScrollHandle::scroll_to_it:
Places row `ix` where `strategy` says, even when the row is already visible.

Unlike [`Self::scroll_to_item`], this forces the requested placement when the strategy
supports one. With [`ScrollStrategy::Nearest`], a visible row still doesn't move. Use it
when a row must land at a fixed position, such as the top after a keyboard jump. The scroll
takes effect on the next prepaint; see [`Self::scroll_to_item`] for an example.

Places row `ix` like [`Self::scroll_to_item_with_offset`], even when the row is already visible.

The `offset` rules are the same as for [`Self::scroll_to_item_with_offset`].

Scrolls like [`Self::scroll_to_item`], and keeps `offset` rows clear at the top of the viewport.

`offset` shrinks the viewport by that many rows from the top, and `strategy` places the
row in what remains:
- [`ScrollStrategy::Top`] puts the row just below the cleared rows.
- [`ScrollStrategy::Center`] centers the row in the rows below the cleared rows.
- [`ScrollStrategy::Bottom`] places the row at the bottom of the viewport. `offset` affects
  only whether the row counts as already visible, not where it lands.

This is non-strict, so a row that is visible below the cleared rows doesn't move the list.
doc_texts.fn:UniformListScrollHandle::y_flipped:
Returns whether item 0 is at the bottom of the list, as set by [`UniformList::y_flipped`]
on the last frame.
doc_texts.fn:ValidatedRasterizedGlyph::new: Validates a glyph raster before it can be used by an atlas builder.
doc_texts.fn:ViewElement::new:
Wraps `view` as an element. The element takes the view's entity id, if it has one.

A view wrapped this way renders every frame, since its parent may hand it new
properties without notifying its entity. Entities and [`AnyView`]s placed as children
directly keep their output between frames instead.
doc_texts.fn:VisualTestAppContext::advance_clock:
Moves the simulated clock forward by `duration`, and runs the tasks that become ready.

Use this for time-based behavior such as tooltip delays.
doc_texts.fn:VisualTestAppContext::capture_screens:
Renders `window` to an image and returns it.

This renders to a texture and reads the pixels back, so the window doesn't need
to be visible on screen.

# Errors

Returns an error if the window has been closed or can't be rendered.
doc_texts.fn:VisualTestAppContext::dispatch_action:
Dispatches `action` to the focused element in `window`, then runs pending tasks.

If the window is closed, the action is dropped silently.
doc_texts.fn:VisualTestAppContext::dispatch_keystr:
Dispatches one keystroke to the focused element in `window`.

If the window is closed, the keystroke is dropped silently. This doesn't run pending tasks.
doc_texts.fn:VisualTestAppContext::executor: Returns a clone of the background executor.
doc_texts.fn:VisualTestAppContext::foreground_exec: Returns a clone of the foreground executor.
doc_texts.fn:VisualTestAppContext::has_global: Returns whether a global of type `G` is set.
doc_texts.fn:VisualTestAppContext::is_screen_captu: Returns whether this platform can capture the screen.
doc_texts.fn:VisualTestAppContext::new:
Creates a context on `platform` with the real rendering and deterministic task scheduling.

The scheduler seed is read from the `SEED` environment variable, and is `0`
when it's unset or isn't a number.

This uses an empty asset source, so SVG icons don't render. Use
[`VisualTestAppContext::with_asset_source`] to load real assets.
doc_texts.fn:VisualTestAppContext::open_offscreen_:
Opens a window of `size` at the origin `(-10000, -10000)`, off every display.

The window is shown and composited, so [`VisualTestAppContext::capture_screenshot`]
can capture it. It doesn't take focus.

# Errors

Returns an error if the window can't be opened.

Opens an off-screen window of 1280 by 800 pixels.

See [`VisualTestAppContext::open_offscreen_window`].
doc_texts.fn:VisualTestAppContext::read: Runs `f` with read-only access to the [`App`].
doc_texts.fn:VisualTestAppContext::read_from_clipb: Returns the clipboard's current item, or `None`.
doc_texts.fn:VisualTestAppContext::read_global:
Runs `f` with the global of type `G`.

# Panics

Panics if no global of type `G` is set.
doc_texts.fn:VisualTestAppContext::run_until_parke:
Runs pending foreground and background tasks until none can make progress.

This doesn't move the simulated clock. Use [`VisualTestAppContext::advance_clock`] for that.
doc_texts.fn:VisualTestAppContext::set_global: Sets the global of type `G`, replacing any previous value.
doc_texts.fn:VisualTestAppContext::simulate_click: Presses and releases the left button at `position`, with click count `1` on both events.
doc_texts.fn:VisualTestAppContext::simulate_event:
Dispatches `event` to `window`, then runs pending tasks.

If the window is closed, the event is dropped silently.
doc_texts.fn:VisualTestAppContext::simulate_input:
Types `input` into `window`, one keystroke per character, then runs pending tasks.

Each keystroke carries its character as the key and as the text, so a space
typed this way reaches text inputs as a space.
doc_texts.fn:VisualTestAppContext::simulate_keystr:
Sends each keystroke in a whitespace-separated list to `window`, then runs pending tasks.

Unlike [`TestAppContext::simulate_keystrokes`](crate::TestAppContext::simulate_keystrokes),
this splits on any whitespace, so a tab or newline separates keystrokes too.

# Panics

Panics if any part isn't a valid keystroke.
doc_texts.fn:VisualTestAppContext::simulate_mouse_: Presses `button` at `position`. The click count is always `1`.
Moves the pointer to `position`, with `button` held if it's `Some`.
Releases `button` at `position`. The click count is always `1`.
doc_texts.fn:VisualTestAppContext::spawn: Spawns a future on the foreground executor. It runs when tasks run.
doc_texts.fn:VisualTestAppContext::text_system: Returns the text system.
doc_texts.fn:VisualTestAppContext::update: Runs `f` with mutable access to the [`App`]. This doesn't run pending tasks.
doc_texts.fn:VisualTestAppContext::update_global:
Runs `f` with mutable access to the global of type `G`.

# Panics

Panics if no global of type `G` is set.
doc_texts.fn:VisualTestAppContext::update_window:
Runs `f` with the window's root view, the [`Window`] and the [`App`].

# Errors

Returns an error if `window` has been closed.
doc_texts.fn:VisualTestAppContext::wait_for:
Waits until `predicate` returns `true` for `entity`, or until `timeout` passes.

The predicate is checked between polls, which are 10 milliseconds apart. The
timeout is measured in real time, not simulated time.

# Errors

Returns an error if `timeout` passes before the predicate is true.
doc_texts.fn:VisualTestAppContext::wait_for_animat: Waits for about two frames (32 milliseconds of simulated time), then runs pending tasks.
doc_texts.fn:VisualTestAppContext::with_asset_sour:
Creates a context on `platform` that loads assets from `asset_source`.

Pass the application's real asset source so that SVG icons render in screenshots.
doc_texts.fn:VisualTestContext::deactivate_window:
Makes this window inactive, as if the user had switched to another window.

Does nothing if the window isn't active. Runs pending tasks.
doc_texts.fn:VisualTestContext::debug_bounds:
Returns the bounds of the element with `debug_selector(selector)` in the last painted frame, or `None`.

Draw the view first, so that the frame contains the element. Use this to click
an element without guessing its position. Builds without `debug_assertions` don't
record selectors, so there this always returns `None`; see
[`InteractiveElement::debug_selector`](crate::InteractiveElement::debug_selector).
doc_texts.fn:VisualTestContext::dispatch_action: Dispatches `action` to the focused element in this window, then runs pending tasks.
doc_texts.fn:VisualTestContext::document_path: Returns the document path set with [`Window::set_document_path`], or `None` if none was set.
doc_texts.fn:VisualTestContext::draw:
Lays out and paints `f`'s element as a root at `origin`, within `space`.

Use this to paint an element on its own, without a root view. It returns the
element's request-layout and prepaint state. The window is refreshed afterward.
doc_texts.fn:VisualTestContext::from_window:
Creates a context for `window` that shares `cx`'s app.

Shadow the [`TestAppContext`] with the result, which is usually what you want:
`let cx = VisualTestContext::from_window(window, cx);`.
doc_texts.fn:VisualTestContext::into_mut:
Leaks this context and returns a mutable reference that stays valid until the test ends.

[`TestAppContext::add_window_view`] and [`TestAppContext::add_empty_window`] use
this to return a context that borrows from the test. The memory is freed when
the test quits.
doc_texts.fn:VisualTestContext::run_until_parked:
Runs pending tasks until none can make progress.

This runs the same scheduler as [`TestAppContext::run_until_parked`]. It doesn't move the simulated clock.
doc_texts.fn:VisualTestContext::simulate_capslock_: Sends a modifiers-changed event with no modifiers and caps lock set to `on`.
doc_texts.fn:VisualTestContext::simulate_click: Presses and releases the left button at `position`, with click count `1` on both events.
doc_texts.fn:VisualTestContext::simulate_close:
Runs the window's should-close callback and returns its result.

Returns `false` if the window has no callback. This doesn't remove the window
from the app, even when the callback returns `true`.
doc_texts.fn:VisualTestContext::simulate_event:
Sends `event` to the window as platform input, then runs pending tasks.

Call [`VisualTestContext::draw`] first, so that hit tests see the current layout.
doc_texts.fn:VisualTestContext::simulate_input:
Types `input` into this window, one keystroke per character, then runs pending tasks.

See [`TestAppContext::simulate_input`] for how characters are sent.
doc_texts.fn:VisualTestContext::simulate_keystroke:
Sends a space-separated list of keystrokes to this window, then runs pending tasks.

This is [`TestAppContext::simulate_keystrokes`] for this window. The same rules
apply: a space separates keystrokes, so use the key name `"space"` only as one
keystroke.
doc_texts.fn:VisualTestContext::simulate_modifiers: Sends a modifiers-changed event with `modifiers`. Caps lock is reported as off.
doc_texts.fn:VisualTestContext::simulate_mouse_dow: Presses `button` at `position` with `modifiers` held. The click count is always `1`.
doc_texts.fn:VisualTestContext::simulate_mouse_mov: Moves the pointer to `position`, with `button` held if it's `Some`.
doc_texts.fn:VisualTestContext::simulate_mouse_up: Releases `button` at `position` with `modifiers` held. The click count is always `1`.
doc_texts.fn:VisualTestContext::simulate_resize:
Resizes the window to `size`. See [`TestAppContext::simulate_window_resize`].

This doesn't paint the window. Call [`VisualTestContext::draw`] to paint at the new size.
doc_texts.fn:VisualTestContext::simulate_scale_fac: Simulates the window moving to a display with a different scale factor.
doc_texts.fn:VisualTestContext::simulate_visibilit: Simulates a change in whether the platform is presenting this window.
doc_texts.fn:VisualTestContext::update: Runs `f` with the window and the app. This doesn't run pending tasks.
doc_texts.fn:VisualTestContext::virtual_keyboard_r: Returns the number of virtual keyboard show requests sent to this test window.
doc_texts.fn:VisualTestContext::window_title: Returns the title set with [`Window::set_window_title`], or `None` if none was set.
doc_texts.fn:WeakEntity::new_invalid: Returns a weak handle that never upgrades. Use it as a placeholder until you have a real entity.
doc_texts.fn:WeakEntity::read_with:
Calls `read` with the entity if it still exists. Returns an error if it has been released.

Use this when you only need to read the value. It works with any [`AppContext`].
doc_texts.fn:WeakEntity::update_in:
Like [`WeakEntity::update`], but also passes the [`Window`] that the entity is shown in.

Returns an error if the entity has been released, or if it isn't shown in a window that is
currently available.
doc_texts.fn:WeakEntity::upgrade: Returns a strong handle to the entity, or `None` if it has been released.
doc_texts.fn:WeakFocusHandle::upgrade: Returns a [`FocusHandle`] for the same element, or `None` if every strong handle is gone.
doc_texts.fn:Window::a11y_frame_number:
How many accessibility trees this window has built; zero before the
first. Lets a caller tell a fresh tree from the one it already read.
doc_texts.fn:Window::a11y_node_bounds: Window-space bounds, in logical pixels, of a node in the last built tree.
doc_texts.fn:Window::a11y_tree:
The accessibility tree built by the last frame, when one was built (see
[`Self::is_a11y_active`] and [`Self::set_a11y_forced`]). Node ids are
stable while the element identity is; bounds come from
[`Self::a11y_node_bounds`].
doc_texts.fn:Window::activate:
Brings the window to the front and focuses it at the platform level.

The platform may refuse, such as when the app isn't allowed to steal focus. If you have an
activation token from the platform, use [`Window::activate_with_token`] instead.
doc_texts.fn:Window::activate_with_token:
Request focus using a token supplied by the desktop shell, such as a
Wayland tray host. Show the window before calling this method.

Returns whether the platform submitted the request. The compositor may
still deny focus. Returns false for empty tokens or unsupported platforms;
callers can then fall back to [`Self::activate`]. Tokens must not
be reused for subsequent activations.
doc_texts.fn:Window::appearance:
Returns whether the system uses a light or dark appearance for this window.

Updated before the callbacks from [`Window::observe_window_appearance`] run.
doc_texts.fn:Window::available_actions:
Returns one instance of each action that a listener on the focused element's path handles.

Use it to populate a command palette. Actions that need input to build are left out.
doc_texts.fn:Window::bindings_for_action:
Returns the key bindings that invoke `action` from the focused element, in the order they were added.

For display, use the last binding, which takes precedence. See
[`Window::highest_precedence_binding_for_action`] to get that one directly.
doc_texts.fn:Window::bindings_for_action_in:
Returns any bindings that would invoke an action on the given focus handle if it were
focused. Bindings are returned in the order they were added. For display, the last binding
should take precedence.
doc_texts.fn:Window::bindings_for_action_in_contex: Returns the key bindings for an action in a context.
doc_texts.fn:Window::blur:
Removes focus from every element in the window.

Focus can be given again afterward with [`Window::focus`]. Pending keystrokes
are cleared. Does nothing if focus is disabled.
doc_texts.fn:Window::bounds:
Returns the window's bounds in global screen coordinates, in logical pixels.

The window can span several displays, so the origin is in the same global space
as the displays. Use [`Window::viewport_size`] for the size of the content area.
doc_texts.fn:Window::bounds_changed:
Refreshes the window's cached size, scale and display, and calls the bounds observers.

The platform calls this when the window resizes or moves between displays. It
reads the new viewport size, scale factor, display and mouse position, redraws
the window, and then calls each callback registered with [`Window::observe`]
on the window bounds. Tests call it to simulate a resize; use
`TestAppWindow::simulate_resize` for that.
doc_texts.fn:Window::capslock: Returns the state of the Caps Lock key.
doc_texts.fn:Window::capture_long_press:
Gives `entity` the current long press. Only the entity that captured it receives its events.

The capture is released when the gesture ends or is cancelled, or when
a replacement touch begins. A listener must also call
[`Self::prevent_default`] on the started event to claim the gesture.
doc_texts.fn:Window::capture_pointer:
Captures the pointer for `hitbox_id`. While captured, all mouse move and mouse up
events will be routed to listeners that check this hitbox's `is_hovered` status,
regardless of actual hit testing. This enables drag operations that continue
even when the pointer moves outside the element's bounds.

The capture is automatically released on mouse up.
doc_texts.fn:Window::captured_hitbox: Returns the hitbox that has captured the pointer, or `None` if the pointer isn't captured.
doc_texts.fn:Window::client_inset: Returns the inset set by [`Window::set_client_inset`], or `None` if none was set.
doc_texts.fn:Window::compute_layout:
Computes the layout of `layout_id` and its descendants within `available_space`.

GPUI calls this for the root of each frame, before prepaint. After it runs, [`Window::layout_bounds`]
returns the bounds of `layout_id` and of any of its descendants. Call it during prepaint.
doc_texts.fn:Window::content_mask:
Returns the content mask in effect, which is the window's bounds unless a parent has clipped it.

Call it during prepaint or paint. See [`Window::with_content_mask`].
doc_texts.fn:Window::context_stack:
Returns the key contexts on the path from the root to the focused element, outermost first.

Key bindings match against this stack. It is empty when nothing has focus.
doc_texts.fn:Window::current_view:
Returns the id of the view whose element is being rendered, prepainted or painted.

Use it when a callback needs to notify the view being drawn, such as the callback
that [`Window::use_asset`] schedules. Call it during prepaint or paint.

# Panics

Panics if no view is being rendered, such as in an event listener or outside a frame.
Debug builds also panic when called outside prepaint and paint.
doc_texts.fn:Window::cycle_debug_frame_overlay_mod:
Advances the debug frame overlay through its hidden, frame-time-only,
and detailed modes.
doc_texts.fn:Window::debug_a11y_tree_json: Debug representation of the last frame's accessibility information.
doc_texts.fn:Window::debug_frame_overlay_mode: Returns the current mode of the debug frame overlay.
doc_texts.fn:Window::default_prevented: Returns whether [`Window::prevent_default`] was called for the event being dispatched.
doc_texts.fn:Window::defer:
Runs `f` with this window after the current update finishes.

Use it to act on this window while the entities that are being updated are
still borrowed. If the window has closed by then, `f` doesn't run.
doc_texts.fn:Window::defer_draw:
Schedules `element` to be drawn on top of the current tree, after the tree is painted.

The element is laid out and painted at `absolute_offset` in window coordinates. Deferred
elements with a higher `priority` are drawn later, so they appear above the others.
Popovers, menus and tooltips use it to escape the clipping of their parents. Pass a
`content_mask` to clip the element during both prepaint and paint, or `None` for no clip.

Call it during prepaint.

# Panics

Panics in debug builds if called outside prepaint. Panics if there is no active node in the
dispatch tree, which happens when no element is being prepainted.
doc_texts.fn:Window::disable_focus:
Removes focus from the window and stops any element in it from receiving focus.

Later calls to [`Window::focus`], [`Window::focus_next`] and [`Window::focus_prev`]
do nothing. Use it when the window is being torn down or is only for display.
doc_texts.fn:Window::dismiss_virtual_keyboard: Requests dismissal of the virtual keyboard without changing GPUI focus.
doc_texts.fn:Window::dispatch_action:
Dispatches `action` to the focused element, after the current update finishes.

The action runs through the focus path, like an action from a keybinding. If
nothing has focus, it is dispatched from the root of the window's last
rendered frame.
doc_texts.fn:Window::dispatch_event:
Dispatches a platform input event to the window and returns how it was handled.

Mouse, keyboard and touch events are routed as described in [input dispatch](crate::_documentation::concepts::input_dispatch).
The result says whether propagation continued and whether a listener called [`Window::prevent_default`].
Platforms call this for every event. Tests normally use the `simulate_*` methods on [`TestAppWindow`](crate::TestAppWindow) instead.
doc_texts.fn:Window::dispatch_keystroke:
Dispatches `keystroke` as if the user had pressed it, and returns whether it was handled.

The keystroke goes through the same path as a real key press: actions from key bindings run
first, then key listeners, then the focused input handler receives its text. The return value
is `true` if a listener stopped propagation or the input handler accepted the text. Tests use
it through [`TestAppWindow::simulate_keystrokes`](crate::TestAppWindow::simulate_keystrokes). Build a keystroke with [`Keystroke::parse`].
doc_texts.fn:Window::display: Determine the display on which the window is visible.
doc_texts.fn:Window::draw:
Builds a new frame from the root view and makes it the rendered frame.

This runs the render, request-layout, prepaint and paint phases, then swaps the
frame in and delivers focus-change listeners. The frame is not shown until
the window presents it to the screen. The returned token must be passed to
[`ArenaClearNeeded::clear`], which frees the element arena for the next frame.
GPUI calls this for every frame that needs one, so most code doesn't call it directly.
doc_texts.fn:Window::drop_image:
Removes every frame of `data` from the renderer's texture atlas, freeing its GPU memory.

Call it when an image is no longer needed. The image is uploaded again the next time it is
painted. The `Result` is always `Ok`, and it exists so the method can be extended later.
doc_texts.fn:Window::element_offset:
Returns the offset that the current element's position is shifted by, in logical pixels.

Scroll containers set it with [`Window::with_element_offset`]. Call it during prepaint.
doc_texts.fn:Window::focus_lost_restore_target:
While focus-lost listeners are being dispatched, returns the closest ancestor of the
previously focused element that can still receive focus, making it a suitable target
for focus restoration. Returns `None` at all other times, or when no such ancestor exists.
doc_texts.fn:Window::focus_next:
Moves focus to the next tab stop in tab order, wrapping at the end.

Tab stops are the focusable elements whose [`FocusHandle::tab_stop`] is `true`,
read from the last rendered frame. If nothing has focus, this moves to the first
tab stop. Does nothing if focus is disabled or there are no tab stops.

GPUI doesn't bind Tab to this method. Bind a key to it with [`App::bind_keys`]
and an action handler, as in the [focus guide](crate::_documentation::guides::focus).
doc_texts.fn:Window::focus_prev:
Moves focus to the previous tab stop in tab order, wrapping at the start.

This is the reverse of [`Window::focus_next`], with the same rules for tab stops
and disabled focus.
doc_texts.fn:Window::focused:
Returns the [`FocusHandle`] of the focused element, or `None` if nothing has focus.

Returns `None` if the focused element's handles have all been dropped.
doc_texts.fn:Window::frame_duration_snapshot: Returns a snapshot of the current frame-duration histograms.
doc_texts.fn:Window::fully_visible_bounds:
Returns a conservative rectangle avoiding platform-known obscured content.

Intersects the visual viewport with the full layout area inset by system
safe areas and keyboard occlusion. Unknown overlays cannot be excluded.
doc_texts.fn:Window::get_asset:
Returns the loaded asset if it is ready, or starts loading it and returns `None`.

Unlike [`Window::use_asset`], this doesn't redraw the view when loading finishes. Use it
when a later redraw from some other cause will pick up the result. Concurrent calls share
one load.
doc_texts.fn:Window::gpu_context:
Returns the GPU device and queue used to render this window, if the backend exposes them.

The returned box holds the backend's device and queue, which you downcast to use. Embedders
that share the device with their own rendering use this. See also [`Window::gpu_device_lost`].
doc_texts.fn:Window::gpu_context_info:
Returns backend-specific GPU information for custom controls.

The returned box has the rendering backend's own type. Downcast it with `downcast_ref` to
read the backend's values.
doc_texts.fn:Window::gpu_device_lost:
Whether the GPU device backing this window has been lost (recovery
happens on a subsequent platform draw). `None` when the backend
cannot know. Embedders that captured the device from
[`Self::gpu_context`] should stop submitting while this is
`Some(true)` and re-acquire the device once it reads `Some(false)`.
doc_texts.fn:Window::gpu_specs:
Returns information about the GPU that renders this window, if the platform reports it.

Currently it returns `None` on macOS and Windows.
doc_texts.fn:Window::handle_input:
Registers `input_handler` to receive text from the platform, if `focus_handle` is focused.

Text input and IME composition go through this handler. It stays
active until the next frame is painted, and it is ignored unless `focus_handle` has focus.
Use [`ElementInputHandler`](crate::ElementInputHandler) to implement it for an element.
Call it during paint.
doc_texts.fn:Window::handler_for:
Wraps `f` as a handler that updates `entity`, if it is still alive.

Like [`Window::listener_for`], but the handler takes only a window and an app, with no event.
Use it for callbacks such as `on_click` handlers that don't need the event value.
doc_texts.fn:Window::has_active_prompt:
Returns whether a prompt rendered by GPUI is currently active in this window.

This is only true for prompts rendered in the window (see
[`App::set_prompt_builder`]), not for platform-native prompt dialogs.
doc_texts.fn:Window::has_image_atlas_entry:
Returns whether every frame of `data` is already uploaded to the texture atlas.

Use it to check whether painting `data` would need an upload. Images with no frames
return `false`.
doc_texts.fn:Window::has_long_press_capture: Returns whether `entity` is the one that captured the current long press.
doc_texts.fn:Window::has_pending_keystrokes:
Returns whether the window is partway through a multi-keystroke binding, such as `cmd-k cmd-s`.

After the first keystroke of such a binding, GPUI waits for the next one. Use this to show
that a sequence is pending.
doc_texts.fn:Window::highest_precedence_binding_fo:
Returns the key binding that takes precedence for `action` from the focused element.

This is the same as the last result of [`Window::bindings_for_action`], without building the list.

Returns the highest precedence key binding that would invoke an action on the given focus
handle if it were focused. This is more efficient than getting the last result of
`bindings_for_action_in`.

Returns the highest precedence key binding for an action in a context. This is more
efficient than getting the last result of `bindings_for_action_in_context`.
doc_texts.fn:Window::inner_window_bounds:
Returns the window's bounds and state without the client-side insets that
Wayland and X11 windows draw around their content.
doc_texts.fn:Window::input_latency_snapshot: Returns a snapshot of the current input-latency histograms.
doc_texts.fn:Window::insert_hitbox_mut:
Like [`Window::insert_hitbox`], but returns a mutable reference so you can set the hitbox's
[`tags`](Hitbox::tags) before the frame ends.

The reference is into this frame's hitbox list, so it stays valid only until the next call
that inserts a hitbox. Call it during prepaint.
doc_texts.fn:Window::insert_inspector_hitbox:
Records `hitbox_id` as belonging to `inspector_id`, so picking mode can select that element.

Does nothing unless the inspector is in picking mode. Call it during prepaint or paint, after
inserting the hitbox.
doc_texts.fn:Window::insert_window_control_hitbox:
Registers `hitbox` as the platform control `area` of a custom title bar.

The platform uses the hitbox to drag, maximize, minimize or close the window when the user
interacts with it. Call it during paint, and see [`WindowControlArea`] for the areas.
doc_texts.fn:Window::insets: Returns the regions of this window obscured by system UI and the keyboard.
doc_texts.fn:Window::invalidate_character_coordina:
Tells the platform to recompute where the input method candidate window should appear.

Call it after the caret moves, so the candidate window follows the text input.
doc_texts.fn:Window::is_a11y_active:
Returns whether accessibility features are active for this frame,
i.e. whether assistive technology (such as a screen reader) is
connected and an accessibility tree is being built.

Use this to skip computing data during rendering that is only
observable through the accessibility tree. When accessibility is
activated, a redraw is forced, so gated work is recomputed before the
next tree update is sent to the platform.

See the [accessibility guide](crate::_documentation::guides::accessibility) for an overview.
doc_texts.fn:Window::is_a11y_enabled:
Returns whether accessibility support is enabled for this window.

This is false when the app was created with [`crate::Application::new_inaccessible`].
Unlike [`Self::is_a11y_active`], this does not depend on whether assistive
technology is currently connected, so it can be used to gate subscriptions
that are only needed for accessibility.
doc_texts.fn:Window::is_action_available:
Returns whether a listener for `action` is on the dispatch path from the focused element.

Use it to enable or disable menu items and buttons that trigger `action`. If nothing has
focus, the path starts at the window's root.
doc_texts.fn:Window::is_action_available_in:
Returns whether a listener for `action` is on the dispatch path from `focus_handle`.

This is [`Window::is_action_available`] for an element other than the focused one.
doc_texts.fn:Window::is_fullscreen: Returns whether the window is in fullscreen mode.
doc_texts.fn:Window::is_inspector_picking: Returns whether the inspector is in picking mode, where clicks select elements instead of reaching them.
doc_texts.fn:Window::is_maximized:
Returns whether the platform reports this window as maximized.

On some platforms, such as Windows, a maximized window is not the same as a
window whose bounds match the display's size.
doc_texts.fn:Window::is_minimizable: Returns whether the window was opened as minimizable in [`WindowOptions::is_minimizable`].
doc_texts.fn:Window::is_resizable: Returns whether the window was opened as resizable in [`WindowOptions::is_resizable`].
doc_texts.fn:Window::is_simple_fullscreen:
Returns whether the window is in simple fullscreen, which covers the whole screen
including the menu bar.

Always `false` on platforms other than macOS.
doc_texts.fn:Window::is_visible:
Whether frames drawn for this window will be shown.

This is not the window's shown/hidden state: a shown window that is
fully behind another window, minimized, or on a sleeping display is not
visible here.
doc_texts.fn:Window::is_window_active:
Returns whether the operating system considers this window active.

Key input goes to the focused element only while the window is active.
doc_texts.fn:Window::is_window_hovered:
Returns whether this is the window that the mouse pointer is over.

On macOS this is the same as [`Window::is_window_active`].
doc_texts.fn:Window::keystroke_text_for:
Returns the keystrokes bound to `action`, formatted for display, such as `"cmd-s"`.

Uses the highest-precedence binding, which is the last one added to the keymap. Returns the
action's name if it has no binding. Use it for labels on menus and tooltips.
doc_texts.fn:Window::last_input_was_keyboard:
Returns whether the most recent input came from the keyboard.

Focus rings and hover styles often check this, so they appear only for keyboard
