navigation. [`HitboxId::is_hovered`] already returns `false` when it is `true`.
doc_texts.fn:Window::last_input_was_touch: Returns whether the last input event came from a touch screen.
doc_texts.fn:Window::layout_bounds:
Returns the bounds of a layout node, in window coordinates, after the element offset is applied.

GPUI passes these bounds to [`Element::prepaint`](crate::Element::prepaint) for you, so you rarely need this method
directly. It is valid during prepaint, after [`Window::compute_layout`] has run. The offset
comes from [`Window::with_element_offset`], such as a scroll position.
doc_texts.fn:Window::line_height: Returns the line height of the current text style, in logical pixels.
doc_texts.fn:Window::listener_for:
Wraps `f` as an event listener that updates the entity `view`, if it is still alive.

The returned closure takes an event, a window and an app, and calls `f` with the view, the
event, the window and a `Context<T>`. If `view` has been released, the call does nothing.
It works like [`Context::listener`] for code that has a window but no `Context` at hand.
doc_texts.fn:Window::merge_all_windows:
Merges all open windows into a single tabbed window.
This is macOS specific.
doc_texts.fn:Window::minimize_window: Minimizes the window at the platform level.
doc_texts.fn:Window::modifiers: Returns the modifier keys (Shift, Control, Alt, Command and so on) held right now.
doc_texts.fn:Window::mouse_hit_test:
Returns the hit test for the mouse position, computed from the last rendered frame.

It lists the hitboxes under the pointer, front to back, with each hitbox's depth and tags.
The result is updated when the mouse moves or the frame is redrawn.
doc_texts.fn:Window::mouse_position:
Returns the last known mouse position, in window coordinates.

The position is updated from the mouse events the window receives.
doc_texts.fn:Window::move_tab_to_new_window:
Moves the tab to a new containing window.
This is macOS specific.
doc_texts.fn:Window::native_window_state:
Encode the window's native restorable state into an opaque blob.
Returns `None` on platforms without native state restoration or if encoding fails.
doc_texts.fn:Window::notify_text_input_changed:
Notifies native text services that the focused component's text changed.

Text components should call this after application-driven edits, in addition
to notifying GPUI to redraw. Unfocused or unregistered components are ignored.
doc_texts.fn:Window::notify_text_selection_changed:
Notifies native text services that the focused component's selection changed.

Text components should call this after application-driven selection changes,
in addition to notifying GPUI to redraw.
doc_texts.fn:Window::observe:
Calls `on_notify` each time `observed` is notified, with a handle to it and this window.

This is the window-aware form of [`Context::observe`]. The callback runs
when the current update finishes, not during the call to [`Context::notify`].
The observation lasts as long as the returned [`Subscription`] is alive, and
it ends early once `observed` is released.
doc_texts.fn:Window::observe_button_layout_changed:
Calls `callback` when the platform's window button layout changes.

The button layout decides which window controls appear in a custom title bar,
and which side they are on. Keep the returned [`Subscription`] alive while you
need the callback; dropping it unsubscribes.
doc_texts.fn:Window::observe_global:
Calls `handler` each time the global `G` is updated, for as long as the subscription is alive.

The window-aware form of [`App::observe_global`]. Keep the returned [`Subscription`] in the
view that uses the global.
doc_texts.fn:Window::observe_release:
Calls `on_release` once when `entity` is released, with its final state and this window.

The callback runs after the last handle to `entity` is dropped. Keep the
returned [`Subscription`] alive until the entity is released; dropping it
cancels the callback.
doc_texts.fn:Window::observe_window_appearance:
Calls `callback` when the system switches between light and dark appearance.

The callback runs during the next update after the change, not inside the
platform callback. Keep the returned [`Subscription`] alive for as long as
you want to be notified; dropping it unsubscribes. See [`Window::appearance`]
to read the current value.
doc_texts.fn:Window::observe_window_display:
Registers a callback invoked when the window moves to another display
or its display's properties change, for example its refresh
interval. [`Self::refresh_interval`] already returns the new value
when the callback runs.
doc_texts.fn:Window::observe_window_visibility: Registers a callback to be invoked when the window's visibility changes.
doc_texts.fn:Window::on_a11y_action:
Register a listener for an accessibility action on a specific node.
The listener will be called when a screen reader requests the given
action on the node identified by `node_id`.

See the [accessibility guide](crate::_documentation::guides::accessibility) for an overview.
doc_texts.fn:Window::on_action:
Register an action listener on this node for the next frame. The type of action
is determined by the first parameter of the given listener. When the next frame is rendered
the listener will be cleared.

This is a fairly low-level method, so prefer using action handlers on elements unless you have
a specific need to register a listener yourself.

This method should only be called as part of the paint phase of element drawing.
doc_texts.fn:Window::on_action_when:
Registers `listener` for `action_type` on the current node, if `condition` is `true`.

Works like [`Window::on_action`], but the listener is registered only when `condition` is
`true`. The listener is cleared when the next frame is painted. Call it during paint.
doc_texts.fn:Window::on_focus_in:
Calls `listener` when `handle`'s element, or one of its descendants, gains focus.

It doesn't fire when focus moves between `handle`'s element and its descendants, because
`handle` already had focus. The listener runs during the focus phase at the end of the frame.
The returned [`Subscription`] keeps the listener active until it is dropped.
Keep the subscription in the view that owns the element, or the listener stops firing.
doc_texts.fn:Window::on_focus_out:
Calls `listener` when `handle`'s element, or one of its descendants, loses focus.

The listener gets a [`FocusOutEvent`] whose `blurred` field identifies the element that lost
focus. The listener runs during the focus phase at the end of the frame. The returned
[`Subscription`] keeps the listener active until it is dropped. [`Context::on_focus_out`]
is the same for the view being rendered.
doc_texts.fn:Window::on_key_event:
Registers a listener for key events of type `Event` on the current element, for the frame being painted.

`Event` is chosen by the type of the listener's first parameter, such as `KeyDownEvent`.
Listeners are cleared when the next frame is painted, so register them on every paint.
This is a low-level method. Prefer the handlers on elements, such as `on_key_down`, unless you
need to register a listener yourself. Call it during paint.
doc_texts.fn:Window::on_modifiers_changed:
Registers a listener for changes to the modifier keys, for the frame being painted.

The listener runs when Shift, Control, Alt or Command goes down or up. Like the other
listeners, it is cleared when the next frame is painted. Call it during paint.
doc_texts.fn:Window::on_window_should_close:
Registers a callback that runs when the user asks to close the window, and can cancel the close.

The callback returns `true` to let the window close and `false` to keep it open, such as when
there are unsaved changes. If the window no longer exists when the request arrives, the close
proceeds. Call it once per window; it sets the platform's close handler.
doc_texts.fn:Window::paint_backdrop_filter:
Paint a backdrop filter into the scene for the next frame at the current z-index. The
renderer blurs the content already painted behind `bounds` and composites the result
into the rounded rectangle described by `bounds` and `corner_radii` — the CSS
`backdrop-filter` effect (frosted glass). Typically the element then paints a translucent
background quad on top so its color tints the blurred backdrop.
`corner_smoothing` ranges from circular corners at `0.0` to maximum smoothing at `1.0`.

Does nothing when `filters` produce no visible blur.

This method should only be called as part of the paint phase of element drawing.
doc_texts.fn:Window::paint_drop_shadows:
Paints the outer shadows in `shadows` behind an element of `bounds` and `corner_radii`.

Paint these before the element's background, so the shadow sits under it. Inset shadows
are skipped; paint those with [`Window::paint_inset_shadows`] after the background.
Call it during paint.
doc_texts.fn:Window::paint_emoji:
Paints an emoji glyph into the scene for the next frame at the current z-index.

The y component of the origin is the baseline of the glyph.
You should generally prefer to use the [`ShapedLine::paint`](crate::ShapedLine::paint) or
[`ShapedText::paint`](crate::ShapedText::paint) methods in the [`TextSystem`](crate::TextSystem).
This method is only useful if you need to paint a single emoji that has already been shaped.

This method should only be called as part of the paint phase of element drawing.
doc_texts.fn:Window::paint_emoji_with_color: Paints a color glyph with an application foreground for `currentColor` layers.
doc_texts.fn:Window::paint_glyph:
Paints a monochrome (non-emoji) glyph into the scene for the next frame at the current z-index.

The y component of the origin is the baseline of the glyph.
You should generally prefer to use the [`ShapedLine::paint`](crate::ShapedLine::paint) or
[`ShapedText::paint`](crate::ShapedText::paint) methods in the [`TextSystem`](crate::TextSystem).
This method is only useful if you need to paint a single glyph that has already been shaped.

This method should only be called as part of the paint phase of element drawing.
doc_texts.fn:Window::paint_image:
Paints `data` into `bounds`, scaled to fit `image_bounds`.

The visible region is `bounds.intersect(&image_bounds)`, and `corner_radii` round the
corners of `bounds`. `frame_index` selects a frame of an animated image, and `grayscale`
paints the image in grayscale. Returns an error if the image can't be uploaded to the
renderer. Call it during paint.
doc_texts.fn:Window::paint_inset_shadows:
Paints the inset shadows in `shadows` inside an element of `bounds` and `corner_radii`.

Paint these after the element's background, so the shadow sits on top of the fill. Outer
shadows are skipped; paint those with [`Window::paint_drop_shadows`] before the background.
Call it during paint.
doc_texts.fn:Window::paint_layer:
Runs `f` inside a new layer clipped to `bounds`, which groups the primitives `f` paints.

A layer is a batch of primitives with the same draw order and no overlaps. Layers
are a performance hint that lets the renderer batch the work. Painting outside `bounds`
is clipped to the intersection of `bounds` and the content mask. If that intersection is
empty, `f` runs with no layer. Call it during paint.
doc_texts.fn:Window::paint_path:
Paints `path` filled with `color`, at the current z-index.

The path's coordinates are in logical pixels within the window, and the content mask and
element opacity apply to it. Call it during paint.
doc_texts.fn:Window::paint_quad:
Paint one or more quads into the scene for the next frame at the current stacking context.
Quads are colored rectangular regions with an optional background, border, and corner radius.
Use [`PaintQuad::new`] and its builder methods to construct the quad.
`quad.corner_smoothing` ranges from circular corners at `0.0` to maximum smoothing at `1.0`.

This method should only be called as part of the paint phase of element drawing.

Note that the `quad.corner_radii` are allowed to exceed the bounds, creating sharp corners
where the circular arcs meet. This will not display well when combined with dashed borders.
Use `Corners::clamp_radii_for_quad_size` if the radii should fit within the bounds.
doc_texts.fn:Window::paint_strikethrough:
Paints a strikethrough line of `width` starting at `origin`, using `style`.

The line is drawn at the current z-index, and the content mask and element opacity apply
to it. Call it during paint.
doc_texts.fn:Window::paint_surface:
Paints a platform surface, such as a video frame, into `bounds`.

`source` identifies the surface. The content mask applies. Call it during paint.
doc_texts.fn:Window::paint_svg:
Paints a monochrome SVG into `bounds`, tinted with `color`.

`path` identifies the SVG for caching. If `data` is `Some`, those bytes are the SVG; if
it is `None`, the SVG is loaded from `path` through the app's asset source. `transformation`
rotates or flips the SVG within `bounds`. Returns an error if the SVG can't be rendered.
Call it during paint.
doc_texts.fn:Window::paint_underline:
Paints an underline of `width` starting at `origin`, using `style`.

The underline is drawn at the current z-index, and the content mask and element opacity
apply to it. `style.wavy` draws a wave instead of a straight line. Call it during paint.
doc_texts.fn:Window::paint_underline_with_exclusio: Paints an underline excluding absolute device-space horizontal spans.
doc_texts.fn:Window::painted_underlines: Returns the underlines in the most recently rendered frame's scene.
doc_texts.fn:Window::parent_relative_layout_bounds:
Returns the bounds of a layout node relative to its parent, snapped to device pixels.

Unlike [`Window::layout_bounds`], this result doesn't depend on where the parent is in the
window, so a child keeps the same sub-pixel position while its parent moves. Text-bearing
elements use it so their glyphs don't shift as a parent scrolls. Call it during prepaint.
doc_texts.fn:Window::pending_input:
Returns the keystrokes typed so far that could still complete a multi-keystroke binding.

Returns `None` when no binding is pending. The list is cleared when the sequence completes,
times out, or focus changes.
Returns pending input that can still complete a multi-stroke key binding. Input left over
from a previous focus can never complete one.
doc_texts.fn:Window::pending_input_keystrokes: Returns the currently pending input keystrokes that might result in a multi-stroke key binding.
doc_texts.fn:Window::perform_a11y_action:
Perform an accessibility action on a node as assistive technology
would: a registered [`Self::on_a11y_action`] listener first, else the
built-in handling (`Click` synthesizes a pointer click at the node's
bounds, `Focus` focuses it, `Blur` blurs the window).
doc_texts.fn:Window::pixel_snap:
Rounds a value in logical pixels to the nearest device pixel.

Use it to keep edges crisp when you draw lines or borders at fractional positions.
doc_texts.fn:Window::pixel_snap_bounds: Rounds each edge of `bounds` to the nearest device pixel. See [`Window::pixel_snap`].
doc_texts.fn:Window::pixel_snap_f64: Rounds an `f64` logical value to the nearest device pixel. See [`Window::pixel_snap`].
doc_texts.fn:Window::pixel_snap_point: Rounds each coordinate of `position` to the nearest device pixel. See [`Window::pixel_snap`].
doc_texts.fn:Window::play_system_bell:
Request the OS to play an alert sound. On some platforms this is associated
with the window, for others it's just a simple global function call.
doc_texts.fn:Window::possible_bindings_for_input:
Returns the bindings that could complete the sequence `input`, given the current key contexts.

Use it with [`Window::pending_input_keystrokes`] to show the next keys of a sequence.
doc_texts.fn:Window::present_if_needed: Presents the most recently drawn frame if it hasn't been presented yet.
doc_texts.fn:Window::prevent_default:
Marks the event being dispatched as handled, so default behavior is skipped.

Currently it stops parent elements from taking focus on a mouse down. Check
the result with [`Window::default_prevented`] in later listeners.
doc_texts.fn:Window::prompt:
Shows a prompt with `message`, `detail` and one button per entry in `answers`.

The returned receiver yields the index of the button the user clicked. The `level` sets the
prompt's icon and emphasis. Unless the app has set a prompt builder, the platform's native
dialog is used. Await the receiver from a task, and don't block on it in a listener.
doc_texts.fn:Window::refresh_interval:
The time between refreshes of the display the window is on, as of the
platform's last display change notification. Variable refresh rate
displays report their maximum rate. Returns `None` when the platform
doesn't report it.
doc_texts.fn:Window::release_pointer: Releases the pointer capture set by [`Window::capture_pointer`], if there is one.
doc_texts.fn:Window::rem_size:
Returns the size of one rem, in logical pixels.

Rems are the unit of [`Styled`](crate::Styled) lengths such as `.text_size(rems(1.))`, so changing the
rem size scales the whole window. The value is the one set by [`Window::set_rem_size`],
or the one from the innermost [`Window::with_rem_size`] while it runs.
doc_texts.fn:Window::remove_window:
Closes this window when the current update finishes.

The window isn't removed in the middle of the update, so you can keep using
the `Window` until the update returns.
doc_texts.fn:Window::render_to_image:
Rasterizes the last rendered frame and returns its pixels as an RGBA image.

The frame isn't shown on screen, and the window doesn't need to be visible.
Use it for visual tests. Returns an error if the platform can't render to an image.
doc_texts.fn:Window::rendered_primitive_counts:
Returns how many quads, monochrome sprites, subpixel sprites and polychrome sprites the last frame contains.

The four counts are in that order. Use them in tests to check that a
change painted or removed primitives, without comparing pixels.
doc_texts.fn:Window::replace_root:
Replaces the window's root view with a new view built by `build_view`.

The window stops referring to the old root and redraws with the new one.
The old view is freed once no other [`Entity`] handles to it remain. The
returned entity is the new root.
doc_texts.fn:Window::request_animation_frame:
Draws the current view again on the next frame, even if nothing changed.

Use it for continuous drawing, such as a video or a canvas that updates
every frame. Call it while rendering or painting the view that should
update. It notifies that view on the next frame, and stops when you stop
calling it.

Purely decorative motion, such as spinners, should use
[`AnimationExt::with_animation`](crate::AnimationExt::with_animation), which
respects [`App::reduce_motion`]. If you use this method for decorative motion
instead, check [`App::reduce_motion`] first.

# Panics

Panics if no view is being rendered or painted. Use [`Window::on_next_frame`]
instead when you aren't inside a view.
doc_texts.fn:Window::request_attention: Asks the operating system to draw attention to this window, such as by bouncing the dock icon.
doc_texts.fn:Window::request_autoscroll:
Asks the scroll containers around the current element to scroll `bounds` into view.

Call it from [`Element::prepaint`](crate::Element::prepaint). Scroll containers such as [`crate::List`] read the request
with [`Window::take_autoscroll`], scroll, and prepaint their children again. Call it during prepaint.
doc_texts.fn:Window::request_decorations:
Requests client-side or server-side window decorations from the platform.

The request applies on Wayland.
doc_texts.fn:Window::request_layout:
Adds a layout node with `style` and `children` to the frame, and returns its id.

Call it from [`Element::request_layout`](crate::Element::request_layout) (or from a view's `render`, which runs during
request layout). Pass the ids of the child nodes you created, and use the returned
[`LayoutId`] to read the node's bounds later with [`Window::layout_bounds`]. Layout is
computed once, after every node is requested, by the framework.

Call it during request layout or prepaint.
doc_texts.fn:Window::request_measured_layout:
Adds a layout node whose size comes from `measure`, which runs during layout.

Use it for content whose size depends on what it contains, such as text. `measure` receives
the known dimensions (`None` where the size is not yet known), the available space on each
axis, the window and the app, and returns the size the node should take. GPUI uses it for
text measurement.

Call it during request layout or prepaint.
doc_texts.fn:Window::request_virtual_keyboard:
Requests the virtual keyboard for the currently focused text input.

Call from a user gesture on platforms that require one. The platform may
decline the request; this does not change focus or the layout viewport.
doc_texts.fn:Window::reset_debug_frame_overlay_sta:
Clears the debug frame overlay's frame-time statistics, except for the
total frame count, and schedules a redraw.
doc_texts.fn:Window::resize: Resizes the window's content area to `size`, in logical pixels.
doc_texts.fn:Window::resolved_direction:
Returns the resolved direction of the current measured or prepainted layout node.

Custom elements can use this when direction changes intrinsic measurement or a detached
sublayout created during prepaint.
doc_texts.fn:Window::resolved_unicode_bidi: Returns the bidirectional formatting mode of the measured layout node.
doc_texts.fn:Window::restore_native_window_state:
Restore the window's native state from a blob previously produced
by [`Window::native_window_state`]. A no-op on platforms without native state restoration.
doc_texts.fn:Window::scale_factor:
Returns the scale factor of the display the window is on.

A value of `2.0` means each logical pixel is two device pixels, as on a Retina
display. GPUI's coordinates are logical pixels; multiply by this value only when
you need device pixels.
doc_texts.fn:Window::set_a11y_forced:
Build this window's accessibility tree every frame, even with no
assistive technology connected, so [`Self::debug_a11y_tree_json`] and
the accessibility actions work for automation. Forces a redraw, since
the tree is built during prepaint. [`crate::Application::new_inaccessible`]
still wins.
doc_texts.fn:Window::set_app_id: Sets the application identifier that the platform uses to group and match windows.
doc_texts.fn:Window::set_client_inset:
Sets the width of the invisible shadow or border that client-side decorations draw.

Use it on Wayland and X11 when your app draws its own decorations. Read it
back with [`Window::client_inset`].
doc_texts.fn:Window::set_cursor_style:
Sets the cursor shown while the pointer is over `hitbox`.

The style applies only while `hitbox` is hovered. Call it during paint. Set it
on a hitbox you inserted during prepaint. Use [`Window::set_window_cursor_style`]
to set the cursor for the whole window.
doc_texts.fn:Window::set_cursor_style_with:
Resolves this hitbox's cursor from window coordinates on pointer input.
Return `None` to use the next cursor request. Cached paints retain the resolver.
doc_texts.fn:Window::set_debug_frame_overlay_mode: Sets the mode of the debug frame overlay and schedules a redraw.
doc_texts.fn:Window::set_document_path:
Set the path of the file this window represents.
On macOS, this sets the window's accessibility document property (AXDocument).
doc_texts.fn:Window::set_exclusive_edge:
Set which anchored edge a layer-shell surface's exclusive zone applies to.
This is only needed to disambiguate a corner-anchored surface; otherwise the
edge is deduced from the anchor. The edge must be a single edge the surface
is anchored to, or it is ignored. (Wayland layer-shell windows only)
doc_texts.fn:Window::set_exclusive_zone:
Set the exclusive zone for a layer-shell surface: how much screen space it
reserves so other surfaces avoid occluding it (e.g. a panel reserving space).
Positive values reserve that distance from the anchored edge, 0 lets the
surface be moved out of others' exclusive zones, and -1 ignores reserved
space and may extend under other surfaces. (Wayland layer-shell windows only)
doc_texts.fn:Window::set_focus_handle:
Connects the current element to `focus_handle` for focus and key dispatch this frame.

If the handle is focused, the frame keeps it focused. [`InteractiveElement::track_focus`](crate::InteractiveElement::track_focus)
calls this for you. Call it during prepaint.
doc_texts.fn:Window::set_input_region:
Linux (wayland) only: Set the window's input region, the area that receives pointer
and touch input. Events outside it pass through to whatever is below the window.

- `Some(rects)` restricts input to the union of `rects`, in window coordinates.
- `Some(&[])` is an empty region, so the window receives no pointer or touch input.
- `None` resets the region to the default, so the whole window receives input again.
doc_texts.fn:Window::set_key_context:
Sets the key context of the current element, which key bindings match against.

A binding with a context such as `"Editor"` applies only when an element on the focus path has
that context. Call it during paint. See [`InteractiveElement::key_context`](crate::InteractiveElement::key_context) for the usual way to set it.
doc_texts.fn:Window::set_layout_direction_text:
Supplies source text used by `LayoutDirection::Auto` for a custom layout node.

Built-in text elements register their content automatically. Call this during
`request_layout` after obtaining the node's [`LayoutId`].
doc_texts.fn:Window::set_modifiers:
Sets the modifier keys that the window reports, without sending an event.

Tests use it to hold a key, such as Shift, while they simulate a click.
doc_texts.fn:Window::set_pending_input_timeout_pau:
Pauses or resumes the current pending input timeout on behalf of `owner`.

A paused timeout resumes automatically if `owner` is released. Returns whether the timeout
state changed. A timeout paused by one owner cannot be resumed by another.
doc_texts.fn:Window::set_rem_size:
Sets the size of one rem, in logical pixels, for the rest of the window's life.

Call it when the user changes the font size. The new size is used the next time the
window lays out, and it doesn't redraw the window by itself. Use [`Window::with_rem_size`]
to change it for part of an element tree.
doc_texts.fn:Window::set_scale_factor: Overrides the display scale factor, and redraws the window. Only available in tests.
doc_texts.fn:Window::set_tabbing_identifier:
Sets the tabbing identifier for the window.
This is macOS specific.
doc_texts.fn:Window::set_tooltip:
Shows `tooltip` for the upcoming frame and returns its [`TooltipId`].

Call it during prepaint. GPUI draws the tooltip above the window's content. Use
[`TooltipId::is_hovered`] to check whether the mouse is over the tooltip.
doc_texts.fn:Window::set_touch_prediction_enabled:
Sets whether recognized touch pans may use the platform's predicted
touch positions. Disabling drops [`TouchEvent::predicted_position`]
before gesture recognition, so pans track only raw touch positions.
doc_texts.fn:Window::set_traffic_light_position: Moves the macOS traffic light buttons to `position`, in window coordinates.
doc_texts.fn:Window::set_view_id:
Sets the view that the current element belongs to, for view caching.

GPUI sets this for each view it renders, so custom elements rarely need it. It exists for
elements built outside a view. The method is expected to go away. Call it during prepaint.
doc_texts.fn:Window::set_visible:
Show or hide the current window at the platform level.

Call [`Window::activate`] separately when the window should also receive focus.
The window manager may still focus a window when it is shown.
doc_texts.fn:Window::set_window_cursor_style:
Sets the cursor for the whole window, overriding any cursor set with [`Window::set_cursor_style`].

Call it during paint.
doc_texts.fn:Window::set_window_cursor_style_with:
Resolves a window-wide cursor from pointer position.
Return `None` to defer to hitbox cursor requests.
doc_texts.fn:Window::set_window_edited: Mark the window as dirty at the platform level.
doc_texts.fn:Window::set_window_title: Sets the window's title in the platform title bar, and in accessibility trees.
doc_texts.fn:Window::show_character_palette:
Show the platform character palette.

On macOS and Windows, opens the system character or emoji picker. On Linux,
opens an installed desktop picker (Plasma, IBus, GNOME Characters, or
KCharSelect); these pickers may require copying and pasting the selection.
Logs a warning if the platform has no available picker.
doc_texts.fn:Window::show_window_menu:
Opens the platform's title bar menu at `position`, in window coordinates.

Use it from a custom title bar with client-side decorations, on Wayland and X11.
doc_texts.fn:Window::simulate_mouse_move:
Sends a mouse move to `position` through normal event dispatch, which updates hover state and tooltips.

Use it in tests. It doesn't draw the window, so call `TestAppWindow::draw` first
if the frame you're testing has not been drawn yet.
doc_texts.fn:Window::simulate_next_frame:
Runs the callbacks scheduled with [`Window::on_next_frame`] and returns how many ran.

Tests have no platform frame loop, so this runs the pending callbacks in place
of the next frame. Callbacks scheduled while it runs wait for the next call.
doc_texts.fn:Window::spawn:
Spawns a future on the foreground executor, and gives it access to this window.

The closure receives an [`AsyncWindowContext`] that the future can use to
update the window after `.await` points. The task runs on the main thread,
and the returned [`Task`] cancels the work when it is dropped.
doc_texts.fn:Window::spawn_with_priority: Like [`Window::spawn`], but schedules the future at the given `priority`.
doc_texts.fn:Window::start_window_move:
Hands window movement to the platform's compositor, so the window follows the pointer.

Call it from a mouse-down handler on your custom title bar, on Wayland and X11.
Mouse events may not arrive while the move is in progress.
doc_texts.fn:Window::start_window_resize: Starts an interactive resize from `edge`, if this window is resizable.
doc_texts.fn:Window::subscribe:
Calls `on_event` each time `entity` emits an event of type `Evt`.

The callback receives a handle to the emitter, the event, and this window. It
is the window-aware form of [`Context::subscribe`]. The subscription lasts as
long as the returned [`Subscription`] is alive, and it ends early once
`entity` is released. `Emitter` must implement [`EventEmitter`] for `Evt`.
doc_texts.fn:Window::tab_bar_visible:
Returns the tab bar visibility.
This is macOS specific.
doc_texts.fn:Window::tabbed_windows:
Returns a list of all tabbed windows and their titles.
This is macOS specific.
doc_texts.fn:Window::take_autoscroll:
Returns and clears the autoscroll request made with [`Window::request_autoscroll`], if any.

Scroll containers call it during prepaint to implement autoscroll. Call it during prepaint.
doc_texts.fn:Window::text_style: Returns the text style in effect, built from the refinements active in [`Window::with_text_style`].
doc_texts.fn:Window::text_system: Returns the text system that shapes and rasterizes text for this window.
doc_texts.fn:Window::titlebar_double_click:
Performs the platform's title bar double-click action, such as zooming or minimizing.

This is macOS specific. Call it from a double-click handler on a custom title bar.
doc_texts.fn:Window::to_async:
Returns an [`AsyncWindowContext`] for this window, which can be held across `.await` points.

Use it inside a task spawned with `cx.spawn` when the task needs to update
this window later.
doc_texts.fn:Window::toggle_fullscreen: Enters fullscreen mode, or leaves it if the window is already fullscreen.
doc_texts.fn:Window::toggle_inspector:
Turns the element inspector on or off for this window.

While on, the window shows the inspector panel, and clicking an element in picking mode selects it.
Available with the `inspector` feature or in debug builds.
doc_texts.fn:Window::toggle_simple_fullscreen:
Toggle simple (borderless) fullscreen, where the window covers the entire
screen including the menu bar and, on notched displays, the area around the
notch. Unlike [`Window::toggle_fullscreen`], this does not move the window
into its own Mission Control space. Only has an effect on macOS.
doc_texts.fn:Window::toggle_window_tab_overview:
Shows or hides the window tab overview.
This is macOS specific.
doc_texts.fn:Window::touch_prediction_enabled:
Whether recognized touch pans may use the platform's predicted touch
positions ([`TouchEvent::predicted_position`]) to compensate for input
latency. Defaults to true.
doc_texts.fn:Window::transact:
Runs `f` during prepaint, and discards its hitboxes, tooltips and other frame data if it returns `Err`.

Use it to prepaint children, check the result, and try again. A successful `f` keeps
everything it registered. The autoscroll support in [`crate::List`] uses this method.
Call it during prepaint.

# Errors

Returns the `Err` value from `f`. Nothing from the failed attempt remains in the frame.
doc_texts.fn:Window::underline_bounds: Returns the snapped device-space bounds used to paint an underline.
doc_texts.fn:Window::use_asset:
Returns the loaded asset, or `None` while it is still loading.

The first call starts loading `source`. When loading finishes, the current view is
notified and redrawn, and later calls return `Some`. Concurrent calls share one load.
Call it during render or paint. See [`Window::get_asset`] for a version that doesn't
redraw the view.
doc_texts.fn:Window::use_keyed_transition:
Creates a new keyed transition with persistent state.

The state for this transition is associated with the provided key and will
persist across renders as long as the key remains the same. This is the
recommended method for most use cases where you want smooth, continuous
animations.

This method should only be called during `Render::render`, `RenderOnce::render`, or the drawing functions of `Element`.
doc_texts.fn:Window::use_state:
Returns state that persists across frames, identified by the call site of this method.

This is [`Window::use_keyed_state`] with a key made from the caller's source location, so
each call site in your code gets its own state. Inside a loop, every iteration shares one
key, so use `use_keyed_state` with an id for each item instead.
doc_texts.fn:Window::use_transition:
Creates a transition whose state persists across frames, identified by the call site.

Like [`Window::use_state`], each call site gets its own state, and every iteration of a loop
shares one. Use [`use_keyed_transition`](Self::use_keyed_transition) with a key for each item
instead.
doc_texts.fn:Window::viewport_size:
Returns the size of the window's content area, in logical pixels.

This excludes window decorations, so it is the size your root view lays out in.
doc_texts.fn:Window::visibility:
Whether the platform is presenting this window's frames (see
[`WindowVisibility`]).
doc_texts.fn:Window::visual_viewport_bounds:
Returns the platform's visible viewport in window-local logical pixels.

Unlike `viewport_size`, this can shrink or move when the keyboard opens.
During drawing this is a consistent frame snapshot. Outside drawing it
reflects the latest platform sample, not a synchronous geometry query.
doc_texts.fn:Window::window_bounds:
Returns the window's bounds and state, such as windowed, maximized or fullscreen.

Save this value to reopen the window at the same place later, as
[`WindowOptions::window_bounds`] expects.
doc_texts.fn:Window::window_controls: Returns which window controls, such as minimize and maximize, the platform supports.
doc_texts.fn:Window::window_decorations:
Returns whether the window uses server-side or client-side decorations.

Client-side decorations mean your app must draw the title bar and window controls.
This applies on Wayland and X11.
doc_texts.fn:Window::window_handle: Returns an [`AnyWindowHandle`] for this window, which can be stored and used later.
doc_texts.fn:Window::window_title:
Returns the window's title as the platform reports it.

This is macOS specific. To set the title, use [`Window::set_window_title`].
doc_texts.fn:Window::with_absolute_element_offset:
Runs `f` with the element offset set to `offset`, ignoring the current offset.

Use it to place an element at a fixed position, such as a drag preview that follows the
pointer. The previous offset is restored when `f` returns. Call it during prepaint.
doc_texts.fn:Window::with_content_mask:
Runs `f` with `mask` intersected with the current content mask.

Painting and hit-testing inside `f` are clipped to the result, and the previous mask
is restored when `f` returns. Passing `None` leaves the mask unchanged. Call it during
prepaint or paint.
doc_texts.fn:Window::with_element_namespace:
Runs `f` with `element_id` pushed onto the id path, so child ids are unique only within it.

Use it inside a custom element to give each group of children its own namespace. For
example, a table can namespace each row's cells by the row's id.
doc_texts.fn:Window::with_element_offset:
Runs `f` with `offset` added to the current element offset, then restores it.

Bounds that elements compute inside `f` are shifted by `offset`, which is how scroll
containers move their children. Call it during prepaint.
doc_texts.fn:Window::with_element_state:
Passes the state stored for `global_id` to `f`, and stores the state `f` returns.

`f` receives `None` the first time, or after the element wasn't rendered in the previous frame.
The state is found by `global_id` and its type `S`, so each type has its own state for the same
element. Call it during prepaint or paint, or during `Render::render` and the element drawing methods.

# Panics

Panics if the state stored for `global_id` has a different type than `S`. A nested call for
the same id and type doesn't see the state that `f` is updating. Use
[`Window::use_keyed_state`] for ordinary state that needs no type juggling.
doc_texts.fn:Window::with_filter_layer:
Isolate the painting performed by `f` into a content-filter group: the renderer renders
everything `f` paints into an offscreen target, blurs it as a single layer, and
composites the result back into the rounded rectangle described by `bounds` and
`corner_radii` — the CSS `filter` effect (e.g. blurring an element and its children).
`corner_smoothing` ranges from circular corners at `0.0` to maximum smoothing at `1.0`.

When `filters` produce no visible blur this simply runs `f` with no offscreen
indirection.

This method should only be called as part of the paint phase of element drawing.
doc_texts.fn:Window::with_global_id:
Runs `f` with a global element id made from `element_id` and the ids already on the stack.

The id is valid only inside `f`. Element state keyed by it, such as the state
behind [`Window::use_state`], is found again on the next frame when the
same path of ids is used. Most code calls [`Window::use_state`] instead.
doc_texts.fn:Window::with_id:
Runs `f` with `element_id` pushed onto the element id stack, then pops it.

Ids nest, so the same id under different parents identifies different elements.
[`InteractiveElement::id`](crate::InteractiveElement::id) and [`Element`](crate::Element) implementations call this for you.
doc_texts.fn:Window::with_image_cache:
Runs `f` with `image_cache` active, so images painted inside `f` load through it.

Pass `None` to run `f` with the cache already in effect. The cache applies only while `f` runs.
doc_texts.fn:Window::with_inspector_state:
Runs `f` with mutable access to the inspector's state for the element `inspector_id`.

The state is `Some` only for the element the inspector has selected. Otherwise `f` gets a
temporary `None`. Element code uses it to expose its own state to the inspector.
doc_texts.fn:Window::with_optional_element_state:
Like [`Window::with_element_state`], but the element may not have an id.

When `global_id` is `None`, `f` receives `None` for the outer option, which means no id was
provided. The inner `Option` is `None` the first time the state is used. When `global_id` is
`Some`, `f` must return `Some` state; when it is `None`, `f` must return `None`, since there is
nothing to store it under. Prefer `with_element_state` when the element always
has an id. Call it during prepaint or paint.
doc_texts.fn:Window::with_rem_size:
Runs `f` with `rem_size` as the rem size, or with the current rem size if `None`.

The override applies to everything `f` lays out, paints or prepaints, and ends when it
returns. Use it to render part of a tree at a different text scale.

# Panics

Panics in debug builds if called outside request layout, prepaint, or paint.
doc_texts.fn:Window::with_tab_group:
Runs `f` as a tab group, so tab navigation visits its focusable elements together.

Tab stops registered inside `f` are ordered by `index` relative to other groups. Pass `None`
to run `f` without creating a group.
doc_texts.fn:Window::with_text_style:
Runs `f` with `style` refined onto the current text style, and restores the previous style afterward.

Text painted and measured inside `f` uses the refined style. Pass `None` to run `f` with
the current style unchanged. Use [`Window::text_style`] to read the combined style.
Call it during request layout, prepaint or paint.
doc_texts.fn:Window::zoom_window: Zooms the window using the platform's zoom behavior.
doc_texts.fn:WindowBackgroundAppearance::is_opaque:
Whether the window's background hides everything behind the window,
letting the platform skip compositing the content it covers.
doc_texts.fn:WindowBackgroundAppearance::is_transp:
Whether the window's background lets content behind the window show
through, either directly, blurred, or via a system backdrop material.
doc_texts.fn:WindowBounds::centered:
Returns `WindowBounds::Windowed` with `size`, centered on the primary display.

Use [`Bounds::centered`] to center on another display.
doc_texts.fn:WindowBounds::get_bounds: Returns the bounds, whatever the state. For a maximized or fullscreen window these are the restore bounds.
doc_texts.fn:WindowButton::id:
Returns a stable element id for rendering this button.

Use the id to find the button's element in a titlebar. The ids are `"minimize"`,
`"maximize"` and `"close"`.
doc_texts.fn:WindowButtonLayout::format: Formats the layout back into a GNOME-style `button-layout` string.
doc_texts.fn:WindowButtonLayout::linux_default: Returns GPUI's fallback layout for Linux titlebars: minimize, maximize and close on the right.
doc_texts.fn:WindowButtonLayout::parse:
Parses a GNOME-style `button-layout` string such as `"close,minimize:maximize"`.

The text before the `:` is the left side and the text after it is the right side.
Names are `minimize`, `maximize` and `close`. Unknown names and repeated buttons
are skipped, and each side keeps at most [`MAX_BUTTONS_PER_SIDE`] buttons.

# Errors

Returns an error when the string names no valid buttons and at least one name is unknown.
doc_texts.fn:WindowHandle::entity:
Returns the root view as an [`Entity`], which you can clone and keep.

# Errors

Fails if the window is closed or if the root view's type no longer matches `V`.
doc_texts.fn:WindowHandle::is_active:
Returns whether the window is active, or `None` if it is closed or currently borrowed.

See [`Window::is_window_active`] for what counts as active.
doc_texts.fn:WindowHandle::new:
Creates a handle for the window with `id`, assuming its root view has type `V`.

This does not check the live root. Reads and updates fail if its type does not match `V`.
[`AnyWindowHandle::downcast`] checks the type recorded in that handle, which may be stale
after [`Window::replace_root`].
doc_texts.fn:WindowHandle::read:
Returns a reference to the root view for reading.

# Errors

Fails if the window is closed or if the root view's type no longer matches `V`.
doc_texts.fn:WindowHandle::read_with:
Passes the root view and the app to `read_with` and returns its result.

# Errors

Fails if the window is closed or if the root view's type no longer matches `V`.
doc_texts.fn:WindowHandle::root:
Returns the window's root view as an entity.

# Errors

Fails if the window is closed or if the root view's type no longer matches `V`.
doc_texts.fn:WindowHandle::update:
Updates the root view, and gives `update` the window and a context for the view.

Use it to change the view from outside the window. Calls to `notify` made in the update
redraw the window on the next frame.

# Errors

Fails if the window is closed or if the root view's type no longer matches `V`.
doc_texts.fn:WindowInsets::effective:
Returns, on each side, the larger of the system inset and the keyboard inset.

Content should stay clear of this area.
doc_texts.fn:WindowOptions::background_appearance:
Returns the window's background appearance for the current platform,
erased into the renderer-facing [`WindowBackgroundAppearance`].
doc_texts.fn:WindowOptions::new:
Returns window options with the platform's defaults: a focused, shown,
resizable, minimizable, movable normal window with a titlebar.
doc_texts.fn:WindowTextSystem::layout_inline:
Lays out text and atomic boxes together, the way an inline element flows in a paragraph.

Each box is an element that sits between characters, such as an icon or
a badge. Text wraps around the boxes. The result is cached like other
layouts.
doc_texts.fn:WindowTextSystem::layout_line:
Lays out one line of text and returns the backend's [`LineLayout`].

Most code should call [`Self::shape_line`] instead, which returns a
[`ShapedLine`] that you can paint. Use this only when you need the raw
layout. `text` must not contain newlines, and nothing checks this here.
doc_texts.fn:WindowTextSystem::new:
Creates a window text system with an empty layout cache on top of `text_system`.

GPUI creates one for each window. You don't need to call this yourself.
doc_texts.fn:WindowTextSystem::shape_text_with_opt:
Shapes a text document with explicit paragraph direction, alignment, and bidi options.

This is the lower-level form of [`Self::shape_text`]. Use it when text
must align within a width different from its wrap width, or must follow
a specific paragraph direction. The `Result` is currently always `Ok`.
doc_texts.fn:WindowVisibility::is_visible: Whether frames drawn for the window will be shown.
doc_texts.fn:__hash_text_macro_location_unstable_d:
Hashes the source location that the [`text`] macro records.

This is an implementation detail of the macro. It is not covered by semver
guarantees, so don't call it directly. Performance doesn't matter because it
runs only on short strings in const contexts.
doc_texts.fn:align_inline_boxes: Applies CSS-like vertical alignment to boxes after a text backend assigns them to lines.
doc_texts.fn:bench_metrics::AllocationCounter::new:
Creates a counter for `metric` over `scope`, failing when the binary's
global allocator is not a [`CountingAllocator`].
doc_texts.fn:bench_metrics::AllocationMetric::unit: The unit noun used in reports.
doc_texts.fn:bench_metrics::AllocationStats::live_: Bytes allocated and not yet freed.
doc_texts.fn:bench_metrics::BenchMeasurement::from:
Returns the measurement configured by [`BENCH_MEASUREMENT_ENV_VAR`].

* unset: Criterion analyzes wall time; every counter this machine
  supports is a secondary: process and calling-thread instructions,
  cycles, and their ratios where [`HardwareCounter`] has a backend
  (Linux, Apple Silicon); branch and cache misses on Linux; voluntary
  context switches and minor page faults from `getrusage`; heap
  allocations (process-wide and calling-thread) and allocated bytes
  where the binary installs [`CountingAllocator`]. Counters that fail to open are skipped with a
  note printed once.
* `wall-time`: wall time only, no counters.
* `instructions`: Criterion analyzes process-wide retired instructions.
* `foreground-instructions`: Criterion analyzes the benchmark thread's
  retired instructions, which excludes background and driver threads
  and is the tighter regression gate for frame cost.
* `allocations`: Criterion analyzes process-wide heap allocations.
* `foreground-allocations`: Criterion analyzes the benchmark thread's
  heap allocations, which excludes background workers' timing noise.

In the instruction and allocation modes wall time becomes a secondary,
and construction fails when the primary is unavailable so CI does not
silently measure something else.

[`Self::from_env`], exiting the process with an actionable message when
the requested measurement can't be used on this machine. For use in
`criterion_group!` `config` expressions, where there is nothing to
propagate an error to.
doc_texts.fn:bench_metrics::BenchMeasurement::name:
Names the primary so ratios can refer to it, e.g. `named("cycles")`
then `with_ratio("IPC", "instructions", "cycles")`. The primary is not
itself reported as a secondary; Criterion already reports it.
doc_texts.fn:bench_metrics::BenchMeasurement::new: Wraps the Criterion measurement whose values Criterion analyzes.
doc_texts.fn:bench_metrics::BenchMeasurement::with:
Adds `name` to reports as the ratio of two secondaries' totals over
each sample, e.g. `with_ratio("IPC", "instructions", "cycles")`.
Unknown names are reported as unavailable rather than failing, so a
ratio can be declared even when one input was skipped on this machine.

Adds a measurement taken alongside the primary on every sample.

`name` labels the metric in reports, e.g. `"instructions"`.
Secondaries start before and end after the primary, so their own
readout stays outside the primary's measured interval.
doc_texts.fn:bench_metrics::CountFormatter::new: Creates a formatter whose values are counts of `unit`, e.g. `"cycles"`.
doc_texts.fn:bench_metrics::HardwareEvent::unit: The unit noun used in reports.
doc_texts.fn:bench_metrics::MetricReport::discard_:
Discards secondary totals accumulated outside a measured interval,
e.g. by Criterion iterating a different benchmark on this thread.
doc_texts.fn:bench_metrics::MetricReport::is_empty: Returns whether any sample has been recorded.
doc_texts.fn:bench_metrics::MetricReport::iter:
`Bencher::iter` for plain Criterion benchmarks: runs `routine` under
Criterion's loop and records this sample's secondary metrics.
doc_texts.fn:bench_metrics::MetricReport::print: Prints one line per metric, each prefixed with `indent`, to stderr.
doc_texts.fn:bench_metrics::MetricReport::record_s:
Records the per-iteration value of every active secondary metric for
the Criterion sample that just finished, using the totals accumulated
since the previous call, and each ratio of those totals.

`iterations` is counted by the caller because Criterion's `Bencher`
does not expose it, and `iter_batched` with `BatchSize::PerIteration`
ends the measurement once per iteration rather than once per sample.
doc_texts.fn:bench_metrics::MetricReport::values:
Returns every recorded per-iteration value (or ratio) for `name`, in
sample order, for programmatic checks on top of the printed summary.
doc_texts.fn:bench_metrics::ResourceMetric::unit: The unit noun used in reports.
doc_texts.fn:bench_metrics::allocation_stats:
Returns the process's allocation totals, or `None` when this binary's
global allocator is not a [`CountingAllocator`]. Differences between two
calls give the allocations, bytes, and live-heap change of the code between
them, across every thread.
doc_texts.fn:bench_platform:
Returns a benchmark platform backed by this thread's shared dispatcher.

The platform uses this thread's shared multithreaded [`ThreadedDispatcher`], so
background work runs with production concurrency in real time. The dispatcher
is cached per thread and reused across benchmark invocations so worker and
timer threads persist for the whole process instead of being recreated for
every Criterion calibration pass.

Text is shaped with the provided platform text system. Benchmarks generated
by `#[gpui::bench]` use the current platform's text system, so text-heavy
benchmark measurements include production shaping and glyph rasterization.

`headless_renderer_factory` supplies a renderer for benchmark windows, e.g.
`gpui_platform::current_headless_renderer`. When present, scenes drawn by
benchmarks are rasterized through the real sprite atlas and submitted to
the GPU on present, so quad/sprite regressions show up in measurements.
When `None`, presenting discards the scene. Currently only macOS provides
a headless renderer (Metal), so GPU submission is excluded from benchmark
measurements on other platforms.
doc_texts.fn:blue: Opaque blue in [`Hsla`], at hue 240 degrees.
doc_texts.fn:calculate_seeds:
Returns the seeds a randomized `#[gpui::test]` or `#[gpui::bench]` runs with, in
order, and whether there is more than one.

With `$SEED` set, runs `$SEED..$SEED + iterations` and ignores `explicit_seeds`.
Otherwise runs `0..iterations` followed by `explicit_seeds`, except that the
default single iteration is dropped when explicit seeds are given.
`$ITERATIONS` overrides `iterations`.
Tests and benchmarks share this so that one `SEED` reproduces either.

This is intended for use by the `gpui::test` and `gpui::bench` macros and generally
should not be used directly.
doc_texts.fn:checkerboard:
Creates a checkerboard of squares in `color`, alternating with transparency.

`size` is the width and height of each square in logical pixels.
doc_texts.fn:colors::Colors::dark: Returns the colors for dark appearances.
doc_texts.fn:colors::Colors::for_appearance:
Returns [`Colors::light`] or [`Colors::dark`] for the window's [`WindowAppearance`].

The returned palette is a snapshot. Ask again after the window appearance changes.
doc_texts.fn:colors::Colors::get_global:
Returns the app-wide colors that [`App::init_colors`] set.

# Panics

Panics if [`App::init_colors`] has not been called.
doc_texts.fn:colors::Colors::light:
Returns the colors for light appearances.

This is the set that [`Colors::default`] returns.
doc_texts.fn:combine_highlights: Combine and merge the highlights and ranges in the two iterators.
doc_texts.fn:div:
Creates an empty [`Div`] element, which you style and fill with children.

Chain styling, event handlers and children onto the result. The element does nothing until it is returned from a
`render` method or passed to a parent.

# Example

```
# use gpui::{div, prelude::*, rgb};
let card = div()
    .flex()
    .flex_col()
    .gap_2()
    .p_3()
    .bg(rgb(0xffffff))
    .child("Title")
    .child("Body");
```
doc_texts.fn:fill: Returns a filled quad with no border and no corner radius.
doc_texts.fn:generate_list_of_all_registered_actio:
Generate a list of all the registered actions.
Useful for transforming the list of available actions into a
format suited for static analysis such as in validating keymaps, or
generating documentation.
doc_texts.fn:get_gamma_correction_ratios:
Returns the gamma correction ratios for subpixel text at `gamma`.

`gamma` is rounded to one decimal place and clamped to the range `1.0` to `2.2`.
doc_texts.fn:green: A dark, opaque green in [`Hsla`], at hue 120 degrees and lightness 0.25.
doc_texts.fn:guess_compositor:
Return which compositor we're guessing we'll use.
Does not attempt to connect to the given compositor.
doc_texts.fn:hash:
Hashes `data` with a fast, non-cryptographic hash, for use as a cache key within one process.

The value can change between builds, so don't store it or compare it across runs.
doc_texts.fn:hsla:
Creates an [`Hsla`] color from hue, saturation, lightness and alpha.

Every argument is a fraction from `0.0` to `1.0`; values outside that range are clamped.
The hue is a fraction of one turn, not degrees: `0.0` is red and `1.0 / 3.0` is green.
If you have a hue in degrees, use [`oklcha`] or convert it before calling this function.

# Examples

```
use gpui::{hsla, red};

assert_eq!(hsla(0.0, 1.0, 0.5, 1.0), red());
```
doc_texts.fn:hsla_to_rgba: Converts an [`Hsla`] color to sRGB [`Rgba`], keeping the alpha.
doc_texts.fn:http_client::BlockedHttpClient::new:
Creates a client that refuses every request. This is the same value as
[`Default::default`].
doc_texts.fn:http_client::FakeHttpClient::with_200: Returns a client that answers every request with `200 OK`.
doc_texts.fn:http_client::FakeHttpClient::with_404: Returns a client that answers every request with `404 Not Found`.
doc_texts.fn:image_cache:
Scopes an image cache to the [`img`](crate::img) elements below it.

Each image in the children uses the cache that `image_cache_provider` returns, instead of the
app-wide cache. Pass an `Entity` of an [`ImageCache`] to share one cache, or [`retain_all`] to get
a cache that lives with this element's state. The provider is called on every layout and paint.

Only [`crate::ImageSource::Resource`] sources use the cache. See [`crate::Img::image_cache`].

# Examples

```
# use gpui::*;
let gallery = image_cache(retain_all("gallery")).children((0..3).map(|ix| {
    img(format!("https://example.com/photos/{ix}.jpg"))
        .size(px(120.))
        .into_any_element()
}));
```
doc_texts.fn:img:
Creates an image element that draws `source`.

Building the element does no work. The image starts loading the first time the element is laid
out, on a background thread. Until it loads, the element has no size unless you set one, and it
draws nothing unless you set a [`StyledImage::with_loading`] placeholder. Once the image loads,
the element takes the image's natural size. If you set only a width or only a height, the other
dimension follows the aspect ratio.

`source` is anything that converts into an [`ImageSource`]. That type explains how a string is
read.

Loaded images are cached, so a second `img` with the same source reuses the decoded image. See
the [images guide](crate::_documentation::guides::images_and_assets) for the cache rules, and
[`crate::image_cache`] to scope them to a group of images.

# Examples

```
# use gpui::*;
let remote = img("https://example.com/avatar.png");
let bundled = img("images/logo.png");
let local = img(std::path::PathBuf::from("assets/banner.jpg"));
```
doc_texts.fn:is_no_action: Returns whether `action` is a [`NoAction`].
doc_texts.fn:is_paragraph_separator:
Returns whether `character` separates Unicode text paragraphs.

Line separator (`U+2028`) is a hard line break within the current paragraph. Consumers are
responsible for treating a CRLF pair as one paragraph separator.
doc_texts.fn:is_unbind: Returns whether `action` is an [`Unbind`].
doc_texts.fn:linear_color_stop:
Creates a color stop of `color` at `percentage` along a gradient line.

`percentage` is in the range `0.0` (the start of the gradient) to `1.0` (the end).
doc_texts.fn:oklcha:
Creates an [`Oklcha`](palette::Oklcha) color from lightness, chroma, hue and alpha.

Unlike [`hsla`], the arguments are not clamped. The hue is in degrees. Use this for

doc_texts.fn:profiler::journal::FrameSnapshot::occ:
Total foreground time occupied within the interval: the union of the
recorded events' spans (clamped to the interval, so nested work like an
action inside an input dispatch is not double counted) plus the folded

doc_texts.fn:rgb:
Creates an opaque [`Rgba`] color from a `0xRRGGBB` hex number.

The highest byte of `hex` is ignored, and the alpha is `1.0`. Use [`rgba`] for a color
with alpha.

# Examples

```
use gpui::rgb;

assert_eq!(rgb(0xffffff).alpha, 1.0);
```
doc_texts.fn:rgb_to_hsla:
Converts an sRGB [`Rgba`] color to [`Hsla`], keeping the alpha.

Use it at an API boundary that stores [`Hsla`], such as [`Styled::bg`](crate::Styled::bg),
when the value you have is [`Rgba`].

Creates a solid background of `color`.

This is the same as converting `color` with `.into()`.

The function reads and writes only the first four bytes of `color`. Bytes after the
first pixel are left unchanged.

# Panics

Panics if `color` has fewer than four bytes.
doc_texts.fn:test::apply_seed_to_proptest_config:
Sets the RNG seed of a proptest config from `SEED`, or from `0` when it's unset.

The same variable then controls both the scheduler seed and proptest's case
generation. The `#[gpui::property_test]` macro uses this helper.

If `SEED` is not a `u64`, this function uses `0`. [`seed_strategy`] panics for
the same input.
doc_texts.fn:test::observe:
Returns a stream that yields `()` each time `entity` notifies.

Dropping the returned stream unsubscribes. For a stream that also ends when the
entity is released, use [`TestAppContext::notifications`].
doc_texts.fn:test::run_test:
Runs `test_fn` for each seed, retrying a failing seed up to `max_retries` times.

The `#[gpui::test]` macro calls this function. It chooses seeds from the
macro's arguments and these environment variables:

- `ITERATIONS=n` overrides the number of iterations.
- `SEED=n` runs only seed `n`, or, with more than one iteration, the seeds
  `n` to `n + iterations - 1`. It replaces `explicit_seeds`.

When more than one seed runs, each seed is printed before it runs, and a
failing seed is printed when its last attempt fails. After the last failure,
`on_fail_fn` runs, then the panic is re-raised.
doc_texts.fn:test::run_test_once:
Runs `test_fn` once on a dispatcher for `seed`, and returns its result.

Unlike [`run_test`], this runs once without retries, and `test_fn` can be an
`FnOnce`. The `#[gpui::property_test]` macro uses it. If `test_fn` panics,
the panic is re-raised after the dispatcher is dropped.
doc_texts.fn:test::seed_strategy:
Returns a proptest strategy for scheduler seeds.

When `SEED` is set, the strategy always produces that value. Otherwise it
produces any `u64`. Seeds are not shrunk, so a failing seed is replayed as
recorded rather than replaced with a smaller seed.
This is for the `#[gpui::property_test]` macro.

# Panics

Panics if `SEED` is set but isn't a `u64`.
doc_texts.fn:utf16_to_utf8_offset:
Converts a UTF-16 code-unit offset into a UTF-8 byte offset.

The reverse of [`utf8_to_utf16_offset`]. Use it on ranges that the platform
sends, before slicing a `String`. An offset past the end returns the UTF-8
length of `text`. An offset inside a surrogate pair returns the offset of the
end of that character.

# Examples

```
use gpui::utf16_to_utf8_offset;

assert_eq!(utf16_to_utf8_offset("A😀B", 3), 5);
assert_eq!(utf16_to_utf8_offset("A😀B", 100), 6);
```

doc_texts.fn:AnyWeakEntity::assert_released:
Asserts that the entity referenced by this weak handle has been fully released.

# Example

```ignore
let entity = cx.new(|_| MyEntity::new());
let weak = entity.downgrade();
drop(entity);

// Verify the entity was released
weak.assert_released();
```

# Debugging Leaks

If this method panics due to leaked handles, set the `LEAK_BACKTRACE` environment
variable to see where the leaked handles were allocated:

```bash
LEAK_BACKTRACE=1 cargo test my_test
```

# Panics

- Panics if any strong handles to the entity are still alive.
- Panics if the entity was recently dropped but cleanup hasn't completed yet
  (resources are retained until the end of the effect cycle).

doc_texts.fn:DevicePixels::to_bytes:
Converts the `DevicePixels` value to the number of bytes needed to represent it in memory.

This function is useful when working with graphical data that needs to be stored in a buffer,
such as images or framebuffers, where each pixel may be represented by a specific number of bytes.

# Arguments

* `bytes_per_pixel` - The number of bytes used to represent a single pixel.

# Returns

The number of bytes required to represent the `DevicePixels` value in memory.

# Examples

```
# use gpui::DevicePixels;
let pixels = DevicePixels(10); // 10 device pixels
let bytes_per_pixel = 4; // Assume each pixel is represented by 4 bytes (e.g., RGBA)
let total_bytes = pixels.to_bytes(bytes_per_pixel);
assert_eq!(total_bytes, 40); // 10 pixels * 4 bytes/pixel = 40 bytes
```

doc_texts.fn:Edges::map:
Applies a function to each field of the `Edges`, producing a new `Edges<U>`.

This method allows for converting an `Edges<T>` to an `Edges<U>` by specifying a closure
that defines how to convert between the two types. The closure is applied to each field
(`top`, `right`, `bottom`, `left`), resulting in new edges of the desired type.

# Arguments

* `f` - A closure that takes a reference to a value of type `T` and returns a value of type `U`.

# Returns

Returns a new `Edges<U>` with each field mapped by the provided function.

# Examples

```
# use gpui::Edges;
let edges = Edges { top: 10, right: 20, bottom: 30, left: 40 };
let edges_float = edges.map(|&value| value as f32 * 1.1);
assert_eq!(edges_float, Edges { top: 11.0, right: 22.0, bottom: 33.0, left: 44.0 });
```

doc_texts.fn:Hitbox::is_hovered:
Checks if the hitbox is currently hovered. Except when handling `ScrollWheelEvent`, this is
typically what you want when determining whether to handle mouse events or paint hover
styles.

This can return `false` even when the hitbox contains the mouse, if a hitbox in front of
this sets `HitboxBehavior::BlockMouse` (`InteractiveElement::occlude`) or
`HitboxBehavior::BlockMouseExceptScroll` (`InteractiveElement::block_mouse_except_scroll`).

Handling of `ScrollWheelEvent` should typically use `should_handle_scroll` instead.
Concretely, this is due to use-cases like overlays that cause the elements under to be
non-interactive while still allowing scrolling. More abstractly, this is because
`is_hovered` is about element interactions directly under the mouse - mouse moves, clicks,
hover styling, etc. In contrast, scrolling is about finding the current outer scrollable
container.

This can return `false` even when the hitbox contains the mouse, if a hitbox in front of
this sets `HitboxBehavior::BlockMouse` (`InteractiveElement::occlude`).

doc_texts.fn:Hsla::blend:
Blends `other` on top of `self` based on `other`'s alpha value. The resulting color is a combination of `self`'s and `other`'s colors.

If `other`'s alpha value is 1.0 or greater, `other` color is fully opaque, thus `other` is returned as the output color.
If `other`'s alpha value is 0.0 or less, `other` color is fully transparent, thus `self` is returned as the output color.
Else, the output color is calculated as a blend of `self` and `other` based on their weighted alpha values.

Assumptions:
- Alpha values are contained in the range [0, 1], with 1 as fully opaque and 0 as fully transparent.
- The relative contributions of `self` and `other` is based on `self`'s alpha value (`self.a`) and `other`'s  alpha value (`other.a`), `self` contributing `self.a * (1.0 - other.a)` and `other` contributing its own alpha value.
- RGB color components are contained in the range [0, 1].
- If `self` and `other` colors are out of the valid range, the blend operation's output and behavior is undefined.

doc_texts.fn:KeyBindingContextPredicate::parse:
Parse a string in the same format as the keymap's context field.

A basic equivalence check against a set of identifiers can performed by
simply writing a string:

`StatusBar` -> A predicate that will match a context with the identifier `StatusBar`

You can also specify a key-value pair:

`mode == visible` -> A predicate that will match a context with the key `mode`
                     with the value `visible`

And a logical operations combining these two checks:

`StatusBar && mode == visible` -> A predicate that will match a context with the
                                  identifier `StatusBar` and the key `mode`
                                  with the value `visible`


There is also a special child `>` operator that will match a predicate that is
below another predicate:

`StatusBar > mode == visible` -> A predicate that will match a context identifier `StatusBar`
                                 and a child context that has the key `mode` with the
                                 value `visible`

This syntax supports `!=`, `||` and `&&` as logical operators.
You can also preface an operation or check with a `!` to negate it.

doc_texts.fn:Keymap::bindings_for_input:
Returns a list of bindings that match the given input, and a boolean indicating whether or
not more bindings might match if the input was longer. Bindings are returned in precedence
order (higher precedence first, reverse of the order they were added to the keymap).

Precedence is defined by the depth in the tree (matches on the Editor take precedence over
matches on the Pane, then the Workspace, etc.). Bindings with no context are treated as the
same as the deepest context.

In the case of multiple bindings at the same depth, the ones added to the keymap later take
precedence. User bindings are added after built-in bindings so that they take precedence.

If a user has disabled a binding with `"x": null` it will not be returned. Disabled bindings
are evaluated with the same precedence rules so you can disable a rule in a given context
only.

doc_texts.fn:Keystroke::should_match:
When matching a key we cannot know whether the user intended to type
the key_char or the key itself. On some non-US keyboards keys we use in our
bindings are behind option (for example `$` is typed `alt-ç` on a Czech keyboard),
and on some keyboards the IME handler converts a sequence of keys into a
specific character (for example `"` is typed as `" space` on a brazilian keyboard).

This method assumes that `self` was typed and `target' is in the keymap, and checks
both possibilities for self against the target.

doc_texts.fn:UniformListScrollHandle::scroll_to_it:
Scroll the list so that the given item index is visible.

This uses non-strict scrolling: if the item is already fully visible, no scrolling occurs.
If the item is out of view, it scrolls the minimum amount to bring it into view according
to the strategy.

Scroll the list so that the given item index is at scroll strategy position.

This uses strict scrolling: the item will always be scrolled to match the strategy position,
even if it's already visible. Use this when you need precise positioning.

Scroll the list so that the given item index is at the exact scroll strategy position with an offset.

This uses strict scrolling: the item will always be scrolled to match the strategy position,
even if it's already visible.

The offset parameter shrinks the effective viewport by the specified number of items
from the corresponding edge, then applies the scroll strategy within that reduced viewport:
- `ScrollStrategy::Top`: Shrinks from top, positions item at the new top
- `ScrollStrategy::Center`: Shrinks from top, centers item in the reduced viewport
- `ScrollStrategy::Bottom`: Shrinks from bottom, positions item at the new bottom

Scroll the list to the given item index with an offset in number of items.

This uses non-strict scrolling: if the item is already visible within the offset region,
no scrolling occurs.
