doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::exit_media_picture: Exit browser picture-in-picture when an element is currently active.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::favicons:
Read favicon candidates from the current document.

This mirrors native desktop tab chrome that reacts to hosted page icons.
It returns resolved URLs from `<link rel="icon">`, shortcut icons,
Apple touch icons, and mask icons in document order. It does not fetch
or decode image bytes.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::find_text:
Find text in the target WebView and move browser selection to the match.

The callback receives `Ok(true)` when the browser found and selected a
match, `Ok(false)` when no match was found, or `Err(...)` when script
execution failed.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::find_text_result:
Find text and return a richer result for native find bars.

The browser still owns the active selection via `window.find(...)`, while
Kael also counts DOM text matches in the current document so apps can
show result counts without custom page JavaScript. Cross-origin frames
and backend-native find match details are not included.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::focus: Move focus into the target WebView when the active backend supports it.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::focus_parent: Move focus from the target WebView back to the parent window.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::focus_selector:
Focus the first element matching a CSS selector in the target WebView.

This is a small browser-island automation helper for native chrome,
tests, and AI agents. It avoids repeating raw `querySelector(...)`
snippets when an app needs to focus a hosted input, editor, or control
before sending edit commands.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::go_back: Navigate the target WebView backward if possible.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::go_forward: Navigate the target WebView forward if possible.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::id: Return the WebView element id this controller targets.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::insert_css:
Insert or replace a named runtime CSS block in the target WebView.

This mirrors browser-runtime `hosted CSS injection(...)` workflows for hosted
widgets and browser-media islands, while using an app-chosen key so CSS
can be updated or removed deterministically later.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::insert_text:
Insert text into the focused browser editor or form control.

This mirrors browser-runtime `hosted page controller.insertText(...)` for command palettes,
AI agents, test automation, and native editor chrome that need to type
into hosted inputs or contenteditable documents without bespoke page
JavaScript. The callback receives whether the browser accepted or
emulated the insertion.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::is_devtools_open: Read whether WebView developer tools are open when the active backend supports it.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::is_loading:
Read whether the target WebView document is still loading.

This mirrors the common browser-runtime `hosted loading query` workflow for
app-owned loading indicators and route guards. It is based on
`document.readyState !== "complete"` rather than backend-native network
activity counters.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::load_html: Load an HTML string into the target WebView.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::media_command:
Run a media command on the first matching browser media element.

The selector may point at an `<audio>`, `<video>`, or descendant element.
This is the selector-scoped counterpart to broad helpers such as
[`Self::play_media`] and [`Self::pause_media`].
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::media_state:
Read state for every browser media element in the target WebView.

This snapshots current `<audio>` and `<video>` elements so native chrome
can drive WebView-hosted players without hand-written state scraping.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::mute_media: Mute every browser media element in the target WebView.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::navigate: Navigate the target WebView to a new URL.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::navigate_with_head: Navigate the target WebView to a new URL with additional request headers.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::new: Create a controller for a WebView element id.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::open_devtools:
Open WebView developer tools when the active backend supports it.

Devtools are available in debug builds on Wry-backed WebViews. Release
builds require a backend/devtools feature that may not be enabled.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::paste: Paste into the focused editable browser element when the backend allows it.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::pause_media:
Pause every browser media element in the target WebView.

This is useful for WebView-hosted video/audio fallbacks, docs widgets,
calls, and other browser-media islands when the native app needs to
pause playback during navigation, window hiding, or route changes.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::play_media:
Play every browser media element in the target WebView.

Browser autoplay and user-gesture policies still apply. Rejected
`play()` promises are intentionally swallowed so a single blocked or
unsupported element does not break the rest of the page script.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::post_bridge_messag: Post a typed bridge envelope into the target WebView.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::post_message: Post a structured message into the target WebView.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::print: Open the platform print dialog for the target WebView content.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::redo: Redo the last undone browser editing action in the target WebView.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::remove_attribute: Remove an attribute from the first element matching a selector.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::remove_class: Remove a CSS class from the first element matching a selector.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::remove_inserted_cs: Remove a named runtime CSS block inserted with [`Self::insert_css`].
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::remove_media_text_:
Remove matching browser text-track elements from the first matching media element.

The media selector may point at an `<audio>`, `<video>`, or descendant
element. The track selector matches a track element's id, label, srclang,
kind, src, or zero-based index.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::remove_storage_ite: Remove one key from the current document's browser Web Storage.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::remove_style_prope: Remove one inline CSS property from the first element matching a selector.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::request_media_full:
Request browser fullscreen for the first available video or media element.

Browser user-gesture and embedding policies still apply. Rejected
fullscreen promises are swallowed so unsupported pages do not break app
script execution.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::request_media_pict:
Request picture-in-picture for the first video element that supports it.

Browser support, page attributes, permissions, and user-gesture policies
still apply. Rejected promises are swallowed.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::reset_form:
Reset the first form matching or containing a CSS selector.

The selector may point at a `<form>` or at a control inside a form. Kael
calls the browser's normal `form.reset()` path so reset events and
default values are handled by the hosted document.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::scroll_by: Scroll the current top document by a relative delta in CSS pixels.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::scroll_selector_in:
Scroll the first matching top-document element into view.

Returns `Ok(None)` when the selector is invalid or no element matches.
Shadow roots and cross-origin frames remain browser-owned.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::scroll_to: Scroll the current top document to an absolute position in CSS pixels.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::seek_media_secs: Seek every browser media element in the target WebView to a time in seconds.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::select_all: Select all editable/browser document content in the target WebView.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::select_media_text_:
Select matching browser text tracks and disable the rest.

The selector matches a track's id, label, language, or zero-based index
string across all current WebView `<audio>` and `<video>` elements.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::selected_html:
Read the current browser selection as HTML.

This is useful for rich-editor context menus, inspectors, and export
flows. Normal document selections are serialized from cloned selection
ranges; focused `<input>` / `<textarea>` selections are returned as
escaped text because those controls do not expose rich HTML fragments.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::selected_text:
Read the current browser selection as text.

This mirrors browser-runtime `hosted selected-text query` for context menus,
inspectors, find bars, and hosted editor chrome. It handles both normal
document selections and focused `<input>` / `<textarea>` selection ranges.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::set_attribute:
Set an attribute on the first element matching a selector.

Use this for simple hosted-widget state such as `aria-*`, `data-*`,
`hidden`, `src`, or `controls`. Page script and browser validation still
own the final behavior of sensitive attributes.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::set_cookie: Set a cookie in this WebView profile.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::set_form_value:
Set the value of the first form control matching a CSS selector.

This covers common hosted form automation for inputs, textareas,
selects, checkboxes, radios, and contenteditable elements. It dispatches
normal `input` and `change` events so page listeners can react as if the
user edited the control.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::set_media_muted:
Mute or unmute every browser media element in the target WebView.

This changes the `muted` property on current `<audio>` and `<video>`
elements. New media elements created by the page should still be managed
by page code or an injected script.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::set_media_options:
Apply common browser media properties to the first matching element.

The selector may point at an `<audio>`, `<video>`, or descendant element.
Kael sets normal media playback surface properties/attributes such as controls,
loop, autoplay, muted, playsinline, poster, preload, controlslist, and
disablePictureInPicture where the browser supports them.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::set_media_playback:
Set the playback rate on every browser media element in the target WebView.

Values below zero are clamped to `0.0`; individual browsers may still
reject rates outside their supported media playback range.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::set_media_source:
Set the source URL for the first matching browser media element.

The selector may point at an `<audio>`, `<video>`, or nested `<source>`
element. Kael updates the element's `src` and calls the browser's normal
`load()` path so metadata, buffering, and media events are owned by the
embedded engine.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::set_media_volume:
Set the volume on every browser media element in the target WebView.

Values are clamped to the browser media element range of `0.0..=1.0`.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::set_storage_item: Set one key in the current document's browser Web Storage.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::set_style_property:
Set one inline CSS property on the first element matching a selector.

The property name is passed to `style.setProperty(...)`, so CSS custom
properties are allowed. This intentionally targets inline styles for
narrow app/agent customization; use [`Self::insert_css`] for larger
stylesheet-level changes.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::set_zoom_factor: Set the target WebView's browser zoom factor.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::stop_finding: Clear the active browser find selection in the target WebView.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::stop_finding_with_:
Stop finding with an native desktop selection action.

This mirrors `hosted find stop(action)`: `ClearSelection`
removes the current browser selection, `KeepSelection` leaves it alone,
and `ActivateSelection` focuses/scrolls the selected match where browser
APIs allow it.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::stop_loading:
Stop loading resources in the target WebView.

This mirrors browser-runtime `hosted load stop` through the browser's
standard `window.stop()` primitive so it works across supported
WebView backends.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::storage_snapshot:
Read `localStorage` and `sessionStorage` from the current document.

This is an on-demand companion to [`WebViewOptions::storage_bridge`].
Browser origin/security rules still apply; blocked areas are returned
with `available: false` and an error string instead of being treated as
a transport failure.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::submit_form:
Submit the first form matching or containing a CSS selector.

The selector may point at a `<form>` or at a control inside a form. Kael
uses the browser's `requestSubmit()` path when available so normal
validation and submit handlers run.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::title:
Read the current `document.title` from the target WebView.

This mirrors browser-runtime `hosted title query` for tab labels,
breadcrumbs, inspectors, and restore flows that need the title on
demand rather than only through title-change events.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::toggle_class:
Toggle a CSS class on the first element matching a selector.

Pass `Some(true)` or `Some(false)` to force the final state, or `None`
to invert the current class state.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::trigger_download:
Ask the hosted document to trigger a browser download for a URL.

This is designed for native context menus and agents that receive a
`linkHref`, `imageSrc`, or `mediaSrc` from Kael's WebView bridges and
need a "Save..." command without taking over networking. The URL is
resolved against the current document and the filename is passed as the
browser `<a download>` hint. Browser origin rules, response headers,
and Kael's download policy handlers still decide whether and where the
download actually completes.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::undo: Undo the last browser editing action in the target WebView.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::unmute_media: Unmute every browser media element in the target WebView.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::url: Read the current URL reported by this WebView.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::user_agent:
Read the effective browser user agent from the target WebView.

This mirrors browser-runtime `hosted user-agent query` for diagnostics,
hosted service compatibility checks, and verifying custom
[`WebViewOptions::user_agent`] configuration.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewController::viewport_snapshot: Read the current top-document viewport and scroll state.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewCookie::http_only: Mark whether the cookie should be hidden from page JavaScript.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewCookie::new: Create a cookie with a name and value.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewCookie::secure: Mark whether the cookie requires a secure transport.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewDialogEvent::from_bridge_messa: Parse a bridge message into a typed dialog event when the kind matches.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewDialogEvent::from_payload: Parse a bridge payload into a typed dialog event.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewDomImageCaptureOptions::height: Set the output height in CSS pixels.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewDomImageCaptureOptions::max_pi: Set the maximum output pixel area.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewDomImageCaptureOptions::size: Set the output size in CSS pixels.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewDomImageCaptureOptions::width: Set the output width in CSS pixels.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewFaviconEvent::from_bridge_mess: Parse a bridge message into a typed favicon event when the kind matches.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewFaviconEvent::from_payload: Parse a bridge payload into a typed favicon event.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewFileInputEvent::from_bridge_me: Parse a bridge message into a typed file-input event when the kind matches.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewFileInputEvent::from_payload: Parse a bridge payload into a typed file-input event.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewFindEvent::from_bridge_message: Parse a bridge message into a typed find event when the kind matches.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewFindEvent::from_payload: Parse a bridge payload into a typed find event.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewFindOptions::backward: Search backward, wrapping around the document.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewFindOptions::forward: Search forward, wrapping around the document.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewFindOptions::search_in_frames: Enable or disable searching frames where the browser supports it.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewFindOptions::whole_word: Enable or disable whole-word matching where the browser supports it.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewFormEvent::from_bridge_message: Parse a bridge message into a typed form event when the kind matches.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewFormEvent::from_payload: Parse a bridge payload into a typed form event.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewKeyboardEvent::from_bridge_mes: Parse a bridge message into a typed keyboard event when the kind matches.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewKeyboardEvent::from_payload: Parse a bridge payload into a typed keyboard event.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewLifecycleEvent::from_bridge_me: Parse a bridge message into a typed lifecycle event when the kind matches.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewLifecycleEvent::from_payload: Parse a bridge payload into a typed lifecycle event.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewLocationEvent::from_bridge_mes: Parse a bridge message into a typed location event when the kind matches.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewLocationEvent::from_payload: Parse a bridge payload into a typed location event.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewMediaElementOptions::autoplay: Set whether the browser autoplay property is enabled.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewMediaElementOptions::controls: Set whether browser-provided media controls are visible.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewMediaElementOptions::loop_enab: Set whether browser loop behavior is enabled.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewMediaElementOptions::muted: Set whether the media element is muted.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewMediaElementOptions::plays_inl: Set whether inline video playback is requested.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewMediaElementOptions::poster: Set the poster image URL for video elements.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewMediaEvent::from_bridge_messag: Parse a bridge message into a typed media event when the kind matches.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewMediaEvent::from_payload: Parse a bridge payload into a typed media event.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewMediaFrameCaptureOptions::heig: Set the output height in pixels.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewMediaFrameCaptureOptions::qual: Set encoder quality for lossy formats.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewMediaFrameCaptureOptions::size: Set the output size in pixels.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewMediaFrameCaptureOptions::widt: Set the output width in pixels.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewMediaTextTrackOptions::default: Mark this track as the browser default.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewMediaTextTrackOptions::label: Set the user-facing label.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewMediaTextTrackOptions::webvtt: Create a WebVTT subtitles track from a URL or data URL.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewNativePermissionRequest::has_e: Whether the origin belongs to the frame that actually requested access.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewNativePermissionRequest::is_ma: Whether the engine positively identified the main frame.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewNativePermissionRequest::kind_: Construct a conservative request when an engine exposes only the kind.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewNetworkEvent::from_bridge_mess: Parse a bridge message into a typed network event when the kind matches.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewNetworkEvent::from_payload: Parse a bridge payload into a typed network event.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::allow_downloads: Allow WebView downloads to use the backend/browser default destination.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::allow_navigation_sche:
Allow navigation only to the supplied URL schemes.

This is intentionally simple: use [`WebViewOptions::on_navigate`] when
hostnames, paths, OAuth redirect URLs, or app-specific policies matter.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::allow_new_windows: Let the platform WebView backend handle new-window requests.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::auth_flow: Persistent profile preset for auth, OAuth, SSO, and hosted account flows.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::background_color: Set the native WebView background color.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::background_color_requ: Return the requested native WebView background color, if one was configured.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::block_drag_drop: Block browser/OS default handling for file drops inside the WebView.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::browser_iframe_policy:
Configure the iframe security boundary used when this WebView is built
as part of a Kael browser application.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::clear_html: Clear the initial HTML document configured for this WebView.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::clear_request_headers: Remove request headers from the WebView's initial URL load.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::clipboard_access: Enable JavaScript clipboard access for pages that use browser clipboard APIs.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::clipboard_access_enab: Enable or disable JavaScript clipboard access where the backend supports it.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::clipboard_access_requ: Return whether JavaScript clipboard access is requested.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::clipboard_event_bridg:
Inject the standard bridge plus browser clipboard event forwarding.

The injected script posts [`WebViewBridgeMessage`] values with the given
kind for hosted `copy`, `cut`, and `paste` events. This is an explicit
opt-in event observer and does not prevent browser defaults.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::console_bridge:
Inject the standard bridge plus browser console forwarding.

The injected script preserves normal console behavior while posting
[`WebViewBridgeMessage`] values with the given kind for `console.*`,
`error`, and `unhandledrejection` events in the hosted page.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::context_menu_bridge:
Inject the standard bridge plus browser context-menu forwarding.

The injected script prevents the browser default context menu and posts
[`WebViewBridgeMessage`] values with the given kind for right-click /
secondary-click events inside WebView content.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::deny_downloads: Deny native WebView downloads and remove browser iframe download permission.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::devtools: Enable WebView developer tools for development.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::devtools_enabled: Enable or disable WebView developer tools.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::devtools_requested: Return whether developer tools are requested for this WebView.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::dialog_bridge:
Inject the standard bridge plus browser dialog observability.

The injected script posts [`WebViewBridgeMessage`] values with the given
kind for `alert`, `confirm`, `prompt`, and `beforeunload` activity while
preserving browser dialog behavior.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::drag_drop_handler_req: Return whether a WebView drag/drop handler is configured.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::embedded_widget: Ephemeral preset for payments, embeds, and third-party widgets.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::favicon_bridge:
Inject the standard bridge plus browser favicon change forwarding.

The injected script posts [`WebViewBridgeMessage`] values with the given
kind whenever favicon link candidates in the hosted document change.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::file_input_bridge:
Inject the standard bridge plus browser file-input selection forwarding.

The injected script posts [`WebViewBridgeMessage`] values with the given
kind whenever hosted `<input type="file">` controls change. Payloads
include browser-exposed file metadata, not local filesystem paths.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::find_result_bridge:
Inject the standard bridge plus native desktop find-result forwarding.

The injected script wraps `window.find(...)` and posts
[`WebViewBridgeMessage`] values with the given kind after browser find
operations run. Use this for native find bars that need `found-in-page`
style updates without polling JavaScript.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::focused: Request that this WebView receive focus when created.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::focused_enabled: Enable or disable initial WebView focus when the backend supports it.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::focused_requested: Return an explicit initial-focus override, if one was requested.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::form_bridge:
Inject the standard bridge plus browser form activity forwarding.

The injected script posts [`WebViewBridgeMessage`] values with the given
kind for hosted submit, reset, change, and input events. Password and
file input values are intentionally omitted from payloads.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::general_autofill_disa: Disable browser-level general autofill where the backend supports it.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::general_autofill_enab: Enable or disable browser-level general autofill where the backend supports it.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::general_autofill_requ: Return an explicit general-autofill override, if one was requested.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::has_persistent_storag: Return whether these options use persistent storage.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::html: Load an HTML string as the WebView's initial document when no URL is supplied.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::html_requested: Return HTML configured for the WebView's initial document.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::inject_css: Inject CSS into each loaded page.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::inject_javascript: Inject JavaScript into each loaded page.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::javascript_disabled: Disable JavaScript for untrusted or static browser content.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::javascript_disabled_e: Enable or disable JavaScript execution where the backend supports it.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::javascript_disabled_r: Return whether JavaScript execution is disabled for this WebView.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::keyboard_event_bridge:
Inject the standard bridge plus browser keyboard/input forwarding.

This observes `keydown`, `keyup`, and `beforeinput` events inside hosted
content for native shortcut chrome, test harnesses, and agent
observability.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::lifecycle_bridge:
Inject the standard bridge plus browser lifecycle/focus forwarding.

The injected script posts [`WebViewBridgeMessage`] values with the given
kind for hosted page focus, blur, visibility, page show/hide, and
fullscreen changes.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::location_bridge:
Inject the standard bridge plus same-document location forwarding.

This observes browser route changes inside hosted content and posts
[`WebViewBridgeMessage`] values with the given kind for native tabs,
breadcrumbs, app-owned Back/Forward buttons, and agent observability.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::media_autoplay: Allow all WebView media to autoplay without user interaction.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::media_autoplay_enable: Enable or disable WebView media autoplay without user interaction.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::media_autoplay_reques: Return an explicit media-autoplay override, if one was requested.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::media_event_bridge:
Inject the standard bridge plus browser media event forwarding.

The injected script posts `WebViewBridgeMessage` values with the given
kind whenever current or future `<audio>` / `<video>` elements emit
common playback, timing, volume, buffering, or error events.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::native_permission_pol:
Set the native browser-engine permission policy.

Unlike [`Self::on_permission_request`], this runs at the native WebView
permission boundary and can grant or deny engine requests that never
pass through the injected JavaScript preflight. The closure must be
thread-safe because WebView2 may invoke it outside Kael's render stack.
WKWebView currently exposes camera and microphone capture here; Windows
and Linux expose the permission categories supported by their engines.
The compatibility form receives only the permission kind. Prefer
[`Self::native_permission_request_policy`] when an origin or user gesture
is part of the security decision.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::native_permission_req:
Set an origin- and frame-aware native browser-engine permission policy.

macOS supplies the requesting security origin and main/subframe state.
WebView2 supplies the requesting origin and user-gesture state, while
WebKitGTK currently supplies a top-level origin approximation. Inspect
[`WebViewNativePermissionRequest::has_exact_origin`] and `frame` before
granting sensitive capabilities to content that can embed frames.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::navigation_state_brid:
Inject same-document navigation state tracking for app-owned pages.

This tracks `pushState`, `replaceState`, and `popstate` entries created
after injection and publishes `window.__kaelNavigationState` for
[`WebViewController::can_go_forward`].
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::network_bridge:
Inject the standard bridge plus hosted fetch/XHR network observability.

The injected script posts [`WebViewBridgeMessage`] values with the given
kind when hosted JavaScript `fetch` and `XMLHttpRequest` calls complete,
error, abort, or time out. This does not intercept or rewrite requests.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::on_bridge_message: Register a handler for typed WebView bridge envelopes.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::on_clipboard_event:
Inject clipboard event forwarding and handle typed clipboard events.

Use this when hosted rich editors, tests, or agents need to observe
copy/cut/paste activity and browser-exposed clipboard data.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::on_console_message:
Inject browser console forwarding and handle typed console events.

Use this for app-owned diagnostics, automated tests, hosted-widget
health checks, and AI-agent observability without opening browser
devtools.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::on_context_menu:
Inject browser context-menu forwarding and handle typed context events.

Use this when native chrome should build an app menu from the clicked
page context, such as selected text, links, images, media, or editable
fields inside hosted browser content.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::on_dialog_event:
Inject browser dialog forwarding and handle typed dialog events.

Use this when native diagnostics, tests, or agents should observe hosted
blocking dialogs and unload prompts. This does not replace the browser's
synchronous dialog result path.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::on_document_title_cha: Register a handler fired when the WebView document title changes.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::on_download_completed: Register a handler fired when a WebView download completes or fails.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::on_download_started:
Register a handler that can allow, deny, or redirect downloads.

This is a native WebView policy callback. Browser iframe parents cannot
synchronously choose a destination or reliably observe completion; use
[`Self::allow_downloads`] or [`Self::deny_downloads`] to configure the
sandbox permission there.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::on_drag_drop:
Register a handler for file drag/drop events inside the WebView.

Return [`WebViewDragDropPolicy::BlockBrowserDefault`] to prevent the
embedded browser from handling the event, or
[`WebViewDragDropPolicy::AllowBrowserDefault`] to preserve browser
behavior such as dropping files onto `<input type="file">`.

On Windows, registering this handler replaces WebView2's drag/drop
controller and disables the page's HTML Drag and Drop APIs. WebView2
cannot honor `AllowBrowserDefault` after interception is enabled. Leave
this handler unset when the hosted page needs native HTML drag/drop.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::on_favicon_changed:
Inject browser favicon forwarding and handle typed favicon events.

Use this when native tabs, breadcrumbs, or history UI should react to
hosted page icon changes without polling.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::on_file_input_event:
Inject file-input forwarding and handle typed file-input events.

Use this when native upload chrome, tests, or agents need to observe
browser file selections inside hosted forms without custom page
JavaScript. Browsers do not expose selected local paths.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::on_find_result:
Inject find-result forwarding and handle typed find events.

This observes app-driven browser find calls, including
[`WebViewController::find_text`] and [`WebViewController::find_text_result`]
when the bridge is injected before those commands are evaluated.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::on_form_event:
Inject browser form forwarding and handle typed form events.

Use this when native validation, progress chrome, tests, or agents need
structured form metadata and field state from hosted checkout, auth,
settings, or admin pages without bespoke page JavaScript.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::on_keyboard_event:
Inject browser keyboard/input forwarding and handle typed events.

This is the closest portable WebView island equivalent to browser-runtime stack
`before-input-event` today. It observes events after browser dispatch
starts; use native shortcut systems for commands that must cancel input
before the page sees it.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::on_lifecycle_event:
Inject lifecycle/focus forwarding and handle typed lifecycle events.

Use this when native chrome, resource throttling, tests, or agents need
to know whether hosted WebView content is focused, visible, active, or
browser-fullscreen.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::on_location_changed:
Inject location forwarding and handle typed location events.

Use this when native chrome should track hosted SPA route changes
without polling `url(...)` and `title(...)`. Pair with
[`Self::navigation_state_bridge`] for same-document Forward state.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::on_media_event:
Inject browser media event forwarding and handle typed media events.

This is the shortest path for custom native controls around
WebView-hosted `<audio>` / `<video>` content: the bridge posts browser
media events and this handler receives parsed [`WebViewMediaEvent`]
values for the requested kind.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::on_message: Register a handler for messages posted from JavaScript.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::on_navigate: Register a handler that can allow or deny navigation attempts.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::on_network_event:
Inject fetch/XHR forwarding and handle typed network events.

Use this when native diagnostics, loading UI, tests, or agents need API
request outcomes without opening browser devtools.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::on_new_window:
Register a handler for `window.open` and target-blank requests.

Without this handler, Kael preserves its compatibility default: if the
normal navigation policy allows the URL, the current WebView navigates to
it and the popup is denied. Use this hook when hosted auth, checkout, or
documentation flows need an explicit popup policy.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::on_page_load: Register a handler fired when the WebView starts or finishes loading a page.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::on_permission_request:
Inject permission preflighting and handle typed permission requests.

This is the WebView-island equivalent of an browser-runtime stack permission request
handler for browser APIs exposed inside hosted content. The embedded
browser remains the final authority for native permission prompts.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::on_pointer_event:
Inject browser pointer context forwarding and handle typed pointer events.

Use this when native status bars, hover previews, tests, or agents need
lightweight link/image/media/editable context for hovered or clicked
browser content.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::on_resource_event:
Inject resource forwarding and handle typed resource events.

Use this when native diagnostics, loading UI, tests, or agents should
observe hosted subresource activity without opening devtools.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::on_scroll_event:
Inject scroll/viewport forwarding and handle typed scroll events.

Use this when native chrome, reader progress, tests, or agents should
observe hosted document scroll state without polling JavaScript.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::on_selection_event:
Inject selection forwarding and handle typed selection events.

Use this when native edit menus, floating formatting chrome, tests, or
agents should observe hosted selection state without polling JavaScript.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::on_storage_event:
Inject Web Storage forwarding and handle typed storage events.

Use this when native account chrome, settings sync, tests, or agents
should observe hosted storage state changes without polling JavaScript.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::open_new_windows_in_c: Navigate the current WebView for `window.open` and target-blank requests.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::permission_bridge:
Inject the standard bridge plus browser permission preflighting.

The injected script wraps browser permission-bearing APIs such as
`getUserMedia`, geolocation, and notifications. A denied Kael response
blocks the page API call before it reaches the embedded browser; allow
and default responses continue to the browser's native permission flow.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::pointer_bridge:
Inject the standard bridge plus browser pointer context forwarding.

The injected script posts [`WebViewBridgeMessage`] values with the given
kind for pointer movement and click-style events inside hosted content.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::request_headers: Add request headers for the WebView's initial URL load.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::request_headers_reque: Return request headers configured for the WebView's initial URL load.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::resource_bridge:
Inject the standard bridge plus browser resource observability.

The injected script posts [`WebViewBridgeMessage`] values with the given
kind for PerformanceResourceTiming entries and element load/error
events. This does not intercept or rewrite requests.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::scroll_bridge:
Inject the standard bridge plus browser scroll/viewport forwarding.

The injected script posts [`WebViewBridgeMessage`] values with the given
kind for hosted document scroll and viewport resize snapshots.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::selection_bridge:
Inject the standard bridge plus browser selection forwarding.

The injected script posts [`WebViewBridgeMessage`] values with the given
kind for hosted document and input selection snapshots.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::storage_bridge:
Inject the standard bridge plus Web Storage event forwarding.

The injected script posts [`WebViewBridgeMessage`] values with the given
kind when hosted content mutates `localStorage` or `sessionStorage`, and
when the browser emits cross-document `storage` events.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::storage_key: Use persistent storage under the supplied profile key.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::transparent_backgroun: Request a transparent native WebView background.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::user_agent: Override the user agent used by the platform WebView.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::web_graphics: Ephemeral preset for browser-only WebGL/WebGPU/canvas surfaces.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::zoom_hotkeys: Enable browser zoom hotkeys and gestures where the backend supports them.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::zoom_hotkeys_enabled: Enable or disable browser zoom hotkeys and gestures.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewOptions::zoom_hotkeys_requeste: Return whether browser zoom hotkeys/gestures are requested.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewPermissionRequest::from_bridge: Parse a bridge message into a typed permission request when the kind matches.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewPermissionRequest::from_payloa: Parse a bridge payload into a typed permission request.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewPointerEvent::from_bridge_mess: Parse a bridge message into a typed pointer event when the kind matches.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewPointerEvent::from_payload: Parse a bridge payload into a typed pointer event.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewResourceEvent::from_bridge_mes: Parse a bridge message into a typed resource event when the kind matches.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewResourceEvent::from_payload: Parse a bridge payload into a typed resource event.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewScrollEvent::from_bridge_messa: Parse a bridge message into a typed scroll event when the kind matches.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewScrollEvent::from_payload: Parse a bridge payload into a typed scroll event.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewSelectionEvent::from_bridge_me: Parse a bridge message into a typed selection event when the kind matches.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewSelectionEvent::from_payload: Parse a bridge payload into a typed selection event.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewStorageEvent::from_bridge_mess: Parse a bridge message into a typed storage event when the kind matches.
doc_texts.fn:WebViewStorageEvent::from_payload: Parse a bridge payload into a typed storage event.
doc_texts.fn:Window::accessibility_tree:
Return the latest accessibility tree produced for this window.

This is useful for diagnostics, automated accessibility verification,
and platform integrations that need a read-only semantic snapshot.
doc_texts.fn:Window::activate_window: Focus the current window and bring it to the foreground at the platform level.
doc_texts.fn:Window::animations_enabled:
Returns whether animations should run at full fidelity for this frame.

False when the system is in low-power mode or the user has enabled the
"reduce motion" accessibility preference.
doc_texts.fn:Window::announce_accessibility: Announce a message to assistive technology.
doc_texts.fn:Window::announce_accessibility_checke: Validate and announce a message to assistive technology.
doc_texts.fn:Window::appearance: Returns the appearance of the current window.
doc_texts.fn:Window::available_actions: Returns all available actions for the focused element.
doc_texts.fn:Window::bindings_for_action:
Returns key bindings that invoke an action on the currently focused element. Bindings are
returned in the order they were added. For display, the last binding should take precedence.
doc_texts.fn:Window::bindings_for_action_in:
Returns any bindings that would invoke an action on the given focus handle if it were
focused. Bindings are returned in the order they were added. For display, the last binding
should take precedence.
doc_texts.fn:Window::bindings_for_action_in_contex: Returns the key bindings for an action in a context.
doc_texts.fn:Window::blur: Remove focus from all elements within this context's window.
doc_texts.fn:Window::bounds: Returns the bounds of the current window in the global coordinate space, which could span across multiple displays.
doc_texts.fn:Window::capslock: The current state of the keyboard's capslock
doc_texts.fn:Window::clear_webview_browsing_data: Clear cookies, cache, local storage, and other browsing data for the WebView profile.
doc_texts.fn:Window::close_webview_devtools: Close developer tools for the WebView with the given identifier when supported.
doc_texts.fn:Window::close_window: Request that the current window close through the platform lifecycle.
doc_texts.fn:Window::compute_layout:
Compute the layout for the given id within the given available space.
This method is called for its side effect, typically by the framework prior to painting.
After calling it, you can request the bounds of the given layout node id or any descendant.

This method should only be called as part of the prepaint phase of element drawing.
doc_texts.fn:Window::content_mask: Obtain the current content mask. This method should only be called during element drawing.
doc_texts.fn:Window::content_protection: Return the current checked content-protection policy, if enabled.
doc_texts.fn:Window::current_view: Get the entity ID for the currently rendering view
doc_texts.fn:Window::default_prevented: Obtain whether default has been prevented for the event currently being dispatched.
doc_texts.fn:Window::defer:
Schedules the given function to be run at the end of the current effect cycle, allowing entities
that are currently on the stack to be returned to the app.
doc_texts.fn:Window::defer_draw:
Defers the drawing of the given element, scheduling it to be painted on top of the currently-drawn tree
at a later time. The `priority` parameter determines the drawing order relative to other deferred elements,
with higher values being drawn on top.

This method should only be called as part of the prepaint phase of element drawing.
doc_texts.fn:Window::delete_webview_cookie: Delete a cookie from the WebView with the given identifier.
doc_texts.fn:Window::disable_focus: Blur the window and don't allow anything in it to be focused again.
doc_texts.fn:Window::dispatch_action: Dispatch the given action on the currently focused element.
doc_texts.fn:Window::dispatch_event: Dispatch a mouse or keyboard event on the window.
doc_texts.fn:Window::dispatch_keystroke:
Dispatch a given keystroke as though the user had typed it.
You can create a keystroke with Keystroke::parse("").
doc_texts.fn:Window::display: Determine the display on which the window is visible.
doc_texts.fn:Window::dock_panels: Compute dock panel bounds from the given workspace for this window.
doc_texts.fn:Window::drain_accessibility_actions: Drain normalized accessibility action requests delivered since the last drain.
doc_texts.fn:Window::draw:
Produces a new frame and assigns it to `rendered_frame`. To actually show
the contents of the new `Scene`, use `present`.
doc_texts.fn:Window::drop_image: Removes an image from the sprite atlas.
doc_texts.fn:Window::element_offset:
Obtain the current element offset. This method should only be called during the
prepaint phase of element drawing.
doc_texts.fn:Window::element_transform:
Obtain the current composed element transform in scaled (device) pixels.

This method should only be called during the paint phase of element drawing.
doc_texts.fn:Window::evaluate_webview_javascript: Evaluate JavaScript in the WebView with the given identifier.
doc_texts.fn:Window::evaluate_webview_javascript_w: Evaluate JavaScript in the WebView with the given identifier and receive its serialized result.
doc_texts.fn:Window::exit_pointer_lock: Release pointer lock owned by this window.
doc_texts.fn:Window::export_frame_png:
Export the current Kael-rendered window scene as a PNG image.

This captures the GPU scene at device-pixel resolution. It deliberately
returns a typed error when content protection is active, or when WebView
overlays/live external surfaces would otherwise be silently omitted.
Platform-owned chrome and the system cursor are not part of the image.
doc_texts.fn:Window::focus: Move focus to the element associated with the given [`FocusHandle`].
doc_texts.fn:Window::focus_accessibility_node: Focus the given accessibility node in the tree.
doc_texts.fn:Window::focus_accessibility_node_chec: Validate and focus an accessibility node in the current tree.
doc_texts.fn:Window::focus_next: Move focus to next tab stop.
doc_texts.fn:Window::focus_next_in_group: Move focus to the next tab stop within the currently focused tab group.
doc_texts.fn:Window::focus_prev: Move focus to previous tab stop.
doc_texts.fn:Window::focus_prev_in_group: Move focus to the previous tab stop within the currently focused tab group.
doc_texts.fn:Window::focus_webview: Move focus into the WebView with the given identifier when supported.
doc_texts.fn:Window::focus_webview_parent: Move focus from the WebView back to the parent window when supported.
doc_texts.fn:Window::focused: Obtain the currently focused [`FocusHandle`]. If no elements are focused, returns `None`.
doc_texts.fn:Window::frame_skip_enabled: Whether whole-frame damage skipping is currently enabled.
doc_texts.fn:Window::frame_timeline:
Returns the frame timing timeline recorded for this window.

Only available with the `inspector` feature or in debug builds. The timeline
is fed automatically at the end of each [`Window::draw`].
doc_texts.fn:Window::game_input_capabilities: Report pointer-lock and controller availability for this window.
doc_texts.fn:Window::gamepads:
Sample all connected controllers at the current display-frame boundary.

The snapshot and native event drain are bounded by the `MAX_GAMEPAD_*`
constants. This method never starts a timer or a background polling loop.
doc_texts.fn:Window::get_asset:
Asynchronously load an asset, if the asset hasn't finished loading or doesn't exist this will return None.
Your view will not be re-drawn once the asset has finished loading.

Note that the multiple calls to this method will only result in one `Asset::load` call at a
time.
doc_texts.fn:Window::go_back_webview: Navigate the WebView with the given identifier backward if possible.
doc_texts.fn:Window::go_forward_webview: Navigate the WebView with the given identifier forward if possible.
doc_texts.fn:Window::gpu_specs:
Read information about the GPU backing this window.

macOS currently returns `None`; Windows, Linux, FreeBSD, and browser
backends report the adapter selected by their renderer.
doc_texts.fn:Window::handle_input:
Sets an input handler, such as [`ElementInputHandler`][element_input_handler], which interfaces with the
platform to receive textual input with proper integration with concerns such
as IME interactions. This handler will be active for the upcoming frame until the following frame is
rendered.

This method should only be called as part of the paint phase of element drawing.

[element_input_handler]: crate::ElementInputHandler
doc_texts.fn:Window::handler_for: Returns a generic handler that invokes the given handler with the view and context associated with the given view handle.
doc_texts.fn:Window::has_accessibility_action_hand: Return whether this window has a handler for one accessibility action.
doc_texts.fn:Window::has_pending_keystrokes: Determine whether a potential multi-stroke key binding is in progress on this window.
doc_texts.fn:Window::has_redo: Returns whether the currently focused element can redo its next shared-history change.
doc_texts.fn:Window::has_undo: Returns whether the currently focused element can undo its next shared-history change.
doc_texts.fn:Window::hide_window: Hide the current window at the platform level.
doc_texts.fn:Window::highest_precedence_binding_fo:
Returns the highest precedence key binding that invokes an action on the currently focused
element. This is more efficient than getting the last result of `bindings_for_action`.

Returns the highest precedence key binding that would invoke an action on the given focus
handle if it were focused. This is more efficient than getting the last result of
`bindings_for_action_in`.

Returns the highest precedence key binding for an action in a context. This is more
efficient than getting the last result of `bindings_for_action_in_context`.
doc_texts.fn:Window::inner_window_bounds: Return the `WindowBounds` excluding insets (Wayland and X11)
doc_texts.fn:Window::insert_hitbox:
This method should be called during `prepaint`. You can use
the returned [Hitbox] during `paint` or in an event handler
to determine whether the inserted hitbox was the topmost.

This method should only be called as part of the prepaint phase of element drawing.
doc_texts.fn:Window::insert_inspector_hitbox:
Registers a hitbox that can be used for inspector picking mode, allowing users to select and
inspect UI elements by clicking on them.
doc_texts.fn:Window::insert_tab_stop:
Sets the focus handle for the current element. This handle will be used to manage focus state
and keyboard event dispatch for the element.

This method should only be called as part of the prepaint phase of element drawing.
Register a focus handle as a tab stop for the current frame. Used by
custom elements that manage focus without going through a Div.
doc_texts.fn:Window::insert_window_control_hitbox:
Set a hitbox which will act as a control area of the platform window.

This method should only be called as part of the paint phase of element drawing.
doc_texts.fn:Window::invalidate_cache: Invalidates retained subtree cache state for elements whose local id matches `element_id`.
doc_texts.fn:Window::invalidate_character_coordina: Updates the IME panel position suggestions for languages like japanese, chinese.
doc_texts.fn:Window::is_action_available: Determine whether the given action is available along the dispatch path to the currently focused element.
doc_texts.fn:Window::is_fullscreen: Returns whether or not the window is currently fullscreen
doc_texts.fn:Window::is_inspector_picking: Returns true if the window is in inspector mode.
doc_texts.fn:Window::is_maximized:
Check if the platform window is maximized
On some platforms (namely Windows) this is different than the bounds being the size of the display
doc_texts.fn:Window::is_webview_devtools_open: Read whether developer tools are open for the WebView with the given identifier.
doc_texts.fn:Window::is_window_active: Returns whether this window is focused by the operating system (receiving key events).
doc_texts.fn:Window::is_window_hovered:
Returns whether this window is considered to be the window
that currently owns the mouse cursor.
On mac, this is equivalent to `is_window_active`.
doc_texts.fn:Window::is_window_visible: Returns whether the current window is visible at the platform level.
doc_texts.fn:Window::keystroke_text_for:
Return a key binding string for an action, to display in the UI. Uses the highest precedence
binding for the action (last binding added to the keymap).
doc_texts.fn:Window::layout_bounds:
Obtain the bounds computed for the given LayoutId relative to the window. This method will usually be invoked by
GPUI itself automatically in order to pass your element its `Bounds` automatically.

This method should only be called as part of element drawing.
doc_texts.fn:Window::line_height: The line height associated with the current text style.
doc_texts.fn:Window::listener_for: Returns a generic event listener that invokes the given listener with the view and context associated with the given view handle.
doc_texts.fn:Window::load_webview_html: Load an HTML string into the WebView with the given identifier.
doc_texts.fn:Window::merge_all_windows:
Merges all open windows into a single tabbed window.
This is macOS specific.
doc_texts.fn:Window::minimize_window: Minimize the current window at the platform level.
doc_texts.fn:Window::modifiers: The current state of the keyboard's modifiers
doc_texts.fn:Window::mouse_position: The position of the mouse relative to the window.
doc_texts.fn:Window::move_tab_to_new_window:
Moves the tab to a new containing window.
This is macOS specific.
doc_texts.fn:Window::navigate_webview: Navigate the WebView with the given identifier to a new URL.
doc_texts.fn:Window::navigate_webview_with_headers: Navigate the WebView with the given identifier to a new URL with additional request headers.
doc_texts.fn:Window::next_anonymous_accessibility_: Return a stable identity for an accessible element without an explicit id.
doc_texts.fn:Window::observe:
Subscribe to events emitted by a entity.
The entity to which you're subscribing must implement the [`EventEmitter`] trait.
The callback will be invoked a handle to the emitting entity, the event, and a window context for the current window.
doc_texts.fn:Window::observe_global:
Register the given handler to be invoked whenever the global of the given type
is updated.
doc_texts.fn:Window::observe_release: Register a callback to be invoked when the given `Entity` is released.
doc_texts.fn:Window::observe_window_appearance: Registers a callback to be invoked when the window appearance changes.
doc_texts.fn:Window::on_accessibility_action:
Register a handler for an assistive-technology action on one node.

Handlers run after the platform accessibility adapter reports a
normalized action request for the current tree.
doc_texts.fn:Window::on_action:
Register an action listener on the window for the next frame. The type of action
is determined by the first parameter of the given listener. When the next frame is rendered
the listener will be cleared.

This is a fairly low-level method, so prefer using action handlers on elements unless you have
a specific need to register a global listener.
doc_texts.fn:Window::on_action_when:
Register an action listener on the window for the next frame if the condition is true.
The type of action is determined by the first parameter of the given listener.
When the next frame is rendered the listener will be cleared.

This is a fairly low-level method, so prefer using action handlers on elements unless you have
a specific need to register a global listener.
doc_texts.fn:Window::on_focus_in:
Register a listener to be called when the given focus handle or one of its descendants receives focus.
This does not fire if the given focus handle - or one of its descendants - was previously focused.
Returns a subscription and persists until the subscription is dropped.
doc_texts.fn:Window::on_focus_out:
Register a listener to be called when the given focus handle or one of its descendants loses focus.
Returns a subscription and persists until the subscription is dropped.
doc_texts.fn:Window::on_gamepad_frame:
Sample controllers once per display frame until cancelled or stopped.

Keep the returned subscription alive for as long as input is wanted.
Dropping it prevents the already-coalesced next-frame callback from
polling or invoking the consumer.
doc_texts.fn:Window::on_key_event:
Register a key event listener on the window for the next frame. The type of event
is determined by the first parameter of the given listener. When the next frame is rendered
the listener will be cleared.

This is a fairly low-level method, so prefer using event handlers on elements unless you have
a specific need to register a global listener.

This method should only be called as part of the paint phase of element drawing.
doc_texts.fn:Window::on_modifiers_changed:
Register a modifiers changed event listener on the window for the next frame.

This is a fairly low-level method, so prefer using event handlers on elements unless you have
a specific need to register a global listener.

This method should only be called as part of the paint phase of element drawing.
doc_texts.fn:Window::on_mouse_event:
Register a mouse event listener on the window for the next frame. The type of event
is determined by the first parameter of the given listener. When the next frame is rendered
the listener will be cleared.

This method should only be called as part of the paint phase of element drawing.
doc_texts.fn:Window::on_next_frame: Schedule the given closure to be run directly after the current frame is rendered.
doc_texts.fn:Window::on_pointer_event:
Register a rich mouse, touch, and pen listener for the next rendered frame.

Unlike the compatibility mouse events, [`PointerInputEvent`] preserves
pointer identity, device type, pressure, tilt, twist, simultaneous button
state, and coalesced high-frequency samples. The listener participates in
the same capture and bubble phases as [`Self::on_mouse_event`].
doc_texts.fn:Window::on_window_should_close:
Register a callback that can interrupt the closing of the current window based the returned boolean.
If the callback returns false, the window won't be closed.
doc_texts.fn:Window::open_webview_devtools: Open developer tools for the WebView with the given identifier when supported.
doc_texts.fn:Window::paint_blur:
Paint a backdrop blur into the scene for the next frame at the current z-index.

This method should only be called as part of the paint phase of element drawing.
doc_texts.fn:Window::paint_emoji:
Paints an emoji glyph into the scene for the next frame at the current z-index.

The y component of the origin is the baseline of the glyph.
You should generally prefer to use the [`ShapedLine::paint`](crate::ShapedLine::paint) or
[`WrappedLine::paint`](crate::WrappedLine::paint) methods in the [`TextSystem`](crate::TextSystem).
This method is only useful if you need to paint a single emoji that has already been shaped.

This method should only be called as part of the paint phase of element drawing.
doc_texts.fn:Window::paint_glyph:
Paints a monochrome (non-emoji) glyph into the scene for the next frame at the current z-index.

The y component of the origin is the baseline of the glyph.
You should generally prefer to use the [`ShapedLine::paint`](crate::ShapedLine::paint) or
[`WrappedLine::paint`](crate::WrappedLine::paint) methods in the [`TextSystem`](crate::TextSystem).
This method is only useful if you need to paint a single glyph that has already been shaped.

This method should only be called as part of the paint phase of element drawing.
doc_texts.fn:Window::paint_image:
Paint an image into the scene for the next frame at the current z-index.
This method returns an error if the frame index is not valid.

This method should only be called as part of the paint phase of element drawing.
doc_texts.fn:Window::paint_layer:
Creates a new painting layer for the specified bounds. A "layer" is a batch
of geometry that are non-overlapping and have the same draw order. This is typically used
for performance reasons.

This method should only be called as part of the paint phase of element drawing.
doc_texts.fn:Window::paint_path:
Paint the given `Path` into the scene for the next frame at the current z-index.

This method should only be called as part of the paint phase of element drawing.
doc_texts.fn:Window::paint_quad:
Paint one or more quads into the scene for the next frame at the current stacking context.
Quads are colored rectangular regions with an optional background, border, and corner radius.
see [`fill`], [`outline`], and [`quad`] to construct this type.

This method should only be called as part of the paint phase of element drawing.

Note that the `quad.corner_radii` are allowed to exceed the bounds, creating sharp corners
where the circular arcs meet. This will not display well when combined with dashed borders.
Use `Corners::clamp_radii_for_quad_size` if the radii should fit within the bounds.
doc_texts.fn:Window::paint_shadows:

doc_texts.fn:Window::request_animation_frame:
Schedule a frame to be drawn on the next animation frame.

This is useful for elements that need to animate continuously, such as a video player or an animated GIF.
It will cause the window to redraw on the next frame, even if no other changes have occurred.

If called from within a view, it will notify that view on the next frame. Otherwise, it will refresh the entire window.
doc_texts.fn:Window::request_autoscroll:
When you call this method during [`Element::prepaint`], containing elements will attempt to
scroll to cause the specified bounds to become visible. When they decide to autoscroll, they will call
[`Element::prepaint`] again with a new set of bounds. See [`crate::List`] for an example of an element
that supports this method being called on the elements it contains. This method should only be
called during the prepaint phase of element drawing.
doc_texts.fn:Window::request_autoscroll_checked: Validate and request autoscroll for drag, selection, and editor surfaces.
doc_texts.fn:Window::request_layout:
Add a node to the layout tree for the current frame. Takes the `Style` of the element for which
layout is being requested, along with the layout ids of any children. This method is called during
calls to the [`Element::request_layout`] trait method and enables any element to participate in layout.

This method should only be called as part of the request_layout or prepaint phase of element drawing.
doc_texts.fn:Window::request_measured_layout:
Add a node to the layout tree for the current frame. Instead of taking a `Style` and children,
this variant takes a function that is invoked during layout so you can use arbitrary logic to
determine the element's size. One place this is used internally is when measuring text.

The given closure is invoked at layout time with the known dimensions and available space and
returns a `Size`.

This method should only be called as part of the request_layout or prepaint phase of element drawing.
doc_texts.fn:Window::request_pointer_lock:
Request relative pointer input for this window.

Browsers require this call to run directly inside a trusted click or key
handler. Native backends require an active window; Wayland also requires
compositor protocol support and pointer focus. While locked,
[`PointerInputEvent::movement`] contains the unbounded relative mouse
delta even though its absolute position stays constrained to the window.

doc_texts.fn:Window::restore_window_state:
Restore a previously captured window state.

This restores the fullscreen state. Window bounds are set at creation
time via `WindowOptions`/`WindowParams`, so this primarily handles
toggling fullscreen to match the saved state.

Set a soft byte budget for this window's glyph/sprite atlas. When set, the renderer
evicts least-recently-used atlas tiles down to the budget at the end of each frame,
bounding glyph-atlas growth on long-running, text-churning UIs. `None` (the default)
disables eviction. Currently honored on the Metal backend.
doc_texts.fn:Window::set_atlas_byte_budget_checked: Validate and set a soft byte budget for this window's glyph/sprite atlas.

doc_texts.fn:Window::set_frame_skip_enabled:
Enable or disable whole-frame damage skipping. When enabled, a frame whose scene
is byte-identical to the previously presented one is not re-rasterized or
re-presented — the compositor keeps the prior contents — which removes redundant
GPU work for mostly-static UIs. Off by default; frames containing live external
surfaces (e.g. video) are never skipped.
doc_texts.fn:Window::set_key_context:

of prepaints can be discarded before prepainting again. This is used to support autoscroll
where we need to prepaint children to detect the autoscroll bounds, then adjust the
element offset and prepaint again. See [`crate::List`] for an example. This method should only be
called during the prepaint phase of element drawing.

doc_texts.fn:Window::with_absolute_element_offset:

doc_texts.fn:Window::with_clip_path:
Clip primitives painted inside the closure to an arbitrary [`crate::ClipShape`]
(circle, ellipse, or convex polygon).

Circles (and equal-radius ellipses) clip exactly through the existing shader-backed
rounded-clip path. Shapes that path cannot express yet — true ellipses and convex
polygons — clip to the shape's bounding box via the content mask as a conservative
fallback until the per-shape mask sample is fused into the pipeline.

This method should only be called during the paint phase of element drawing.
doc_texts.fn:Window::with_color_filter:
Compose a color filter onto the current element color filter for the duration of
the given closure. Primitives painted inside (quads, sprites, shadows, underlines)
inherit the composed filter, so a filter on a div applies to its whole subtree.
Multiplicative factors multiply; grayscale combines so that fully gray wins.

This method should only be called during the paint phase of element drawing.
doc_texts.fn:Window::with_content_mask:
Invoke the given function with the given content mask after intersecting it
with the current mask. This method should only be called during element drawing.
doc_texts.fn:Window::with_element_namespace:
Provide elements in the called function with a new namespace in which their identifiers must be unique.
This can be used within a custom element to distinguish multiple sets of child elements.
doc_texts.fn:Window::with_element_offset:
Updates the global element offset relative to the current offset. This is used to implement
scrolling. This method should only be called during the prepaint phase of element drawing.
doc_texts.fn:Window::with_element_state:
Updates or initializes state for an element with the given id that lives across multiple
frames. If an element with this ID existed in the rendered frame, its state will be passed
to the given closure. The state returned by the closure will be stored so it can be referenced
when drawing the next frame. This method should only be called as part of element drawing.
doc_texts.fn:Window::with_element_transform:
Compose a transformation onto the current element transform for the duration of
the given closure. Primitives painted inside inherit the composed transform:
quads, paths, SVGs, and text follow it. Box shadows, backdrop blurs, underlines,
images, emoji, and video surfaces do not yet transform. The transformation is
expressed in scaled (device) pixels. Hitboxes are unaffected.

This method should only be called during the paint phase of element drawing.
doc_texts.fn:Window::with_global_id:
Acquire a globally unique identifier for the given ElementId.
Only valid for the duration of the provided closure.
doc_texts.fn:Window::with_id: Immediately push an element ID onto the stack. Useful for simplifying IDs in lists
doc_texts.fn:Window::with_image_cache: Executes the provided function with the specified image cache.
doc_texts.fn:Window::with_inspector_state: Executes the provided function with mutable access to an inspector state.
doc_texts.fn:Window::with_optional_element_state:
A variant of `with_element_state` that allows the element's id to be optional. This is a convenience
method for elements where the element id may or may not be assigned. Prefer using `with_element_state`
when the element is guaranteed to have an id.

The first option means 'no ID provided'
The second option means 'not yet initialized'
doc_texts.fn:Window::with_rem_size:

doc_texts.fn:Window::with_rounded_clip:
Clip primitives painted inside the given closure to a rounded rectangle.
Quads, sprites (text, icons, images), shadows, underlines, and backdrop
blurs honor the clip; paths and video surfaces do not yet. When rounded
clips nest, the innermost clip's corners win; rectangular clipping still
applies through the regular content mask. The clip is evaluated in screen
space and does not follow element transforms.

This method should only be called during the paint phase of element drawing.

Use [`Window::text_style`] to get the current, combined text style. This method
should only be called as part of element drawing.

doc_texts.fn:accessibility::AccessibilityTree::to_:
Build a full AccessKit [`accesskit::TreeUpdate`] from this tree.

Only nodes reachable from the root are emitted, and every parent's child
list is filtered to nodes that actually exist, so the resulting update is
always internally consistent (AccessKit panics on a malformed tree).
Hidden nodes are pruned along with their subtrees.

Build a full AccessKit update ordered safely relative to the previous tree.

AccessKit applies node records sequentially. When a retained node moves
between parents, the old parent must release it before the new parent
claims it. Otherwise the consumer can transiently orphan a newly added
node and panic while emitting platform change events. This is especially
easy to trigger when scrolling changes which semantic containers are
painted in a frame.
Content-safe tree summary for diagnostics and automation traces.

doc_texts.fn:apply_clip_mask_bgra:
Apply a coverage `mask` to a tightly-packed 8-bit BGRA (or RGBA) pixel buffer in place,
scaling each pixel's alpha by its mask value. The visual effect is a clip: content is
kept where the mask is `1.0` and cut where it is `0.0`, with anti-aliased edges in
between. `mask` is row-major with one entry per pixel; extra pixels are left untouched.

Moves the item at `from` to `to` within `items`, clamping `to` into range.

Returns whether the vector changed. Both core's delegate-based list and
higher-level data-driven lists route their reorder through this primitive so
the move semantics never drift apart.
doc_texts.fn:auto:
Returns a `Length` representing an automatic length.

The `auto` length is often used in layout calculations where the length should be determined
by the layout context itself rather than being explicitly set. This is commonly used in CSS
for properties like `width`, `height`, `margin`, `padding`, etc., where `auto` can be used
to instruct the layout engine to calculate the size based on other factors like the size of the
container or the intrinsic size of the content.

doc_texts.fn:dev_tools::dev::watch_styles:
Live-reload design tokens from a styles file without recompiling.

Watches `path` (a JSON or TOML theme file carrying any subset of the color,
typography, spacing, radius, and shadow tokens) and applies every successful
reload to the global [`crate::Theme`], so edits to spacing/color/typography
take effect in the running app on save. This is the styles slice of hot
reload — the cheapest iteration-speed win while full code hot-patch is out of
scope. The initial load is applied immediately; a parse error on a later edit
is logged and the previous styles are kept.

```no_run
# use kael::App;
# fn demo(cx: &mut App) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
kael::dev::watch_styles(cx, "theme.toml")?;
# Ok(())
# }
```

doc_texts.fn:effect_layer:
Wraps a child subtree and applies CSS-style `filter` effects to it by rendering the
subtree to an offscreen tile and compositing it with a gaussian content blur and/or a
drop shadow that follows the subtree's actual silhouette.

The effect is a soft, frosted approximation rather than an exact CSS gaussian. The
shadow's spread radius (the `spread_radius` of the [`BoxShadow`]) is ignored; only its
`offset`, `color`, and `blur_radius` are used.

Place the layer inside a parent with a stable, explicit size (or give the child one) so
its offscreen tile bounds are well defined; a zero-or-flex-derived size can yield an empty
tile. Leave room around the child for a drop shadow's offset and blur, since the shadow is
clipped to the layer's content mask.

doc_texts.fn:gpu::App::notify_memory_pressure:
Dispatch a pressure level to all subscribers, recording it as the current level.
A [`MemoryPressureLevel::Critical`] notification also evicts every registered GPU
resource down to budget before the subscribers run.
doc_texts.fn:gpu::App::notify_memory_pressure_chec: Dispatch pressure while containing and reporting owner callback panics.
doc_texts.fn:gpu::App::on_memory_pressure:
Subscribe to GPU-memory pressure transitions. The callback fires when the level
changes (via [`App::poll_memory_pressure`] or [`App::notify_memory_pressure`]),
letting the app shed its own caches. Drop the returned [`Subscription`] to
unsubscribe, or call [`Subscription::detach`] to keep it for the app's lifetime.
doc_texts.fn:gpu::App::poll_memory_pressure:
Query the device GPU-memory budget, map it to a [`MemoryPressureLevel`], and
dispatch to subscribers if the level changed since the last poll. Returns the
current level (`Normal` when no budget is available). Call once per frame or on a
timer to drive automatic cache shedding.
doc_texts.fn:gpu::App::set_atlas_byte_budget:
Set a soft glyph/sprite-atlas byte budget across all currently open windows. When
set, each window's renderer evicts least-recently-used atlas tiles down to the budget
at the end of every frame, bounding glyph-atlas memory growth on long-running,
text-churning UIs. Size it against the device with [`App::gpu_memory_budget`]; `None`
disables eviction (the default). Currently honored on the Metal backend.
doc_texts.fn:gpu::App::set_gpu_budget:
Set the soft GPU-memory budget the app's [`GpuMemoryManager`] enforces over
resources registered through [`App::with_gpu_memory_manager`]. Does not evict
on its own; eviction happens on [`App::notify_memory_pressure`]
([`MemoryPressureLevel::Critical`]) or an explicit
[`GpuMemoryManager::evict_to_budget`].
doc_texts.fn:gpu::App::with_gpu_memory_manager:
Run `f` against the app-wide [`GpuMemoryManager`] to register, touch, release,
or evict GPU resources. This is the single point subsystems and apps use to put
their evictable GPU caches under the shared budget.

derived from the read-back pixels; on a CPU-only backend the real scene
is built and batched and the checksum is derived from its structure.

only on the GPU backend.

GPU read-back as [`Self::render_frame`], but lets interaction benchmarks
mutate visible work without changing scene complexity.

resize leaves the renderer at its previous size. Off-screen targets are
created for the new viewport by the next render.

explicit WebView island.

The current native backend can open many direct file/URL/container sources
through FFmpeg, but browser-managed streaming manifests such as HLS and DASH
are better routed through WebView until native streaming backends land.

doc_texts.fn:reorder_target:
Translates a drag from a source item to an insertion slot into the final
`(from, to)` index pair, or `None` when the move is a no-op or out of range.

An insertion slot sits *between* items (`0..=len`); when the slot is past the
source the target shifts down by one to account for the source being lifted
out first. This is the canonical reorder index math shared by every sortable
list so virtualized (delegate) and data-driven lists agree on what a drop
means.

doc_texts.fn:scroll_elasticity::add_scroll_elastic:
Integrates boundary `delta` into the rubber-band `overscroll` with
progressive damping.

The further the content is already stretched, the stiffer the band becomes:
damping eases from `0.62` near the boundary down to `0.22` at the
`128px` limit, and the result is clamped to that limit. This is the canonical
stretch curve; share it so every scroll surface feels the same.
doc_texts.fn:scroll_elasticity::advance_scroll_ela:
Advances the rubber-band `overscroll` one frame toward zero.

Decay is a frame-rate-independent exponential (`rate = 12.0`): `last_advance`
tracks the previous wall-clock instant so the snap-back covers the same
distance per unit time at 60Hz, 120Hz, or any frame cadence. Returns `true`
while the band is still settling and `false` once it has snapped flush
(within `0.25px`), at which point `last_advance` is reset.
doc_texts.fn:scroll_elasticity::apply_scroll_delta:
Applies a single-axis scroll `delta` to an `offset`, routing any motion past
the bounds into rubber-band `overscroll`.

This is the full per-axis pipeline used by core scrolling: reverse deltas
first [`consume_scroll_elasticity`], the offset is clamped to
`[-max_offset, 0]`, and the portion that would exceed the boundary is fed
into [`add_scroll_elasticity`]. With `rubber_band_enabled` false (or no
scrollable range) the offset is hard-clamped and overscroll is cleared.
doc_texts.fn:scroll_elasticity::consume_scroll_ela:
Consumes scroll `delta` against an existing `overscroll` before it reaches
the content.

When the content is already stretched past a boundary, a reverse scroll
first un-stretches the rubber band rather than scrolling the content. The
returned value is the remaining delta (if any) that should be applied to the
content offset once the overscroll has been neutralized.
